The probability of stopping inside a short window is a known function of a few stop probabilities the policy emits, yet GRPO estimates it by sampling. A group of rollouts that all agree gives no gradient, even when all fail; the push on the stop threshold is strongest where the model is unsure, whichever outcome is right; and whole-rollout credit reaches decisions the reward never judges. Confining the credit to the window removes only that leakage. Window likelihood (WL) samples the words but integrates over the stop decisions, so the probability of the correct outcome is computed exactly and its logarithm maximised. On HumDial-FDBench, across four open models, WL gives the best F1 and lowers both error rates by more than their confidence intervals, without talking into silence.

papers.title: Absolutely universal projective embeddings of long-root geometries of orthogonal type
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split Chevalley group of type $B_n$ ($n \geq 3$) or $D_n$ ($n \geq 4$), let $L$ be its Lie algebra and $Γ$ its long-root geometry, namely $Γ$ is the line-grassmannian of the polar space associated to $G$. It is well known that $L$ hosts a projective embedding of $Γ$, called the adjoint embedding, which realizes $Γ$ as a projective variety in the projective geometry of the underlying vector space of $L$. It is also known that $Γ$ admits the absolutely universal projective embedding, which is such that all projective embeddings of $Γ$ can be obtained from it as projections. When the field $F$ over which $G$ is defined is finite, the universal embedding of $Γ$ is just the same as the adjoint embedding. The same is not necessarily true when $F$ is infinite. Indeed, as we shall prove in this paper, the universal projective embedding of $Γ$ lives in a direct sum $K\oplus L$ for an $F$-vector space $K$, the dual of which is isomorphic to the derivation space $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ of $F$, which in general is non-trivial. Accordingly, the adjoint embedding of $Γ$ is universal if and only if $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ is trivial, namely $F$ is either perfect of positive characteristic or algebraic over its minimum subfield.

papers.title: Zoom Where the Answer Looks: Cross-Resolution Self-Distillation for MLLMs under Visual-Token Budgets
papers.abstract: Under the small per-view visual-token budgets of efficient deployment, the fine text of documents, charts and infographics becomes illegible to multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Zooming in recovers it, but the region must be chosen before the model answers. Existing methods decode an answer or a box first, at the cost of generation, or read the attention available before answering, which localizes the evidence only in top layers whose depth varies with model size. Learned region proposers instead distill the attention of the model's answers, but on the same budgeted view. Yet this attention is precise only on a view the model can read: on Qwen3-VL-4B, a window around its peak covers 83% of the evidence on a high-resolution view but 54% on the budgeted view. Since answers and high-resolution views are available during training, we introduce LookZoom, a zooming method that trains a dedicated look token by cross-resolution self-distillation of the answer's attention: with the MLLM frozen, the token learns to attend on the budgeted view, before any answer, where the model's own correct answers attend on a high-resolution view. The region around its attention peak is the window to zoom into, and reinforcement learning then trains the MLLM to answer from both views. With 98 visual tokens per view on five text-rich benchmarks, LookZoom surpasses attention-guided zooming by 20-24 points and grounding-based zooming and learned crop routing by 12-15 points on Qwen3-VL at three scales, and it outperforms learned region proposers at every budget from 98 to 392 tokens. On Qwen3-VL, the look token alone, with the MLLM frozen, already surpasses every baseline that leaves the language model unchanged, and the recipe carries over to InternVL3.5 and Qwen2.5-VL.

papers.title: CAMGen: A Core Change-Aware Multi-View Framework for Commit Message Generation
papers.abstract: Commit messages help developers understand code changes and support software maintenance. Recent approaches use repository context to improve commit message generation (CMG) with large language models (LLMs). However, existing CMG methods provide limited support for understanding how local edits affect functionality jointly implemented by multiple code entities. This functional understanding is essential for generating commit messages that explain the main change and its impact. To address this problem, we propose CAMGen, a core change-aware multi-view commit message generation framework that incorporates functional context into generation. CAMGen identifies core entities that represent the primary change intent. It then forms candidate functional units through repository-wide semantic clustering and uses those containing the core entities to construct a Functional Semantic View. This view supplies semantic context for interpreting the affected functionality. CAMGen also uses context provided by the Structural Dependency View and the Historical Exemplar View. The context from all three views is then provided to the LLM together with the code diff to guide CMG. Experimental results across three programming languages show that CAMGen outperforms representative CMG baselines, including LLM-based approaches, on most automatic evaluation metrics. Human evaluation further shows that CAMGen generates more complete commit messages with clearer explanations of change rationale and impact. These results demonstrate the value of functional context and complementary repository information for CMG.

papers.title: IORA: Irregular Object Immobilization under Restricted Actuation
papers.abstract: Stable grasping under task-specific disturbances is important for robotic manipulation. However, most dexterous grasp synthesis methods are developed for highly actuated hands in free space, and low-DoF hands may not be able to realize the contact topologies required by these grasps. Meanwhile, support surfaces can provide useful contact forces, but are often treated only as geometric constraints. We present a support-aware grasp synthesis framework for object immobilization with low-DoF coupled hands. Given irregular object geometry, our method represents both hand and object local surface regions as graphs and searches for kinematically feasible matchings between them. We then refine the wrist pose and motor state for geometric contact feasibility and validates the refined grasps through physical rollouts. Starting from the validated grasp pose, an optional task-guided local search explores nearby grasp configurations by varying the wrist pose and motor state, and selects one according to the specified task condition. Experiments on diverse objects show that our method generates various grasp configurations that achieve high grasp success and strong disturbance resistance. Real-world experiments further demonstrate physically executable grasps which enable object immobilization in cooking scenario.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes, complex null geodesics and singularity resolution in regular AdS black holes
papers.abstract: The black hole singularity is hidden behind its horizon, and it is difficult to determine whether it is resolved by quantum gravity or stringy effects. For an AdS-Schwarzschild black hole, it is known that the two-point function of the dual conformal field theory has a singularity associated with a null geodesic that bounces off the black hole singularity. In this paper, we investigate how the resolution of the black hole singularity is encoded in the dual conformal field theory by considering regular AdS black holes as regularized geometries. Using WKB analysis, we compute the quasinormal modes of regular AdS black holes and read off the dual two-point functions from the modes. We find that the singularity corresponding to the bouncing null geodesic for singular black holes is replaced by a smooth bump associated with a complex, rather than real, null geodesic. The location of the complex geodesic singularity is supported by analyzing the structure of the operator product expansion for the two-point function. Our results provide a holographic signature of black hole singularity resolution and clarify how information about the regular interior is encoded in boundary correlation functions.

papers.title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
papers.abstract: Deep learning models have become essential tools in medical imaging, yet training them end-to-end for diverse tasks remains challenging due to limited labeled data and computational constraints. To address this, we introduce Brain2Vec, a foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans pooled from multiple studies. Brain2Vec can serve both as a weight initialization backbone for fine-tuning downstream tasks and as a standalone feature extractor. We evaluated Brain2Vec in three tasks: downstream predictive performance, convergence speed, and embedding quality. Using Brain2Vec's pretrained weights as initialization and fine-tuning on labeled data for a brain age prediction task, results demonstrate improved final accuracy and faster convergence compared to random initialization. Additionally, its frozen embeddings outperform anatomically defined volumetric features on four of five downstream classification tasks and perform competitively with a state-of-the-art foundation model pre-trained on substantially more data. On the independent BrainFMBench benchmark, Brain2Vec ranked first among six pretrained brain MRI foundation models on 9 of 15 sex, age, and BMI prediction tasks across five cohorts. Lastly, we show that Brain2Vec encodes information primarily from a spatially localized and neuroanatomically meaningful set of brain regions, and that manipulating a subset of latent features produces monotonic, region-specific effects on the reconstructed anatomy. Brain2Vec code and trained models are available as an open-source package on https://github.com/CBICA/Brain2Vec. Users can apply Brain2Vec locally by installing the package, or directly through the NiChart cloud platform https://cloud.neuroimagingchart.com, where Brain2Vec features can be derived without requiring local installation or specialized infrastructure.

papers.title: KatoANN: Enabling Near-Exact Vector Search at the Speed of Lossy Scans with CPU Matrix Engines
papers.abstract: Emerging CPU matrix engines, such as Intel AMX, enable high throughput by batching multiple queries. However, they support only low-precision formats, which can significantly degrade recall (i.e., search quality). We present KatoANN, the first approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search system that achieves both high throughput and high recall simultaneously on CPU matrix engines. Specifically, KatoANN represents each vector using a 16-bit code, splits it into high- and low-byte planes, and computes near-exact distances using 8-bit matrix multiplications that the matrix engine supports. To reduce extra multiplication overhead, it ranks all candidates by their high bytes alone and refines only a few survivors with the full distance. KatoANN also reduces memory footprint since it does not maintain a full-precision copy of the vectors. We implement a KatoANN prototype on Intel AMX. Our experimental results show that KatoANN outperforms existing partition-based systems across the high-recall range.

papers.title: Least energy solutions for a quasilinear Neumann problem
papers.abstract: We study the existence of nonconstant weak solutions and the qualitative behavior of the least energy level for a class of quasilinear elliptic problems with Neumann boundary conditions of the form \[ -\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}(a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}u) +\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_s a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}uD_{x_j}u =g(u)-λu \quad \text{in }Ω. \] Since the associated energy functional is neither of class $C^1$ nor locally Lipschitz, the classical Nehari manifold method cannot be applied directly. We therefore rely on variational techniques combined with nonsmooth critical point theory. For $λ>0$, we prove the existence of least energy solutions and show that, under suitable assumptions, they are nonconstant for large $λ$ and constant for sufficiently small $λ$. Moreover, the least energy level tends to $+\infty$ as $λ\to+\infty$. In the indefinite regime, a key ingredient is a spectral decomposition of $H^1(Ω)$ associated with the linear operator \[ \mathcal L_0u :=-\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}\bigl(a_{ij}(x,0)D_{x_i}u\bigr). \]

papers.title: Pluralistic Alignment in Large Language Models: Objectives, Human References, and Preference Representations
papers.abstract: Pluralistic alignment aims to represent meaningful variation in human preferences rather than collapse heterogeneous judgments into a single target. Yet existing work often mixes three distinct questions: what pluralistic behavior a model should exhibit, whose preferences define the reference, and what evidence is sufficient to demonstrate success. We organize the literature around a two-layer taxonomy. Layer 1 distinguishes representing a range of human-supported viewpoints (Overton Pluralism), adapting faithfully to a specified perspective or preference condition (Steerable Pluralism), and matching the response distribution observed in a target population (Distributional Pluralism). Layer 2 distinguishes aggregate populations, countries and regions, and subgroups as human references. Preference representation, implementation mechanism, modality, and evidence quality are treated as cross-cutting design choices rather than additional forms of pluralism. We synthesize a protocol-bounded corpus of 70 works on pluralistic alignment and neighboring areas, using the objective-by-human-reference matrix to map existing approaches and identify underexplored combinations. The coded literature concentrates on Steerable Pluralism and Distributional Pluralism, while eligible Overton Pluralism work appears only at the aggregate-population level under our stated protocol. We then connect each objective to the evidence needed to support it, including perspective validity, conditional fidelity, distributional fidelity, support preservation, and uncertainty in subgroup estimates. Together, the taxonomy and evaluation framework clarify what current methods establish, where their claims exceed their evidence, and how future systems can represent disagreement without mistaking variation for faithful representation.

papers.title: Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra
papers.abstract: Recent advances in general-purpose AI models and agentic systems have enabled them to perform some CAD tasks. A systematic assessment is now needed to establish what these systems can accomplish and how well their outputs meet engineering requirements. This paper presents an empirical study of GPT-6 Astra, a SOTA general-purpose AI model, across four basic CAD tasks: model understanding, generation, editing, and evaluation. We design test cases spanning different levels of complexity and engineering requirements. The results show that GPT-6 Astra can support multiple stages of CAD workflows, with successful outcomes in cases involving nontrivial geometric complexity. This suggests that general-purpose AI is beginning to offer practical value in almost all steps in CAD workflow. However, gaps remain between generating visually plausible geometry and producing valid, functional, and editable CAD models. Recurring errors in freeform geometry, parameter dependencies, and mating relationships between parts limit engineering usefulness. Agentic iterative refinement can improve results but does not consistently resolve critical errors; long completion times further constrain practical use.

papers.title: Synthetic Image Oversampling for Rare-Class Representation Learning in Deep Facial Phenotyping
papers.abstract: Recent deep facial phenotyping methods can support the recognition of genetic syndromes, but patient images are often scarce and unevenly distributed across disorders. Synthetic facial images offer a way to supplement the training data without collecting additional patient photographs. Their usefulness, however, depends on whether they improve recognition of real patients: generated images may introduce artifacts or repeat features already represented in the training set. It is therefore necessary to examine both how much synthetic augmentation to use and which disorders benefit. We investigate disease-specific synthetic oversampling using images from the Phenotypic Disease Image Database to augment a subset of the GestaltMatcher Database. We compare increasing augmentation levels in an image-based model, GestaltMatcher-Arc, and a multimodal model, GestaltMML, while keeping the real training and patient-disjoint evaluation partitions fixed. Repeated training runs assess overall and disease-specific accuracy, and an exploratory embedding analysis examines changes in class compactness and separation. Augmentation improves mean recognition accuracy in both training setups, although gains remain modest in GestaltMatcher-Arc and continue across the tested levels in GestaltMML. These aggregate improvements are accompanied by uneven disease-level responses, including reduced accuracy for some disorders. In the embedding analysis, disorders with fewer real training images tend to gain more class separation, but geometric changes do not consistently track classification performance. Together, the findings support synthetic oversampling for limited-data facial phenotyping and emphasize the need to assess its amount and benefit for individual disorders within each training setup.

papers.title: Chinese Decision: A Family of Language Models for Single-Pass Probabilistic Decision-Making
papers.abstract: Many applications need either a probability distribution over a few decisions or a set of typed spans from a text, and both are usually obtained by generating text. We present Chinese Decision, a family of Chinese models that answers both with a single forward pass and no generated token: candidate-letter logits give probabilities for Boolean, categorical, and ordinal decisions, and a small span head reading an echoed copy of the input gives typed character spans. Both readouts share one backbone and one merged LoRA, so a unified model is one weight file. We release decision-only and unified models at 0.8B, 2B, and 4B (Qwen3.5), trained for one epoch on 13.05 million decisions and, for the unified models, on CJ-IE, a 1.2-million-row Chinese extraction mixture. On the full 307,900-decision CJ-Bench, the unified 4B model reaches 86.86% accuracy, above every reported baseline and the decision-only 4B model (85.97%), and extracts spans on CJ-IE with micro F1 of 68.9. Retention has a price: against a 0.8B model continued on CJ-IE alone, which reaches 73.9 F1 but forgets CJ-Bench (71.02%), keeping decision ability costs 5.0 to 10.7 F1 points, shrinking with size. Gains of the unified models over decision-only ones are small, and all comparisons rest on single training runs with paired clustered bootstrap intervals.

papers.title: Fixed-Point Abundances and the Onset of Extinctions in Multispecies Lotka-Volterra Ecosystems
papers.abstract: I investigate the average and variance of species abundance distributions for fixed-point solutions to generalized Lotka-Volterra ecosystems. Two different analytical methods are constructed. First, I build up on the perturbative Random Matrix Theory approach developed in my earlier work [Phys. Rev. E. 113, L062202 (2026)], and formalize this method diagrammatically. The abundance average is given by a sum of planar diagrams with non-crossing vertex pairings which can be encoded as Dyck paths. This allows me to express the combinatorial factor multiplying perturbative terms at each order as Catalan and Narayana numbers, following which the abundance average is given by the latter's generating functions. In this way, the infinite perturbation expansion is exactly resummed in a closed-form formula. I have not been able to find a similar resummation for the abundance variance, however diagrammatic Feynman rules are expressed, following which the perturbative series can be calculated to any desirable order. Second, I do the same calculations using the cavity method, which gives closed-form formulas for both the abundance average and variance. For the average, the cavity formula gives the exact same result as the perturbative approach when the average interspecies interaction vanishes. When this is not the case, the two results are functionally different, however they are hardly distinguishable in their parametric range of validity. Comparison with numerical data indicate that the cavity result is more accurate over a larger parameter range.

papers.title: PingpongDuo: Agile Humanoid Table Tennis Doubles with Safe Team Coordination
papers.abstract: Unlike singles, humanoid table tennis doubles requires teammates to strike in strict alternation while sharing a confined workspace. Rapid repositioning can compromise striking accuracy, while uncoordinated teammate movements introduce collision risks. We present PingpongDuo, a hierarchical framework for agile humanoid doubles with safe team coordination. At the team level, a planner jointly selects positioning targets and uses learned risk estimates to filter risky proposals, preferentially preserving the current striker's target. At the individual level, separate footwork and striking skills combine agile movement with precise racket control. The skills are guided by human motion references, including footwork collected from human doubles play, and trained from states produced by one another to support rapid transitions. A racket-arm residual further refines strikes after movement using return feedback from a simulator calibrated with real ball-flight and contact measurements. In simulation, PingpongDuo improves the ball-return success rate by 13.2% over the state-of-the-art baseline, while achieving approximately 2 cm positioning error during clearance. In real-world experiments, a robot completes a 2.15 m clearance-and-recovery cycle in 2.4 s with a peak speed of 2.23 m/s, while two robots sustain more than 10 consecutive strikes in strict alternation.

papers.title: Similar Models, Broken Odds: Where Luce's Axiom Fails in Chatbot Arena
papers.abstract: Chatbot Arena gives each language model one Bradley-Terry score, which fixes how often any model should beat any other. Choice theory predicts where this fails: near-copies are compared on the few details in which they differ, so votes between them are more decisive than their scores imply, exactly for the comparison a lab cares about, a new version against the old one. On 1.8 million Arena votes, votes between versions of one model are 1.37 times as decisive as Bradley-Terry predicts, between sizes of one generation 1.26 times and between models of one lab 1.12 times; a release a year later points the same way, and the effect survives tie, prompt, topic and timing checks. How alike two models' answers are worded and formatted tracks the effect. Plain scores leave the odds between relatives about 9% too close to even on held-out votes; a correction with four to six parameters roughly halves this and predicts held-out votes better, mostly by modeling ties, while the leaderboard order barely moves; frozen and carried to new releases, its gains in head-to-head odds are too small for our test to establish. With language-model judges and three-answer menus, a near-copy takes votes mostly from its twin when choices are pooled over prompts (log-odds shift +0.10, 95% interval 0.05 to 0.16), less so within a prompt.

papers.title: A converse to Littlewood-type theorem for random Dirichlet series
papers.abstract: This article investigates random Dirichlet series within the framework of Hardy and mixed norm spaces of Dirichlet series. For randomization methods by sequences of non-constant independent and identically distributed random variables, we completely characterize when the random symbol space of the Hardy space $\mathscr{H}^p$ (respectively, the mixed norm space $\mathscr{H}^{p,q}_α$) coincides with $\mathscr{H}^2$ (respectively, $\mathscr{H}^{2,q}_α$). We also obtain some integrability results when Dirichlet series belong to the corresponding random symbol spaces. The same methods also yield a complete characterization for mixed norm spaces on the unit disk in the range $0<q<4$, closing the gap between previously known necessary and sufficient conditions.

papers.title: Surface-to-Volume Homogenization of NonLinear Steklov Eigencouples with NonHomogeneous Orlicz Growth in Perforated Domains
papers.abstract: We study normalized principal Steklov eigencouples on periodically perforated domains when both the bulk energy and the boundary normalization have general, possibly nonhomogeneous, Orlicz growth. The surface term on the hole boundaries carries the critical surface-to-volume scaling. For each fixed mass level, the constrained minima converge along the whole family, while selected minimizers, fluxes and Lagrange multipliers converge along subsequences to the corresponding objects of a homogenized problem. In the limit, the bulk operator is given by a convex cell problem, and the boundary term becomes a volume term weighted by the total surface density of the reference hole. The key tool is a strong approximation of the microscopic traces by cell averages, measured in the scaled surface modular.

papers.title: PATTERN Can Be Solved from Memory: Testing Graph Neural Networks on Unseen Patterns
papers.abstract: PATTERN asks graph neural networks to find a planted subgraph in a new host graph. The hosts change, but the benchmark draws just 100 patterns and reuses them across training and test splits. A lookup that extracts these patterns from the training labels achieves 96.6% class-weighted accuracy on the official test split, above every published result, without fitting a model or consulting the generator. On unseen patterns, the same lookup scores 50.6%. A matcher that also uses the generator reaches 99.2% on the official split. Among five graph networks we retrained, GRASS and PPGT go from the top two on the official split to the bottom two on unseen patterns. Each loses 8.1 percentage points even when familiar and unseen patterns are matched in size. Logistic regression on two-hop node statistics scores above every run of the five networks on unseen patterns. For CKGConv, the advantage follows the training patterns: it reappears with each of three independently drawn pattern libraries and disappears when every training and validation graph gets a new pattern. Generator-based inference also scores 82.3% on CLUSTER, compared with a published best of 81.6%. On Minesweeper's released board, four of eight planned chains produced samples within the time budget; none converged, but their pooled predictions reached 99.86% ROC AUC, above the published best of 99.55%. PATTERN's official split tests its intended task of finding familiar patterns in new graphs. We recommend reporting the same checkpoint's score on unseen patterns alongside it.

papers.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
papers.abstract: Large language models struggle to reliably identify and correct errors in their own reasoning. Unlike prior training-based approaches that fine-tune an LLM to generate revisions or feedback, we learn where to intervene in failed rollouts and determine how to redirect them. To choose where to intervene, we train a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder using only final-answer correctness. For redirection, we find that under a fixed generation budget, the tested inline injections fail to reliably redirect reasoning, whereas presenting the same instruction in a new user turn changes the model's course. The resulting correction framework, UPTURN (User-Prompt TURN injection at a learned position), requires no LLM fine-tuning: it retains a selected prefix, injects an instruction as a new user turn, and regenerates the suffix. Across four reasoners and six math benchmarks, UPTURN improves average accuracy in every setting over a 32-rollout baseline. It outperforms self-correction and reflection-token injection baselines under matched correction budgets, transfers across reasoners and to GPQA-Diamond without retraining, and complements GRPO and self-correction methods.

papers.title: ECGGuard: Deep Watermarking of Electrocardiogram Signals With Error-Correcting
papers.abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings pass through multiple networks and systems before automated interpretation, leaving patient metadata vulnerable to loss. Digital watermarking can embed this metadata in the signal, but conventional methods fail under time shifts, and high waveform similarity does not guarantee the same downstream diagnosis. We present \rev{ECGGuard}, a deep watermarking framework for single-lead ECG. A fully convolutional generator embeds the payload without signal quantization, a detector decodes the message frame by frame and checks for watermark presence, and during training a frozen arrhythmia classifier penalizes changes that would alter its predictions. Because high bit accuracy does not ensure whole-message recovery, the payload is protected by extended Hamming codes, \rev{a validation-selected channel ordering}, and soft-decision decoding. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, \rev{averaged over three training runs, ECGGuard} keeps bit accuracy above \rev{98\%} under time shifts of 10 to 50 samples, where transform-domain baselines drop to chance. The coded 16-bit payload is recovered exactly in \rev{99.95\%} of clean segments\rev{, in over 96\%} under time shifts, 10\% sample deletion, or 10\% packet loss\rev{, and in 99.1\% for unseen subjects}. \rev{For the guiding classifier, the diagnostic loss limits the drop in ventricular-beat sensitivity to 1.6 percentage points on the test records (35.0 without it) and to 12.2 points for unseen subjects (67.0 without it); the drop grows to 10.3 points for independently trained classifiers, and the protection does not transfer to an external database.} \rev{ECGGuard} has 0.56 million parameters and needs about \rev{19}~ms per segment on a desktop CPU.

papers.title: Intentionally Overidentifying Local Projections
papers.abstract: Local projections (LPs) have become a standard tool for estimating dynamic effects in macroeconomics and are typically implemented using ordinary least squares (OLS) for a given lag order. We propose an alternative approach that exploits additional lags as excluded instrumental variables (IVs). Under a finite-order model with martingale-difference shocks, the resulting (optimally weighted) IV estimator is never asymptotically less efficient than OLS and, as we show, can deliver substantial efficiency gains when data are persistent. For the unit-root AR(1) data with i.i.d. errors, our baseline IV estimator (with one overidentifying restriction) has asymptotic variance $2-h^{-1}$, compared with $h$, the asymptotic variance of the OLS lag-augmented estimator in Montiel Olea and Plagborg-Møller (2021), for an integer propagation horizon $h$. We then develop IV-based LP inference that is robust to unknown persistence and moderate local model misspecification. We also characterize the trade-off between the degree of misspecification and the number of additional lag controls. Through simulations and an empirical application, we demonstrate that the proposed method can yield meaningfully shorter confidence intervals for impulse responses than OLS in finite samples.

papers.title: Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis
papers.abstract: The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic operator equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper formalizes the reduction process and proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a fast one-time symbolic phase via its sparse prefix-sum property, the runtime bus-type projection overhead and indirect mapping caches are entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The proposed algorithm is implemented in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 28.1-37.9 times faster than the MATPOWER-style baseline and 8.9-9.7 times faster than the in-house Schäfer-Braun-inspired assembly (V1); on PEGASE 9241, it outperforms optimized traditional C++ assembly routines by 3.72 times in cold construction and 2.59 times across iterations. End-to-end, the iteration-loop solve time with KLU is 1.16-1.97 times faster than the native C++ LightSim2Grid and up to 95.5 times faster than pandapower, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.

papers.title: Photon evolution through light-particle conversion in stochastic magnetic fields: Kramers--Kronig relations and universality
papers.abstract: We study photon conversion into light particles, such as dilatons, axions, and gravitons, induced by background magnetic fields, and formulate the resulting evolution in terms of the Stokes parameters. We show that photon conversion reduces to an effective non-unitary evolution of the photon sector. In the perturbative regime, the Hermitian and anti-Hermitian parts of the effective photon Hamiltonian are related through Kramers--Kronig relations, revealing that the changes in the Stokes parameters are not independent. We apply this general framework to photon evolution in Gaussian stochastic magnetic fields with possible helicity, and derive the ensemble-averaged evolution of the Stokes parameters. We find that two nonzero contributions arise even in the absence of magnetic helicity, which respectively correspond to the overall attenuation of all the Stokes parameters and to an irrelevant overall phase. We also find that magnetic helicity gives rise to two additional contributions, one of which changes the circular polarization while the other induces a rotation of linear polarization. These contributions form two Kramers--Kronig pairs. In particular, photon conversion induced by magnetic helicity is accompanied by both circular-polarization and birefringent responses. The same structure appears in dilaton-photon, axion-photon, and graviton-photon systems, revealing universality of photon conversion in magnetic fields.

papers.title: Synchronization Reveals Market Structure That Classical Randomness Tests Cannot Detect
papers.abstract: Whether asset prices contain structure beyond a random walk is classically assessed with variance-ratio tests of the random-walk hypothesis. Synchronization measures from physics, notably the Kuramoto order parameter applied across trading timescales, have been proposed as an alternative diagnostic of market state, but they have been validated on single asset classes and never compared with the variance-ratio test on the same data. We compute a cross-timeframe Kuramoto coherence measure and a heteroskedasticity-robust Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio on identical windows for 61 instruments spanning cryptocurrencies, foreign exchange, metals, equity indices and single-name equities. The two diagnostics are statistically independent. We explain this analytically: coherence decomposes exactly into a direction-agreement channel and a volatility-agreement channel, and under sign-symmetric returns the direction channel is independent of the variance ratio and of every other statistic built from squared returns; simulations confirm the prediction. Coherence tracks the directional cleanliness of recent price moves in all five asset classes, whereas the variance-ratio test cannot reject the random walk for most of the panel. Held to finance benchmarks with strict information timing, however, coherence adds almost nothing to heterogeneous autoregressive volatility forecasts out of sample, and trading rules built on it earn no gross return outside cryptocurrency, where trading the coherence direction at high coherence breaks even at about five basis points per round trip. Failing to reject weak-form efficiency therefore does not rule out directional structure, but the structure that synchronization reveals is mostly descriptive and economically thin.

papers.title: Personalized Federated Vector Autoregression with Personalization Diversity
papers.abstract: Personalized federated estimation of high-dimensional time series faces two challenges: identifying shared dynamics and retaining the statistical gains from pooling. We address these challenges through personalization diversity in a vector autoregressive model with shared low-rank dynamics, shared sparse links, and personalized sparse departures. A cross-client support-frequency cap yields a sharp majority threshold for shared-personalized identification, while an additional cross-client $\ell_q$ condition captures approximate diversity and controls approximation under a smaller working personalization frequency cap. We develop PerFeCT-VAR, Personalized Federated Vector Autoregression via Frequency-Capped Thresholding, which jointly enforces clientwise sparsity and cross-client frequency constraints. Under suitable sampling and cross-component compatibility conditions, we establish initialization guarantees and joint local linear convergence for heterogeneous stationary client distributions. Our componentwise error bounds show that diversity attenuates both estimation and approximation errors transmitted from personalized to shared components, and quantify the tradeoff induced by the working cap. These bounds identify regimes in which the shared components attain pooled accuracy despite non-vanishing personalized effects, while personalized estimation achieves local-sample accuracy on average. Simulations and an application to multistore retail revenue data illustrate the estimation, forecasting, and interpretive benefits of the proposed framework.

papers.title: SyclKittens: A Tile Programming Model for Programmers and Coding Agents on Intel GPUs
papers.abstract: New AI accelerators arrive before the kernels that make them fast, because peak kernel performance requires architecture-specific expertise in operand pipelines and data-movement techniques. Coding agents can now write, compile, and tune kernels on their own, so they could greatly accelerate kernel development and optimization. What agents produce depends on the interfaces they are given. These interfaces may expose a machine's raw capabilities or encode the known-good methods for exploiting its hardware features efficiently. We test the performance impact of these two interfaces on Intel GPUs through controlled experiments with five coding models on three kernels. With raw SYCL and execution feedback, Opus 4.8, the strongest of the three models tested with Claude Code, writes a single-GPU GEMM kernel reaching only 57.5% of Intel's tuned oneDNN library. We present SyclKittens, a hardware-aware tile programming model for Intel GPUs that encodes these known-good methods, so its operations place operands in matrix-engine layouts, prefetch through the L1 cache, and communicate over the fabric that links GPU stacks into a node. With SyclKittens under the same agent, task, and feedback budget, the agent reaches 82.1%, showing that encoded methods turn hardware capabilities into performance. Workload-specific policies stay programmable, and engineers and agents jointly refine these schedules in SyclKittens to build a kernel suite that reaches approximately 96% of oneDNN in geometric mean across GEMM shapes. The suite runs Llama-3.1-8B inference 1.59 times faster than torch.compile on one GPU and up to 2.91 times faster than a matched multi-GPU decode path on Intel's oneCCL. SyclKittens is open source and available at https://github.com/intel/SyclKittens.

papers.title: From TS-SUF-2 to TS-SUF-4: Practical Security Enhancements for FROST2 Threshold Signatures
papers.abstract: Threshold signature schemes play a vital role in securing digital assets within blockchain and distributed systems. FROST2 stands out as a practical threshold Schnorr signature scheme, noted for its efficiency and compatibility with standard verification processes. However, under the one-more discrete logarithm assumption, with static corruption and centralized key generation settings, FROST2 has been shown by Bellare et al. (in CRYPTO 2022) to achieve only TS-SUF-2 security, which is a consequence of its vulnerability to TS-UF-3 attacks. In this paper, we address this security limitation by presenting an enhanced variant of FROST2, namely, FROST2+ which achieves the TS-SUF-4 security level under the same computational assumptions as the original FROST2. FROST2+ strengthens FROST2 by integrating additional pre-processing token verifications that help mitigate TS-UF-3 and TS-UF-4 vulnerabilities while maintaining practical efficiency. We show that FROST2+ can achieve TS-SUF-4 security not only under the same conditions as the original FROST2 analysis, but also when initialized with a distributed key generation protocol such as PedPoP. Our benchmark using ZCash's FROST library shows that the performance of FROST2+ is comparable to FROST2 and about 64-79% faster than FROST when precomputation is enabled.

papers.title: Nearly Optimal Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with 1-Bit Feedback
papers.abstract: We study fixed-confidence best-arm identification under strict 1-bit feedback constraints. At each round, the learner selects an arm and a query set, and receives only a single bit indicating whether the sampled reward belongs to that set. We consider a distribution-free finite-variance setting with arm-wise localization, where direct empirical mean estimation is no longer available and clipping becomes unavoidable. We first formulate a time-uniform 1-bit mean-estimation primitive based on randomized threshold queries and a clipped tail-integral identity. We then embed this primitive into candidate-challenger best-arm identification algorithms. A fixed-clipping algorithm gives a simple anytime $(ε,δ)$-PAC guarantee, while a phased adaptive-clipping algorithm matches the clipping level to the current resolution and yields a gap-adaptive sample complexity. We also prove a $K$-arm worst-case information-theoretic lower bound showing that the logarithmic penalty caused by finite-variance 1-bit feedback is intrinsic. This bound matches the leading dependence of the phased algorithm up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: An abstract averaging method for quasilinear equations
papers.abstract: We develop an abstract averaging method for equations $Mx=\varepsilon N(x,\varepsilon)$ in Banach spaces. The method applies when the equation can be separated into an averaged compatibility condition and a nonlinear complementary problem, and it allows the principal operator $M$ to be genuinely nonlinear. We prove that every nondegenerate zero of the corresponding averaged equation generates, for all sufficiently small nonzero values of $\varepsilon$, a nearby solution. Under a suitable small Lipschitz condition this solution is locally unique, while in the differentiable case it belongs to a unique local $C^1$ branch. The framework contains the abstract linear Fredholm averaging theory as a special case, but also covers quasilinear problems for which the principal operator has no invertible linearization at the reference state. We also determine the leading asymptotic profile of the solutions. Applications are given to a vector $p$-Laplacian Duffing system and to a nonsmooth problem in a Hilbert space.

papers.title: Cross-Benchmark Transfer from RL on Agentic Coding Tasks
papers.abstract: Coding agents often fail in the last mile: they build most of a feature but drop a requirement, test only the cases their implementation already handles, break behavior that was supposed to stay intact, or validate against an unchecked assumption. We ask whether reinforcement learning (RL) on expert-built agentic coding tasks closes this gap, and whether what the agent learns transfers beyond the training distribution. We post-train Kimi K2.7 Code, a 1T-parameter (32B active) open-weight mixture-of-experts model, with RL alone on 1,700 tasks: 1,000 repository tasks graded by hidden fail-to-pass tests and by pass-to-pass tests of existing behavior, and 700 terminal tasks graded by expert-written hidden verifiers. The reward is the fraction of target checks passed and drops to zero if any pass-to-pass test fails. One epoch of GSPO on a rank-32 LoRA adapter improves pass@1 on each of the six external benchmarks we evaluated, across three agent harnesses: SWE-Bench Pro (60.1 to 64.8), DeepSWE (31.0 to 43.4), Terminal-Bench 2.1 (67.4 to 82.0), Terminal-Bench 3 (1.4 to 12.1), Terminal-Bench 4 (0.0 to 7.6), and SWE-Marathon (5.0 to 25.0). Pooled over the five independent task sets (Terminal-Bench 4 revises Terminal-Bench 3), the improvement is significant (p < 0.001), and it remains significant on the three sets released after the training data was collected (p = 0.004); the model also improves under both harnesses never used in training. Median trajectories on DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench 3 are 24-35% shorter in agent steps. The base model's failed DeepSWE runs are mostly near-misses, and on the tasks the trained model newly solves, paired trajectories show it avoiding each of the four failure modes above.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Conversational Home Energy Management Systems
papers.abstract: The growing complexity in home energy management (HEM) demands advanced systems that guide occupants toward informed energy decisions reflecting their background, preferences, and context. Large language model (LLM)-integrated HEM systems (HEMS) have demonstrated promise, but previous studies relied on single-turn or single-task evaluations with response accuracy as the primary metric. Whether such systems deliver effective interactions across the extended multi-turn dialogues typical of real-world use remains an open question. This study introduces a comprehensive evaluation framework of LLM-integrated HEMS derived from the Goal-Question-Metric methodology, organized across five categories: task performance, factual accuracy, interaction quality, control capability, and system efficiency. A total of 23 metrics across multi-turn conversations are proposed and an LLM-as-judge pipeline is employed to enable scalable automated scoring. Its reliability is validated against three trained human coders: after iterative rubric calibration, twelve of the fifteen LLM-scored metrics reached strong agreement (ICC >= 0.73), three of them perfect, while the remaining three exhibited near-zero variance in human scores and are instead reported via mean absolute error (0.04-0.28). To demonstrate the framework's effectiveness, 970 dialogues -- 16 scenarios and five personas -- were generated and evaluated across four conversational HEMS configurations spanning a sophistication gradient, from a vanilla LLM with raw energy data to a multi-agent HEMS. The framework distinguished the four configurations across multiple evaluation dimensions, revealing their respective strengths and weaknesses. This study contributes to conversational HEMS by providing a reproducible, multi-dimensional evaluation methodology that comprehensively assesses sustained, context-aware system performance.

papers.title: MeanFlowAdvantage: Stable Reward Fine-Tuning for Few-Step Average-Velocity Generators
papers.abstract: MeanFlow enables efficient few-step generation by predicting interval-average velocities, but this representation creates a mismatch for reward fine-tuning: existing advantage-based objectives are typically defined on instantaneous velocities or equivalent $x_0$-space predictions, whereas inference directly uses the learned average-velocity map. We introduce MeanFlowAdvantage, a signed advantage-weighted least-squares objective for average-velocity generators. Our key construction uses a shared, detached MeanFlow derivative correction to express the reward objective in prediction space while making rollout and reference regularization exact penalties on the average-velocity network deployed at inference. The resulting formulation preserves MeanFlow's native few-step sampler and provides a direct mechanism for transferring reward improvements to the deployed flow map. On SD3.5-Medium, MeanFlowAdvantage improves all eight reported metrics over the matched four-step MeanFlowNFT baseline and, with only four NFEs, matches or exceeds the 40-step DiffusionNFT baseline on six of eight metrics. The same objective also transfers to DNA promoter design, where it supports both teacher-free on-policy RL for a generator defined on a manifold and teacher-guided reward-graded distillation, with the latter yielding the lowest one-step Sei profile MSE among the compared configurations.

papers.title: Approximate majorization and high-order capacity of quantum depolarizing channels
papers.abstract: A central challenge in quantum information theory is to determine whether entanglement provides an advantage for information processing when coherent operations across multiple channel uses are allowed. For depolarizing channels, King's proof of the additivity of the minimum output entropy rules out such an advantage for classical communication at leading asymptotic order, while leaving open the possibility of an advantage for higher orders. In this work, we conjecture a majorization relation for the outputs of depolarizing channels and prove an approximate version of this conjecture. Our proof combines an exact ordering of shifted log-determinants with an anti-concentration bound for the spectrum of the product-state output, refining King's analysis based on Schatten norms. An additional logarithmic second-moment estimate controls arbitrary channel outputs. As a direct application, we obtain a tight third-order expansion for the classical capacity of quantum depolarizing channels. Consequently, entangled codewords and collective decoding can improve the logarithm of the message size over the product-coding strategy by at most $O(1)$ bits, sharpening our understanding of the role of entanglement in the finite-blocklength regime.

papers.title: Mind the RefGAP: Correcting Reference Attention in Diffusion-Based Visual Editing
papers.abstract: Reference-guided diffusion editors struggle to faithfully reproduce user-provided references. We observe that many diffusion editors allocate limited attention to the reference. For example, in LoomVideo, edit-region queries assign less than 1% of their attention mass to the reference. We introduce RefGAP, a training-free correction that determines logit-offset magnitudes online at each layer from the reference-attention mass measured during the forward pass. Positive offsets to reference logits strengthen reference usage by edit-region queries, while negative offsets for keep-region queries limit reference-induced changes outside the edit. Two global coefficients control the correction; they are selected once on validation data from four development diffusion editors and held fixed. Across seven diffusion-based image/video editors, RefGAP improves identity fidelity in head swapping and face swapping, where identity takes priority; on some editors this raises pose error, which delaying the correction reduces. RefGAP achieves a fidelity-preservation trade-off comparable to separately tuned constant edit-side biases, without per-approach strength sweeps. Additional experiments on virtual try-on and background replacement evaluate transfer beyond identity editing.

papers.title: VC-dimension of distance graphs in finite field geometries
papers.abstract: We study the VC-dimension of distance graphs of large subsets of vector spaces over finite fields. For $3\leq k\leq d$, we prove the distance graph of $E\subset \F_q^d$ has VC-dimension at least $k$ provided that $|E|>Cq^{\min(d-1,\frac{d+k-1}{2})}$. We also show that this exponent is sharp in the $k=d$ case.

papers.title: The Alignment Illusion in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Layer-wise visual-text similarity in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) is widely interpreted as evidence that the language model progressively integrates visual content into a shared representation space. This reading rests on the assumption that scalar alignment scores reflect content-level cross-modal interaction. To test this assumption, we apply controlled interventions to the visual stream. Across 13 MLLMs from five families spanning 0.5B to 72B parameters, replacing projector-output visual tokens with Gaussian noise sharply reduces task accuracy, yet four standard scalar measures (CKA, SVCCA, MIR, and the leading principal-angle cosine) fail to consistently separate the corrupted stream from the original. We call this failure the alignment illusion and trace it to the shared language-model pathway: anisotropic MLP down-projections pull visual and text tokens toward common output directions, producing weight-induced alignment. We introduce the principal-angle gap (PA gap), defined as the difference between the top two principal-angle cosines, to distinguish leading-direction dominance from the broader overlap observed with structured visual content. Under graded visual corruption, the PA gap tracks task accuracy more consistently than the scalar scores we consider; under a structured but irrelevant image, it further exposes regimes in which internal geometry and task accuracy come apart. Internal visual-text alignment in MLLMs is therefore best read as a geometric diagnostic of the visual stream inside the language model rather than a direct proxy for content-level cross-modal interaction, and is most informative when calibrated by controlled task evidence.

papers.title: Learning the Maximum Tolerated Dose for Continuous Toxicity via Monotone Bayesian Trees
papers.abstract: Phase I cancer trials seek the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) while protecting patients from excessive toxicity. Dose assignments must therefore balance patient safety with learning the dose--toxicity relationship as data accrue. We model continuously measured toxicity outcomes using two forms of Bayesian additive regression trees (BART): isotonic BART projects posterior response curves onto nondecreasing functions, whereas monotone BART constrains the model. Joint curve and variance draws induce an MTD posterior that guides dose selection through escalation with overdose control (EWOC). We compare these methods with three parametric procedures across seven dose--toxicity curves in simulation. We assess dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) counts, above-MTD assignments, signed last-dose error, and relative absolute error. The tree procedures attained the lowest mean RAE on four nonlinear curves and jointly minimized mean DLT counts and above-MTD assignments on four curves. A Bayesian reinforcement learning perspective formulates these sequential decisions as a finite-horizon planning problem. Dose restrictions yield a lower bound on last-dose error; under exact posterior-predictive evaluation, an EWOC-based rollout policy has no greater expected weighted loss than its baseline. Dose Trial Lab, a desktop simulator for all five procedures, accompanies the supplementary material.

papers.title: SN 2025aedz: A typical short-plateau type IIP supernova with rapid post-peak decline
papers.abstract: Type IIP supernovae (SNe IIP) are the most common subclass of core-collapse SNe in observations. However, SNe IIP with short plateaus of the order of tens of days are rarely observed. The progenitors for this kind of SN can help to address the red supergiant issue in stellar evolution. In this article, we report optical photometry and spectroscopy of SN\,2025aedz, a rapidly post-peak declining SN IIP with a typical short plateau. It exhibits a peak absolute magnitude of $M_r=-17.16\pm0.03$\,mag. The $r$-band light curve shows a steep early post-peak decline of $\sim5\,\mathrm{mag}\,(100\,\mathrm{d})^{-1}$ followed by a relatively short plateau, with a plateau duration of $\sim50\pm3$\,d. The overall spectral evolution is consistent with that of normal SNe~IIP, showing a blue continuum with prominent Balmer P-Cygni profiles during the photospheric phase, followed by the gradual strengthening of hydrogen and metal lines as the ejecta cools down, although the metal lines remain weak and the expansion velocities decline rapidly. SN\,2025aedz is similar to the short-plateau SN\,2018gj in its overall evolution, whereas its pronounced early decline resembles that of SN\,2023ufx, which has the shortest plateau duration known so far. The radioactive tail of the bolometric light curve implies a synthesized $^{56}$Ni mass of $\sim0.03\pm0.01\,M_\odot$. Motivated by the steep early decline, we performed radiation hydrodynamic modelling using \texttt{MESA+STELLA} by exploring different circumstellar material configurations to reproduce its early bolometric light curve. These simulations indicate that SN\,2025aedz originated from a progenitor with a relatively low-mass hydrogen envelope, possibly produced through enhanced mass loss or binary interaction, while the steep early decline is likely explained by additional luminosity from circumstellar interaction.

papers.title: Hidden not Deleted: How Networks Suppress Entangled Features
papers.abstract: When a neural network stops reporting a feature, has it forgotten the feature or merely hidden it? Shared representations complicate the answer: removing one feature's direction can also damage another feature. We study this problem in a small autoencoder that compresses and reconstructs inputs, allowing individual feature contributions to be traced directly. With the representation fixed, restoring a single bias partially recovers target detection by exposing a signal hidden behind the output's activation threshold. Tests on target-absent inputs distinguish this recovery from interventions that simply increase output. The same bias intervention becomes less effective when the representation is allowed to change. We find that training only the other outputs can weaken the target's contribution, even without a loss on its own output. A conditional theoretical analysis explains how interference with retained predictions creates this pressure. Yet more flexible predictors still detect residual target information. These findings show how recovery depends on feature geometry and on which parameters are trained, and why a silent output is insufficient evidence of forgetting.

papers.title: Polynomial Decay in Absorbing Continuous-Time Markov Chains
papers.abstract: Let $P(t)$ be the transition function of an absorbing continuous-time Markov chain on a countable state space. We study asymptotic relations of the form $p_{ij}(t)\sim a_{ij} L(t)$, $t\to\infty$, where $L$ is independent of $i$ and $j$. We obtain general conditions under which the coefficient matrix $A=(a_{ij})$ has rank one and describe the resulting consequences for survival probabilities and conditional distributions. The analysis applies to both reducible and irreducible chains. We also construct an irreducible counterexample, based on a killed random walk on a homogeneous tree, for which a common asymptotic scale exists but the coefficient matrix has rank greater than one. This shows that irreducibility alone does not imply rank-one asymptotics. The results identify conditions under which fixed-state transition asymptotics determine the asymptotic behaviour of the entire transition function and clarify the limitations of such conclusions in the absence of additional structure.

papers.title: Contract-Based Decomposition of Temporal Logic Specifications for Networked Systems under Arbitrary Partitions
papers.abstract: Computational complexity is an inherent limitation of formal synthesis for networked systems, and decomposing the global specification into local ones relaxes this limitation at the cost of conservatism. Since the granularity of the partition governs this trade-off, it is reasonable to treat the partition as a design variable, which calls for local specifications that remain correct for every partition. To this end, this paper gives each agent a local specification, written as an assume-guarantee contract that the agent can establish from local information. We first derive a necessary and sufficient condition for these contracts to decompose the global specification under a given partition. Building on this, we then present a condition under which the decomposition is correct for every partition, so that the partition becomes a free design variable. For linear dynamics and signal temporal logic formulas with affine predicates, we further synthesize a controller for each coalition by a tube-based approach. Finally, simulations on a network of input-coupled tanks show how the choice of partition trades computational cost against conservatism.

papers.title: ResGraph: Cross-Model Graph-based Index Migration via Residual Reachability in ANN Search
papers.abstract: Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) underpins large-scale vector retrieval in search, recommendation, and retrieval-augmented generation. Graph-based indexes have demonstrated state-of-the-art search performance for ANNS: they connect each corpus vector to a small set of nearby or navigationally useful vertices and answer queries by traversing the resulting graph. Because these edges are selected using construction-time distances, the graph index is tied to the embedding model; re-encoding a corpus with a new model may change distances and neighborhoods of the vectors, and reconstructing the graph for the new embedding vectors incurs substantial construction cost and delays deployment. When the embedding model changes, we observe a phenomenon in the old graph index that we call residual reachability: although derived from different models, the vectors describe the same underlying objects and often retain part of their similarity structure, which the old graph reflects as connectivity, leaving many exact new-model neighbors reachable within a few hops. Motivated by this observation, we develop ResGraph, an index-migration framework that exploits the residual reachability of the old graph index to construct the new graph index faster. ResGraph provides two migration paths. Res-Local performs parallel shallow expansion over the inherited graph index and screens second-hop candidates with packed position sign codes before exact evaluation. Res-Search uses hop-bounded beam traversal to explore beyond shallow expansion. Across eight text and image migrations, ResGraph attains up to 17.43 times speedup on constructing the new graph index than the fastest degree-matched reconstruction method while keeping competitive recalls.

papers.title: Asymptotic counting of integers with prime factors $p_{r^a s^b}$
papers.abstract: Let $p_n$ be the $n$th prime, and let $r,s\ge2$ be fixed multiplicatively independent integers. We count the integers up to $x$ whose prime factors all have the form $p_{r^a s^b}$ with integers $a,b\ge0$. Our asymptotic formula for this count has relative error $o(1)$ and is explicit down to the multiplicative constant. For $(r,s)=(2,3)$ these integers are the prime codes of the ordinals below $ω^{ω^2}$, so the formula settles that case of the counting problem of Vernaeve, Vindas and Weiermann.

papers.title: Beyond Embedding Transfer: Architectural Interfaces, Iso-Parameter Scaling, and Preconditioner-Governed Consolidation in Grokking
papers.abstract: Grokking, or delayed generalization after memorization, incurs substantial training steps across algebraic tasks. Cross-operator transfer from a grokked donor accelerates target acquisition, yet post-grokking AdamW continuation triggers test-accuracy relapse as unannealed updates drift across residual interfaces and decaying second moments amplify late gradients. Across depths one to three on modular arithmetic ($\mathbb{Z}_{113}$), non-Abelian $S_5$ conjugation, and real-sensory MNIST modular arithmetic, we separate representational transfer from preconditioner-governed consolidation across thirteen experimental batteries. First, co-transferring internal blocks accelerates one-layer and two-layer modular takeoff beyond boundary interfaces, while graded prefix pinning bounds depth-three drift under unannealed continuation. Second, an iso-parameter $S_5$ scaling grid separates attention head dimension from MLP width: widening two-head attention to dimension $64$ reaches $98.54\%$ cold accuracy at $427\mathrm{k}$ parameters and $85.95\%$ boundary-only transfer, while final-slot representations refine conjugation directly across blocks without an intermediate binary-product bottleneck. Third, Plateau-Gated Leaky Consolidation pairs validation-envelope step damping with leaky second-moment decay, reaching $84.85\%$ zero-leakage validation-gated risk-constrained accuracy across five pre-saturation two-layer $S_5$ suites while cutting step budget relative to hard anchoring. Fourth, transferring a grokked visual trunk and blocks to image-disjoint MNIST targets reaches $92.27\%$ and $90.76\%$ accuracy, prunes odd centroid harmonics, and reaches $90.42\%$ risk-constrained accuracy across $60/60$ branches without hyperparameter retuning.

papers.title: Cloud-Edge LLM Collaborative Learning via Accelerating Personalized Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Amid the rapid advancement of physical-world intelligence, cloud-edge collaborative large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising roadmap for practical LLM deployment. However, existing cloud-edge paradigms struggle to balance global consensus with local personalization, which fails to satisfy the need for a unified knowledge foundation on the cloud and domain-specific adaptation at the edge. To address this, we propose a personalized bilevel optimization framework that formalizes cloud-edge LLM collaboration as a dual structure: the upper level optimizes edge-side personalization, while the lower level governs cloud-side knowledge transfer, reaching cloud-edge evolving in coordination. We then propose CIDERS: while the cloud performs knowledge transfer to the learnable backbone, the key lies in embedding global trajectories into each local personalization step via consensus-variate correction to reconcile personalization with consensus. We provide a comprehensive theoretical analysis, including a geometric characterization of the local trajectory and a full convergence guarantee, revealing an explicit trade-off structure between personalization and global convergence. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2-1.5B show CIDERS high performance and can significantly improve the accuracy (as much as 200\%+). Control-state diagnostics further show strong preservation of the local orthogonal component, while a separate cross-domain evaluation finds only a small matched-domain response advantage.

papers.title: Resonant saddles, tangencies with small spheres, and the characteristic flow
papers.abstract: We study resonant Siegel saddles in $\C^2$, with eigenvalue ratio $-p/q$, where $p,q$ are coprime positive integers, through their position relative to small round spheres. An intrinsic invariant $k$, defined through a resonance index that measures approximate first integrals, equals the first resonant obstruction. For $k<\infty$, the maximal contact order with the linear foliation is $m=k(p+q)+1$, and suitably normalized charts give $2k$ tangency circles. We compute their transverse type: resonant terms cancel to first order, and Poincaré--Dulac normalization through degree $2m-1$ makes every contact a saddle, while weaker normalization can produce elliptic arcs and periodic characteristic orbits. For the exact model we describe the whole-sphere flow and the correspondence between its tangency circles and separatrix sectors. In arbitrary charts the characteristic return map near a separatrix circle realizes its holonomy, whose $p$-th iterate has, when $k<\infty$, multiplicity $kp+1$, with $kp$ attracting and $kp$ repelling petals. Classical rigidity of resonant holonomy then recovers the analytic saddle class from $C^1$ orbital equivalence near that circle. We also describe tangency loci for arbitrary nondegenerate germs by the numerical range and the leading orbital form.

papers.title: Liouville regular Jordan curves
papers.abstract: We investigate Liouville regular Jordan curves, which were introduced in our previous paper as "Jordan curves that admit continuous Legendrian lifts". We prove that a Jordan curve satisfying certain variation conditions in a neighborhood of each point is Liouville regular. We also prove that the boundary of a Jordan domain is Liouville regular if the images of the radial tails under a conformal mapping have uniformly vanishing length. Together with our previous result, these criteria show that each such Jordan curve admits an inscribed rectangle in every prescribed similarity class.

papers.title: Who Is Prioritized? Current Need versus Predicted Gains in China's Dibao Allocation: Evidence from a Revealed-Allocation Model
papers.abstract: Using the 2017--2021 China Household Finance Survey panel and a sample of 3,102 households that did not receive Dibao in 2017, this paper applies the BBK revealed-allocation model to examine how household economic circumstances and predicted policy gains explain observed Dibao receipt in China. We find that household income is the allocation criterion most difficult to substitute with other factors. When all gain-adjustment terms are positive, constraining the income-rank coefficient to be nonnegative reduces the model's original improvement in fit by approximately 33.6\%; by contrast, setting both predicted-gain coefficients for food consumption and education spending to zero still preserves approximately 95.6\% of that improvement. These results indicate that observed Dibao allocation places greater emphasis on prioritizing households facing current livelihood hardship than on pursuing predictable short-run improvements in expenditure outcomes. This allocation orientation reflects the trade-off in social assistance between basic-livelihood protection and expected policy gains and offers a new perspective on the potential long-run social-welfare value of basic-livelihood protection.

papers.title: The periodic Wulff problem in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We characterize the minimizers of the anisotropic perimeter in the two-dimensional flat torus under an area constraint. We show that, as the prescribed area increases, global minimizers undergo two phase transitions, changing from a droplet (a rescaled Wulff shape) to a flat band wrapping around the torus in a preferred direction determined by the anisotropy (lamellar phase), and finally to a bubble (the complement of a reflected and rescaled Wulff shape). The transition thresholds are given explicitly in terms of the area and the lattice width of the Wulff shape. For certain non-symmetric surface tensions, the lamellar phase is absent altogether. Finally, we characterize the surface tensions for which further minimizers appear: this may happen only in the lamellar regime, and exactly when the Wulff shape has a corner whose normal cone contains, in its interior, a direction realizing the lattice width; in this case there are infinitely many minimizers.

papers.title: A Theory of Information Architecture for Networked Decisions: Freshness, Locality, and Coordination
papers.abstract: A broader view of a network can help agents coordinate, but collecting that view takes time. When is a fresh local observation more useful than an older view of the whole network, and when should an agent look only partway across it? We study agents that repeatedly minimize a shared quadratic cost in an environment that evolves independently of their actions. An information architecture specifies what each agent observes and how old those observations are. Each agent uses a synchronized neighborhood snapshot, so extending its scope also ages the nearby readings used in the decision. We assume that the optimal action with complete information is affine in the state, and that the conditional mean of the current state equals the old state scaled by a common exponential decay factor. Using the classical Marschak--Radner decomposition, we derive the delay threshold beyond which fresh local information outperforms a complete but older global view. This comparison allows non-Gaussian states and nonlinear decision rules. We then determine how far an agent should look by balancing the benefit of additional observations against their greater age. In a Gaussian spatial model on a line, we derive the optimal observation radius: looking beyond the local node pays only when information travels more than twice the spatial correlation length in one coherence time. The preferred information architecture also depends on the decision being made. On a fixed 64-node ring, increasing only the reach of the decision weights from 0.7 to 6 hops shifts the optimal observation radius from one to five hops.

papers.title: A Governance Methodology Layer for AI-Assisted Software Development: Defect Taxonomy, Controlled Ablation, and a Test of Process-Over-Capability
papers.abstract: Autonomous coding agents produce output that passes syntactic checks -- compilation, type safety, CI -- at high velocity. Yet syntactic correctness does not imply semantic correctness: design boundaries, security invariants, and maintainability contracts remain structurally invisible to automated pipelines. This paper makes four contributions. First, we present a defect-class taxonomy grounded in five AI agent permission and governance modules, separating defects structurally detectable by static analysis from those requiring semantic review. Second, we describe a runtime-decoupled governance gate -- a file-based protocol that reads generator output and emits a structured verdict without API coupling, hence portable across generators. Third, we formalize methodology-as-code: expressing a verification protocol as a version-controlled, executable artifact whose two layers separate portable methodology from host automation. Fourth, we report a controlled ablation experiment (E-ablation, N=5 artifacts, 8-item independent ground truth) comparing harness-structured review against a token-matched unstructured prompt. The structured condition records 62% lenient recall against 50%, with 25% strict against 0%. A severity-grade differential reported earlier does not survive blind re-grading and is withdrawn (Sec. 6.6). An independent-session re-test with blind scoring does not replicate that contrast: the conditions differ by one strict hit in 24 (6/24 against 5/24), the structured aggregate again 25% and the unstructured 0% not recurring (Sec. 6.7). Both conditions miss document-quality defects identified by a human QA reviewer, indicating complementarity between structured AI review and human process inspection. A later pre-registered test varying model tier (184 runs) did not support process design as the dominant factor: under strict scoring the tier effect was larger (Sec. 6.8).

papers.title: Exceptional model structures and the induced extriangulated categories
papers.abstract: A Hovey triple $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}, \mathcal{W})$ is {\it exceptional}, if $(\mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F}, \ \mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F} \cap \mathcal{W})$ is not a Frobenius pair. One has a disjoint union $\{\text{Hovey triple}\} = \{\text{Hereditary Hovey triple}\} \ \dot\bigcup \ \{\text{Exceptional Hovey triple}\}$ \ $\dot\bigcup \ \{\text{non-hereditary and non-exceptional Hovey triple}\}.$ Exceptional Hovey triples appear widely. For a selfinjective Nakayama algebra $A= kC_n/J^t$, $A\mbox{-}{\rm mod}$ admits exceptional Hovey triples if and only if $\gcd (n, t) \ge 2$ and $t \geq 3$. Their homotopy categories reveal new phenomena. Nakaoka-Palu's Theorem implies that there is a triangulation on $\frac{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W}.$ It is proved that a Hovey triple in a weakly idempotent complete extriangulated category $(\mathcal A, \mathbb E, \mathfrak s)$ is exceptional if and only if the induced extriangulated structure $\bigl(\frac{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W}, \ \overline{\mathbb E}, \ \overline{\mathfrak s}\bigr)$ is not {\it canonically triangulated}. Between this extriangulated structure and the one arising from the triangulation, the intermediate extriangulated structures are in one-to-one correspondence with Serre subcategories of $\mathrm{fp}((\frac{\mathcal P(\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F)}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W})^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathrm{Ab})$.

papers.title: Quasicrystalline Inflation: From the Cosmological Dipole to Primordial Diffraction
papers.abstract: We propose quasicrystalline inflation. Six quasiperiodic phases decompose into three phonons and three phasons. It turns out that a coherent pure-phason displacement can generate a local power dipole while the linear traceless quadrupole vanishes. From spatially varying quadratic effective field theory, we derive off-diagonal correlations whose momentum transfer is restricted to integer combinations of the six icosahedral wavevectors. These correlated off-diagonal signals provide a characteristic observational signature of primordial quasiperiodic order, primordial diffraction.

papers.title: The $α$-Limit Problem: Convergence of a Linear Degenerate Interface Transmission Problem
papers.abstract: We study the singular limit of a family of linear degenerate interface transmission problems arising from a regularization procedure in the newly proposed Two-Parameter Diffuse Domain Method (DDM2p). For $α>0$, the regularized problem admits a strictly convex variational formulation on $H^{1}(Ω)$. In the limit $α\to0$, the problem degenerates to a weakly coupled interface system with a nonstandard energy structure. To characterize the limit, we introduce a closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal{H}\subset H^{1}(Ω)$, defined through an auxiliary Helmholtz problem on an annular subdomain $Ω_2\subset Ω$, and identify the limiting energy functional $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ on $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that the regularized energies $\mathcal{E}_α$ restricted to $\mathcal{H}$ $Γ$-converge to $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ in the strong $L^{2}(Ω)$ topology, using the standard framework. Consequently, minimizers of $\mathcal{E}_α$ converge to the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{E}_{0}$, which is shown to be equivalent to the solution of the limiting interface problem.
