The proposed framework accommodates nontrivial intersections of local loss subspaces by retaining the coupling between the plant and common estimation errors. A Hurwitz condition on the coupled dynamics, together with a sufficient consensus-gain bound, guarantees exponential closed-loop convergence for every fixed feedback selection in a compact family. For polytopic feedback families, a quotient-preserving parameterization of output injections enables joint synthesis of nominal feedback and observer gains via alternating linear matrix inequalities, followed by a convex semidefinite program certifying a common consensus gain. A numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed design.

papers.title: On Applications of Polynomial-Time Group Isomorphism Algorithm
papers.abstract: The group isomorphism problem is a fundamental problem in computational group theory and is closely related to many other problems. Recently, Qiao and Zhang proposed a polynomial-time algorithm for finite group isomorphism in the multiplication-table model that computes the coset of all isomorphisms. Based on the algorithm of Qiao and Zhang, we study applications to finite associative ring isomorphism, bilinear map isotopism over finite commutative rings and free three-tensor isomorphism over finite commutative rings. First, we obtain a polynomial-time algorithm that returns the coset of all isomorphisms for finite associative rings. Second, we extend efficient isotopism and isomorphism algorithms for bilinear maps and free three-tensors from fields to general finite commutative rings.

papers.title: Separability defects in artificial satellite theory: intermediaries, zonal harmonics and secular separatrices
papers.abstract: A five-input Poisson-bracket operator, which reproduces the Levi-Civita separability expressions and is cubic in the Hamiltonian, is used as a diagnostic of artificial satellite theory, in a modified polar-nodal chart regular at prograde equatorial orbits. For the general intermediary proposed by the author in 2020, covering those of Sterne, Garfinkel, Brouwer, Aksnes, Cid and Lahulla and Deprit, the linearised defects vanish if and only if the integrability ansatz holds, the condition for additive first-order Hamilton-Jacobi separation in polar-nodal variables. Second-order defects follow in closed form, and the coupling with the nodal pair comes from the dependence on the physical latitude, shared by the zonal term, Aksnes's intermediary and the originals of Sterne and Garfinkel. For every axisymmetric field the radial defect is linear, with a torque form, and the first-order zonal defect is the operator response to the first-order Lie generator, which also gives the second-order mean radial defect per revolution. In its gauge the long-period second-order average is common to intermediaries without latitude terms. Oblate structures with a displaced centre separate the zonal field exactly if and only if its coefficients satisfy the recurrence of Vinti's translated spheroidal potential, and along orbits propagated over 300 periods in the field truncated at $J_4$ they conserve the approximate third integral better than the centred structure, by median factors of 23 to 77. On secular separatrices the integrated defect is the derivative of the Melnikov function, tested in the eccentric Kozai-Lidov problem, and transverse zero sets of the operator define event surfaces.

papers.title: Hybrid Krotov gradient descent Optimization for Quantum Machine Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a Krotov-inspired discrete adjoint optimization scheme for quantum machine learning and focus on a hybrid online-to-batch schedule. The method transfers the forward/costate/local-update logic of continuous-time optimal control to parameterized quantum circuits by replacing time locality with gate-index locality. For a broad class of fixed-generator variational gates and terminal-state losses, we show that the batch Krotov direction coincides with the exact gradient of the empirical loss. Under standard smoothness assumptions, this yields monotonic descent and convergence of the batch method, and convergence of the tail of the hybrid method after a finite switch to the batch phase. Empirically, we benchmark hybrid Krotov against the tuned PennyLane optimizer suite and L-BFGS-B on a four-bit parity classifier and on the Pérez-Salinas data re-uploading classifier for the crown problem. Across matched hyperparameter sweeps with three seeds per configuration, hybrid Krotov dominates every tuned first-order baseline and matches the strongest structured PennyLane methods on parity, while approaching the accuracy of L-BFGS-B on Pérez-Salinas at first-order per-iteration cost.

papers.title: Generalized hydraulic neural operators turbocharging sewer digital twins
papers.abstract: Hydraulic digital twins are emerging as the next-generation paradigm for operating and managing sewer systems. Conventional hydraulic digital twinning relies on running physics-based models (e.g., Saint-Venant equations), which are computationally expensive and often too slow for real-time applications. Although surrogates (e.g., neural networks) can be fast, existing approaches are typically non-generalizable, requiring costly retraining for unseen pipes, networks, or flow conditions. Here, we develop a fast, generalized and differentiable multi-branch neural operator trained on solutions of the Saint-Venant equations that predicts in-pipe hydraulics. The learned operator reproduces complex hydraulic dynamics with high fidelity while achieving thousand- to million-fold speedups for online prediction, data assimilation, and diagnostics. Equally importantly, the learned operator generalizes to unseen pipes, networks, and flow conditions without retraining. These advances address key computational barriers to real-time sewer digital twins, opening new opportunities for more responsive flood-risk management and protection of urban water environments.

papers.title: Few-Ion Schottky Power Scaling and Automated Reconstruction of Single-Ion Events
papers.abstract: Non-destructive Schottky diagnostics at heavy-ion storage rings is broadly exploited to measure revolution frequencies and intensities of stored ions. The mean Schottky power of incoherent stored ions is expected to be proportional to their number. An empirical examination of this response in few-ion populations is important for interpreting individual occupancy changes. We present an automated staircase reconstruction of the power in a selected frequency band of time-resolved Schottky spectra. The procedure was applied to 7008 selected injections recorded with a resonant cavity pickup at the Experimental Storage Ring at GSI during an experiment on the nuclear two-photon decay of the first excited $0^+$ state in bare $^{98}\mathrm{Mo}^{42+}$. The distribution of freely fitted level heights exhibits maxima close to integer multiples of a single-ion power scale up to approximately five ions. This is consistent with an approximately additive mean power response under the present measurement conditions. The reconstructed occupancy histories also retain population dwell intervals and resolved disappearance times for subsequent lifetime analyses.

papers.title: High-order IMEX local discontinuous Galerkin methods with sparse grids for high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop a high-order IMEX-LDG scheme on sparse grids for solving nonlinear parabolic PDEs in moderate to high dimensions. The method combines the advantages of LDG methods for convection--diffusion problems, IMEX-RK time integrators for stiff systems, and sparse-grid techniques to mitigate the curse of dimensionality. The resulting scheme is fully parallelized in MPI, is robust, efficient, and scalable, making it suitable for a wide range of applications involving high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs.

papers.title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
papers.abstract: Direct image-to-video diffusion models entangle pixel synthesis with implicit latent motion, precluding persistent 3D mechanical equilibrium, mid-rollout intervention, and counterfactual force control. Conversely, single-pass programmatic 3D reconstruction from an uncalibrated photograph leaves monocular depth and support clearance underconstrained, causing reconstructed scenes to interpenetrate or collapse under gravity. We present TelePhysica, a closed-loop framework that reconstructs an executable, multi-regime physical world from a single photograph to drive stateful 3D interaction and trajectory-grounded video synthesis. A vision-language coding agent synthesizes separable visual meshes and declarative physical models within a two-stage verification loop that pairs pixel-aligned silhouette critique with a zero-force gravitational equilibrium preflight. The verified world compiles into a unified solver coupling rigid bodies, articulated chains, co-dimensional cloth shells, and 3D tetrahedral elastodynamics, whose simulated rollouts condition pretrained video diffusion models through pixel-aligned structural streams. On a 100-scene single-image benchmark, closed-loop execution raises equilibrium-verified world recovery from $0\%$ in single-pass synthesis to $81\%$. Controlled constitutive ablations show over an order-of-magnitude larger localized corner displacement and out-of-plane pleating in finite-element cloth than in matched rigid-plate proxies. Conditioning video diffusion on simulated trajectories increases dynamic motion-mask overlap by $2{\times}\text{--}5{\times}$ and preserves motion direction under counterfactual force reversals where direct image-to-video models fail.

papers.title: Grid-Compliance Testing of Wind Turbines through Virtualized Component Tests: Testing Concept and Test Bench
papers.abstract: As the proportion of inverter-connected wind turbines increases, test methods for evaluating their grid behavior are becoming increasingly important. This paper presents a Power Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHiL)-based method for grid connection testing of wind turbines. For the first time, geographically distributed simulations of aerodynamics via the Internet and of the grid model via a fiber-optic connection are integrated into certification-relevant tests. The concept expands upon the methods described in IEC TS 61400-21-4. Initial experimental results confirm high emulation quality and sufficiently low latencies, and meet the requirements for a standards-compliant grid emulation.

papers.title: Upper bounds for the number of spanning forests of a graph
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $F(G)$ denote the number of spanning forests of $G$. Bencs and Csikvári proved that every $r$-regular graph $G$ with $r\ge 2$ satisfies $F(G)\le r^n$. Motivated by this result, they conjectured that if $G$ has minimum degree at least $3$, then $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$, where $(d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n)$ is the degree sequence of $G$. In this paper, we prove that graphs with minimum degree at least $n/3$ $(n\geq7)$ satisfy $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$. We also construct a counterexample to the conjecture. We therefore further study the enumeration of spanning forests in general graphs, proving an upper bound in terms of the degree sequence and characterizing the extremal graphs attaining this bound. In addition, using the matrix-forest theorem, we obtain an upper bound for the number of spanning forests of a connected graph in terms of its algebraic connectivity, and characterize the extremal graphs attaining this bound.

papers.title: Zero-SM NCCL: A Systematic Guide to Designing and Deploying SM-Free GPU Communication
papers.abstract: GPU communication libraries such as NCCL use Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) for data movement and synchronization, slowing overlapped computation at a cost that grows with interconnect bandwidth. We present Zero-SM NCCL, which communicates within and across scale-up domains without launching any SM kernel. It synchronizes through CUDA stream memory operations, moves data asynchronously with copy engines within a scale-up domain, and drives network RDMA from a stream-ordered CPU proxy. It supports data-movement collectives such as AllGather and AlltoAll, plus one-sided ncclPutSignal and ncclWaitSignal APIs. On GB200 NVL72 and B200 NVL8 systems, Zero-SM collectives reach up to 1.36x higher AllGather bandwidth than NCCL's legacy SM-based kernels and cut the median slowdown of overlapped GEMMs from 33% to 4%, at a higher latency per operation. In Megatron-LM training, they accelerate FSDP by up to 3.5%, and one-sided puts accelerate pipeline parallelism by up to 15%. Zero-SM communication is not a universal win, however. Through an end-to-end study across models and parallelism strategies, we show that it pays off for large transfers in GPU-bound workloads and for deep pipelines with large bubbles, but loses on small messages and host-bound workloads. We distill these findings into guidelines for enabling zero-SM communication in NCCL and building it into other libraries.

papers.title: Learning nonlinear interactions and cross-feature couplings with product-unit residual networks
papers.abstract: Understanding nonlinear feature interactions is crucial in science and engineering, yet standard multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) often capture such interactions only implicitly, leading to entangled representations that can impair robustness and interpretability. We investigate complex-valued product-unit residual networks (CV-PURe) that integrate multiplicative product units with residual connections to explicitly model cross-feature couplings while stabilizing optimization. We conduct a systematic evaluation on an interaction-driven synthetic benchmark and real-world datasets and evaluate prediction together with input-level interaction recovery under a reproducible protocol. Across five data splits and five training seeds, CV-PURe achieves the lowest mean RMSE on four of six scientific benchmarks, reducing Friedman error by 53.9% relative to MLP. Its Friedman interaction maps assign 60.7% of total strength to the known interacting pair, compared with 31.0% for MLP. On a synthetic task containing third- and fourth-order products and 20 distractors, CV-PURe reduces RMSE from 0.1376 to 0.0797 relative to a complex-valued MLP and recovers all nine true pairwise projections in every training/sampling repetition. Bike Sharing experiments connect improved prediction to the contribution of temporal, calendar, and seasonal context through paired ablations of both PURe variants. Parkinsons Telemonitoring extends the context analysis to repeated measurements. Noise and learning-curve evaluations demonstrate sustained predictive gains under perturbed inputs and limited supervision, while inference measurements quantify computational cost. This article extends our ICCS 2026 paper, Modeling Nonlinear Feature Interactions with Product-Unit Residual Networks (doi:10.1007/978-3-032-29921-5_6).

papers.title: Vestiges of magnon fractionalization in the quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet rouaite Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ with alternating ferro- and antiferromagnetic $S=\frac{1}{2}$ chains
papers.abstract: Ferro- and antiferromagnetic quantum spin chains host qualitatively distinct elementary excitations --- magnons ($S=1$, bosonic quasiparticles) and spinons ($S=\frac{1}{2}$, fractionalized quasiparticles), respectively. Weakly coupled networks of both chain types therefore provide an ideal platform for exploring spinon-magnon coupling and the hybridization of sharp magnon modes with spinon continua. Here we investigate the spin-excitation spectrum of the frustrated quantum magnet rouaite, Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ --- a model realization of weakly coupled ferro- and antiferromagnetic Cu$^{2+}$ spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ chains. The frustrated interchain interactions, while weaker than the dominant intrachain exchange, are sufficient to stabilize a long-range-ordered state that is not reproduced by classical calculations. Neutron spectroscopy reveals a spectrum of well-defined spin waves associated with both types of chains, with clear signatures of hybridization but no observable spinon continuum. Certain magnon branches resulting from this hybridization exhibit substantial broadening near the zone center. We attribute this to vestiges of spinon fractionalization persisting partway through the dimensional crossover from isolated quantum spin chains to a 2D network of frustrated spins.

papers.title: Measuring Public Participation in Local Government: An Audio-Based Instrument for Classifying Speakers in City Council Meetings
papers.abstract: How much does the public actually speak in local government? Despite sustained interest in democratic participation, we lack large-scale measures of public voice at the local level, because the underlying record -- audio of open meetings -- has been prohibitively costly to convert into data. We contribute a measurement instrument: an audio-analysis pipeline that classifies each speaker in a city council meeting as an elected official or a member of the public directly from audio, and aggregates these labels into validated measures of participation such as floor-time share. The pipeline first segments each recording by speaker, then classifies each speaker with a multimodal large language model (MLLM), using the meeting's own temporal structure (neighboring speakers, iterative refinement, and a majority vote across three classifiers) as supporting components. We collect 1,618 recordings from seven U.S. cities (2017-2023); after diarization and quality control, the analytic corpus is 1,565 meetings from five cities. The task is non-trivial: audio quality is uneven, members of the public speak informally and are often introduced only briefly, and speech frequently overlaps. Even so, segmentation reaches 89% accuracy (mean pairwise kappa=0.84), and the classifier reaches 87.7% accuracy (kappa=0.736, public-participant F1=0.832) on ground truth from five cities (N=1,761 speakers) -- agreement comparable to that among the human annotators themselves. At scale, members of the public receive a median of just 10% of floor time, the top speaker is an official in over 94% of meetings, and public participation declined over COVID-19 without recovering by 2023. The instrument measures participation directly from audio, without transcription or linkage to external voter or property records, establishing audio-as-data as a practical approach for the study of local politics.

papers.title: Spin-adapted sample-based quantum diagonalization with randomized time evolution
papers.abstract: Quantum algorithms based on the classical post-processing of measurement samples have emerged as effective and robust methods to approximate low-energy wavefunctions of many-body quantum systems on present-day and early-fault-tolerant quantum devices. This paper introduces a generic framework for enforcing spin symmetry within these approaches. We tailor this framework to SqDRIFT, a sample-based quantum diagonalization variant that uses the qDRIFT randomized compilation protocol to generate the quantum samples. We discuss how three key components of SqDRIFT (the initial-state preparation, the construction of the time-evolution circuits, and the classical post-processing) can be adapted to incorporate spin symmetry. We show that spin-pure circuits alone are not sufficient, since the sampled determinants generally span a subspace that is not closed under $\hat{S}^2$, and we restore this closure by completing the sampled electronic configurations. In classical simulations of 4-aminobenzonitrile and of an $[\text{Fe}(\text{NH}_{3})_{4}]^{2+}$ model complex, and in experiments on an IBM quantum processor for the oxo-Mn(Salen) complex, this spin-adapted post-processing yields roots that are exact spin eigenfunctions at every subspace size. On hardware, it does so with diagonalized subspaces two to three orders of magnitude smaller than those of the conventional constructions for the same circuit depth.

papers.title: Stochastic inverse source problem in inhomogeneous media: far-field statistics
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with an inverse random source problem for the stochastic Helmholtz equation in a known three-dimensional inhomogeneous medium. The source is driven by spatial white noise. We seek to recover its mean and strength from the mean and cross-frequency covariance of the far-field pattern. For a smooth nontrapping wave speed, we use the spectral measure of the acoustic operator to relate the far-field data to the source statistics. Under a priori regularity bounds, this relation gives conditional stability for the source mean and the source strength. We derive explicit reconstruction formulas for both quantities and bound the errors due to frequency truncation and data perturbations. We also obtain mean-square error bounds for reconstructions from finitely many independent experiments. Numerical experiments illustrate the reconstruction accuracy and the effects of bandwidth and sample size.

papers.title: Quantifying the Advantage of Coarser DPOR
papers.abstract: Dynamic partial-order reduction (DPOR) has emerged as a promising approach to addressing interleaving explosion in bounded model checking of concurrent programs. Given an equivalence relation on interleavings, the model checker explores a program's executions while minimizing repeated visits to the same class; optimal model checkers avoid such repetition altogether. A coarser equivalence promises faster exploration by reducing the number of classes. This has motivated alternatives to Mazurkiewicz's trace equivalence such as reads-from and reads-value-from equivalence. This promise, however, does not always materialize in practice: while a coarser equivalence can yield exponentially fewer classes on some families of programs, it may offer little or no reduction for the program at hand. We show how to quantify the advantage of coarser equivalences for individual programs. We focus on the problem of counting the reads-from (RF) equivalence classes induced by a given program, as well as the problem of computing the ratio of RF to Mazurkiewicz class counts under sequential consistency. We show that both problems are $\#\mathrm{P}$-hard and that the reduction ratio remains hard to approximate accurately under standard complexity assumptions. Guided by these limits, we present CoEst, a sampling-based algorithm for estimating both the RF count and its ratio to the Mazurkiewicz count. For a fixed number of threads, each trial runs in polynomial time and yields unbiased count estimates. As the number of independent trials grows, the count and ratio estimates converge almost surely to their true values. Our algorithm can provide statistical evidence for deciding whether Mazurkiewicz or RF model checking is likely to be faster for a given program. In experiments across 34 benchmark configurations, our method selects the faster checker in 99.4% of runs using a one-minute estimation budget.

papers.title: A Realizability-Based Kinetic-Fluid Domain Decomposition Method for Single-Temperature Gas Mixtures
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a domain-adaptive numerical method for multi-species kinetic models that relax toward a single-temperature and single-velocity hydrodynamic limit. To this end, we derive moment realizability matrices for this regime. In this way the ideas of Levermore, Morokoff, and Nadiga are extended to non-equilibrium mixtures in which inter-species and intra-species collisions occur at comparable rates, so that all species relax to a common velocity and a common temperature. The realizability conditions are used as an indicator to divide the computational domain, at each time step, into macroscopic and kinetic regions. In the kinetic regions, where the continuum description fails (e.g., across strong shocks, non-equilibrium interfaces, or kinetic boundary layers), the method solves the multi-species kinetic equations. Close to local thermodynamic equilibrium, the Euler equations of the mixture are solved instead. Confining the kinetic computations to the non-equilibrium regions reduces the simulation time, while the results remain close to those of the full kinetic solver. The method is discretized on Cartesian grids with high-order schemes in space and time. The kinetic equations are integrated with an Asymptotic-Preserving Implicit-Explicit (IMEX) scheme, so that a consistent discretization of the single-velocity, single-temperature Euler system of the mixture is recovered when the Knudsen number goes to zero. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first realizability-based adaptive spatial domain decomposition method for gas mixtures in this single-velocity, single-temperature setting.

papers.title: Agent-as-a-Judge
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has progressed from task-specific systems toward general models spanning perception, generation, reasoning, and autonomous interaction, making reliable evaluation essential for comparison, deployment, and post-training feedback. At scale, modern evaluation pipelines increasingly rely on LLM-as-a-Judge to produce scores, preferences, and critiques; in its fixed-context setting, the judge relies on the supplied evaluand and evaluation materials. Yet a reliable verdict may require evidence beyond the supplied evaluand and context---either because critical environmental states remain unrecorded in the static execution log, or because controversial factual claims require external verification. Passive judges cannot obtain that missing evidence before deciding, especially when evaluating agent trajectories, executable artifacts, or domain-specific reports. Recent work therefore develops active evaluators that seek missing evidence and update their grounds for judgment before deciding. We bring these advances together through Agent-as-a-Judge, focusing on how evaluators construct and control checking processes within the broader LLM-based judging landscape. We define the scope through evaluation-directed checks and the use of their results, covering both structured workflows and observation-driven control. We organize the design space by multi-agent collaboration, tool integration, memory, and planning, and show how these mechanisms supply the checks and evidence on which a verdict rests. We consolidate published scores and reproduce missing entries for key agentic judges; the comparison reveals uneven agentic gains and motivates dedicated agentic evaluation. We conclude by characterizing application demands and open challenges in cost, reliability, safety, and governance that condition trusted deployment of agentic judges at scale.

papers.title: Product units in gated recurrent networks enhance prediction of nuclear masses and charge radii
papers.abstract: The prediction of nuclear properties using machine learning can complement theoretical models and advance the exploration of poorly known domains of the nuclear chart. We propose a machine learning technique for predicting nuclear masses and charge radii based on gated recurrent units (GRU) that integrates learnable product-unit mappings into the candidate state to model multiplicative dependencies among neighboring nuclei. Computations are performed in the complex domain to jointly capture amplitude and phase dynamics. Across three data partitions and three training seeds per partition, AM-PU-GRU achieves a mean mass interpolation RMSE of 0.2698 MeV and a temporal RMSE of 0.1905 MeV. Configuration comparisons support the integration of learned products into gated recurrence. Without mass inputs, MI-PU-GRU predicts charge radii with an RMSE of 0.019947 fm, 14.40% below the fixed WS* prior. Matched radius controls further show how candidate fusion shapes the benefit of learned products. Paired errors, nuclide-resolved maps, and inference measurements characterize predictive gains and computational cost. This article is an extended version of our ICCS 2026 conference paper (doi:10.1007/978-3-032-29921-5_10).

papers.title: Linear-optical generation of approximate higher-component cat states
papers.abstract: We propose a method for generating higher-component cat states by interfering two $N$-component cat states on a half beam splitter and measuring one output with a photon-number-resolving detector. The Fock components of the conditional output are restricted to a single residue class modulo $2N$. For $N=3$, an ideal six-component cat state can be generated exactly, while for arbitrary $N$, the conditional output approaches an ideal $2N$-component cat state for sufficiently large input amplitudes.

papers.title: A$^3$: Adaptive Audio Agent Framework for Collaborative Edge Computing
papers.abstract: Embedded audio agents need a nearby edge server for speed, but a server-dependent agent returns nothing when the link fails. We present A$^3$, an adaptive audio agent framework that places whole pipeline stages on the server, keeps a complete fallback agent on devices that can host one, and hedges both paths with a link-aware deadline that decides when to give up on the server. On Jetson devices and an RTX A4500 server, A$^3$ matches the server-only agent on a healthy link, answers every request in a full outage on the AGX, and beats a percentile hedge in simulated outages.

papers.title: Spectrum of a 2D QFT analogue of the SYK model
papers.abstract: We study the spectrum of the two-dimensional generalisation of the SYK model proposed by Turiaci and Verlinde, in which chiral Majorana fermions with a topological kinetic term interact through random $2q$-fermion couplings. We compute the four-point function at order $1/N$ in the conformal limit. In addition to the conformal Casimir, the ladder kernels commute with the operator that exchanges a single lightcone coordinate. As a result, the four-point function splits into an even and an odd sector, which the kernels do not mix. In each sector we construct a complete eigenbasis of the Casimir, find the eigenvalues of the kernels in closed form and sum the ladder diagrams. The poles in the ladder sum lie on a spectral curve in the plane of the two conformal weights. A conformal solution in the IR limit breaks the symmetries of the model under chiral reparametrisations and local Lorentz transformations, and the kernel has eigenvalue one on the corresponding modes. The reparametrisation modes, with conformal weights $(2,0)$ and $(0,2)$, are non-normalisable, whereas the Lorentz mode of the odd sector, with weights $(1,1)$, is normalisable. We determine the region where the sum of ladders can be represented in a contour form analogous to that of the one-dimensional SYK model.

papers.title: Exact stochastic theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation mediated by RNA-binding proteins
papers.abstract: While analytical theories of transcriptional feedback loops have been well established, exact stochastic analyses of post-transcriptional feedback loops remain relatively scarce and are notoriously challenging. Here, we develop an exact theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation, in which reversible protein-mRNA binding modulates both translation and mRNA stability. We derive the state-dependent protein burst-size distribution, the steady-state protein number distribution in terms of confluent Heun functions, and an exact criterion for sub-Poissonian fluctuations. By comparing transcriptional and post-transcriptional networks, we reveal a reversal in their relative advantages in noise suppression and rhythm transmission: negative feedback favors post-transcriptional regulation, whereas positive feedback favors transcriptional regulation. Our results reveal how the regulatory pattern fundamentally shapes gene expression fluctuations and dynamic responses.

papers.title: Strong endpoint estimates for bilinear spherical averaging operators on closed hypersurfaces and curved patches
papers.abstract: Tainara Borges~\cite[Section~7.1, Question~7.2]{Borges2026} asked whether the strong $L^1\times L^1\to L^{1/2}$ estimate for bilinear spherical averages extends to all compact smooth hypersurfaces without boundary and with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We give a positive answer when $d\ge2$. The geometric argument concerns the difference projection $(y,z)\mapsto y-z$: at every critical point, two definite directions in its fiber already ensure that the projected surface measure has bounded density. This condition holds for the closed hypersurfaces in the original question. The ensuing strong endpoint uses the localization principle of Iosevich, Palsson and Sovine~\cite[Propositions~4.1--4.2]{IPS2022}. Our proof also establishes a partial positive result for the curvature-rank problem in Borges~\cite[Question~7.1]{Borges2026}. We exhibit a smooth full-curvature patch with boundary for which the strong estimate fails. The endpoint yields the entire fixed-scale Hölder family.

papers.title: Probing Dirac Heavy Neutral Leptons through EFT-Induced Meson Decays
papers.abstract: We investigate dimension-six operators involving pairs of Dirac-type heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) at beam-dump and far-forward experiments. In the $ν$SMEFT framework, lepton-number-conserving four-fermion operators couple HNL pairs to quarks and induce two and three-body charm and bottom meson decays. We study the $c\to u$, $b\to d$, and $b\to s$ transitions at FASER2, FACET, SHiP, and two FPF@FCC configurations. HNL production depends on the cut-off scale $Λ$, while the lifetime depends on the active-sterile mixing $|V_{eN}|^2$. Sizable production can therefore coexist with the small mixing needed for HNLs to reach distant detectors. We project sensitivities in the $(M_N,|V_{eN}|^2)$ and $(M_N,Λ)$ planes, accounting for two and three-body decays and constraints from invisible and semivisible meson decays. SHiP is particularly sensitive to $c\to u$, while the larger FCC-LLP2 configuration probes $b\to d, s$. We find that EFT-induced pair production extends long-lived HNL searches to very small mixing and complements other probes of the $ν$SMEFT heavy-neutrino sector.

papers.title: Compatible zero-sum partitions of finite Abelian groups and their applications
papers.abstract: Let $(Γ,+)$ be a finite Abelian group and let $g\inΓ\setminus\{0\}$. A partition of $Γ$ is called $g$-compatible if no part contains both $x$ and $x+g$. For a prescribed involution $h$ and odd $r\ge3$, we prove that $Γ$ admits an $h$-compatible partition into zero-sum $r$-element sets if and only if $r$ divides $|Γ|$ and $Γ$ has at least three involutions. Moreover, the partition can be chosen so that the multigraph whose vertices are its parts and whose edges are the pairs $\{x,x+h\}$ is Hamiltonian and has a proper edge coloring with $r$ colors. We also give examples, for groups of odd order and for even block sizes, in which zero-sum partitions exist but compatible ones do not. We give two applications of these partitions. For block size three, we obtain complete mappings whose cycles are precisely the parts of the partition. We also construct Hamiltonian $r$-regular $Γ$-distance-magic graphs admitting $0$ and every involution of $Γ$ as magic constants.

papers.title: Perfect Matching Complexes of $3\times 2n$ Grid Graph
papers.abstract: The perfect matching complex of a simple graph $G$ is an abstract simplicial complex whose facets (maximal faces) are precisely the perfect matchings of $G$. In this article, we study the topology of the perfect matching complex of the $3\times 2n$ grid graph and show that it is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of $f_{n-1}$ copies of $(n-1)$-dimensional spheres, where $f_{k}$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number. This proves a particular case of the conjecture given by Chandrakar and Singh for perfect matching complex of grid graphs.

papers.title: SWAM: Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging for Efficient Vision Transformers
papers.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve strong performance on image recognition tasks, yet their quadratic self-attention complexity over input tokens creates prohibitive computational costs for practical deployment. Token reduction methods offer a practical solution by progressively reducing the token sequence during the forward pass. We propose Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging (SWAM), a training-based token merging framework that extends the Bipartite Soft Matching (BSM) with two saliency-aware mechanisms. We introduce a two-step matching formulation in which cosine similarity decides candidate pairs, while a multiplicative maximum saliency penalty regulates their selection for merging. We then further use asymmetric exponential saliency-weighted aggregation, which allows more salient tokens to contribute more strongly to the merged representation. A lightweight MLP-based saliency prediction module (75k parameters per stage, 1% of backbone parameters) supervised via attention rollout is trained end-to-end jointly with a DeiT-Small backbone using a composite cross-entropy, knowledge-distillation, and saliency-alignment objective. On CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-100, under a conservative schedule that reduces tokens from 196 to 100 patch tokens, with the CLS token retained throughout, 27.5% FLOPs reduction and 1.35 times speedup, SWAM matches or exceeds baseline across the reported results. Under an aggressive schedule (196 to 70 tokens with the CLS token kept throughout, 33.8% FLOPs reduction, and 1.46 times speedup), accuracy gains are achieved on ImageNet-100 (+0.23%) with minimal losses on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet.

papers.title: Unsupervised Machine Learning Classification of FRB 20121102A across Distinct Active Episodes: Implications for FRB Emission Physics and Source Environments
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin. Identifying distinct burst populations and investigating their variations across active episodes provide important insights into the physical origins of repeating FRBs. In this paper, we apply an unsupervised machine learning approach to bursts from three active episodes of FRB 20121102A observed by the Five-hundred-metre Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST). Our analysis reveals four distinct clusters primarily distinguished by their spectral properties. Notably, Cluster 1 exhibits bimodal-like distributions in central frequency and bandwidth and contains nearly all high-energy bursts, with a mean energy about an order of magnitude higher than those of the other clusters. It also occupies a distinct region in the width--fluence parameter space. These results suggest that this cluster may represent a distinct burst population potentially associated with different emission physics. Furthermore, the fractions of different burst clusters vary across active episodes. Cluster 1 accounts for about 27\% of the bursts in 2019, compared with about 8\% in 2022 and 2023. Cluster 2, with higher central frequencies and narrower bandwidths, has the largest fraction in 2019 and 2022, whereas Cluster 3, with broader bandwidths and intermediate central frequencies, has the largest fraction in 2023. These variations may indicate changes in the physical conditions of the emission regions or the local propagation environment across active episodes.

papers.title: DeCompCert: A Verified Decompiler for CompCert-Generated AArch64
papers.abstract: DeCompCert is a Rocq-verified decompiler for AArch64 assembly generated by CompCert. It reconstructs CompCert C through nine reverse passes, combining deductively verified transformations with translation validation. Untrusted OCaml and Datalog analyses propose candidate reconstructions, while verified validators accept only candidates that satisfy the required semantic correspondence. The composed correctness theorem guarantees that every defined, safe behavior of an accepted C reconstruction is matched by the input CompCert assembly; under a safety assumption, the two programs are observationally equivalent. We evaluate DeCompCert on approximately 2.16 million lines of C. With exact function and call signatures, it reconstructs and recompiles all 3,173 eligible contexts under both unoptimized and optimized CompCert pipelines. Without retained signatures, its cumulative inference portfolio validates 2,606 of 3,164 contexts (82.4%), while the platform-plus-IDA configuration validates 2,407 contexts (76.1%). Native execution and output-quality experiments further evaluate the generated C and characterize the remaining limitations in signature recovery and source resemblance.

papers.title: Endogenous Parcel Contiguity and Rent Indeterminacy in a Finite-Household Monocentric City
papers.abstract: We study a monocentric city with finitely many households, each of which may hold any measurable set of land and incurs commuting costs that depend on the spatial distribution of its holdings. In equilibrium, every parcel is an interval and parcels are ordered by lot size from the center outward. The freedom to adjust land holdings at any location restricts supporting rents to a band between the competing bid rents and the assigned household's bid rent. This band excludes rents that support the same allocation when lots are restricted to intervals, including the one constructed by Berliant and Fujita (1992), and makes the existence of a supporting rent a substantive question even with identical households. We give sufficient conditions for the existence of a locally supporting rent that meets every household's budget and deters all small deviations. We also show that any equilibrium minimizes the real resource cost of attaining equilibrium utilities and extend the sorting result to heterogeneous households under a single-crossing condition. Finally, we discuss the relation to hedonic models, distinguishing the prices of whole parcels from location-specific rents that govern the cost of changes in parcel boundaries and fragmentation.

papers.title: InfiHall-Bench: A Benchmark for Hallucination Evaluation in Autoregressive Text-to-Image Generation
papers.abstract: Hallucination benchmarks for text-to-image generation are predominantly designed around diffusion models, limiting their diagnostic value for visual autoregressive (VAR) models and the development of mitigation methods. We identify two limitations in existing prompt construction paradigms: many prompts are no longer challenging for modern generators, while category-based construction relies on recurring object-attribute-relation templates and rarely tests interactions among multiple visual requirements within a single image. We introduce InfiHall-Bench, a controlled benchmark of 411 prompts constructed by systematically composing five foundational and visually verifiable skills: attribute binding, spatial relation, action relation, part consistency, and scene consistency. Each prompt covers 4.05 annotated skills on average, enabling the evaluation of hallucinations under diverse combinations of visual requirements. Using this benchmark, we find that hallucinations in VAR models exhibit a scale-wise persistence pattern: semantic errors can emerge at different autoregressive scales and are rarely corrected by subsequent fine-scale steps. Motivated by this observation, we propose Confidence-Masked Hallucination Mitigation (CMHM), which estimates the prediction confidence of target visual tokens at each autoregressive scale during teacher-forced fine-tuning. CMHM downweights reliably predicted tokens, allowing optimization to focus on uncertain predictions across scales. Experiments show that InfiHall-Bench distinguishes models that existing compositional benchmarks rate as comparable, while CMHM consistently outperforms uniform LoRA fine-tuning for VAR-based text-to-image generation.

papers.title: evgmrf: An R Package For Gaussian Markov Random Field Extreme Value Models
papers.abstract: We introduce \textsf{evgmrf}, an \textsf{R} package for fitting spatially varying extreme value models using Gaussian Markov random fields (GMRFs). The package supports the generalized extreme value distribution for block maxima, the generalized Pareto distribution for threshold exceedances, the Poisson--GPD point-process model, and the $r$-largest order-statistics model. Distributional parameters may vary over regular spatial grids or arbitrary regions that can be represented by a valid adjacency matrix, with optional fixed effects and covariate dependence. Spatial structure is represented through intrinsic conditional autoregressive, proper conditional autoregressive, and Besag--York--Mollié 2 models, which are extended with non-Gaussian random-effect distributions. Estimation uses penalized likelihood with smoothing or dependence hyper-parameters estimated using a Laplace approximation, exploiting sparse precision matrices for computational efficiency. The package provides methods for model summaries, spatial visualization, prediction on link and response scales, estimation of extreme quantiles, and uncertainty quantification in the form of approximate standard error estimates, or via simulations from parameter sampling distributions. Examples based on gridded and county-level precipitation data illustrate the use of the package for spatial modelling of environmental extremes. \textsf{evgmrf} provides a unified, accessible framework for extreme value analyses in which distributional parameters exhibit structured spatial variation.

papers.title: Stochastic Nonlocal Conservation Laws with Lévy Noise: Stability, BV Estimates, and Vanishing Viscosity
papers.abstract: We study one-dimensional stochastic nonlocal conservation laws with a convolution-type interaction field, driven by multiplicative Brownian noise and compensated Poisson random measures. The nonlocal operator modifies the classical entropy structure, while the jump noise produces nonlinear correction terms in the entropy inequality. We introduce a notion of stochastic entropy solution and establish an $L^1$-stability estimate using spatial doubling of variables and the Itô--Lévy formula. This yields uniqueness in the vanishing-viscosity class and, under additional bounds, a localized Cauchy estimate of order $\sqrt{\varepsilon+\varepsilon'}$. Existence is obtained by vanishing viscosity: we construct the viscous solutions through a Faedo--Galerkin scheme and derive viscosity-uniform $L^1$ and localized $BV$ estimates, which allow us to pass to the limit and obtain a spatially $BV$ stochastic entropy solution.

papers.title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls
papers.abstract: When a conversational Voice AI agent places an outbound call, the far end may be a live person, a voicemail greeting, an interactive voice response (IVR) system, or increasingly another AI system answering on the callee's behalf. Standard Answering Machine Detection (AMD) reports only whether a human or a machine picked up, a design meant for human call centres, where one machine is as uninteresting as another. That single bit does not tell a Voice AI agent what to do, since leaving a voicemail message, navigating an IVR and holding a short exchange with another AI are three different actions and a two-valued label cannot distinguish them. In 1,000 randomly sampled calls from our own outbound deployment, a live person answered 48.1%, a voicemail system 44.6%, an AI 6.9% and an IVR 0.4%. Our proposed framework, FEND, reads the far end's audio and its streaming transcript and runs one detector for each automated class (voicemail, IVR, AI callee), with human the default when nothing fires, returning a single label within 20 seconds. On a public benchmark the voicemail components reach 100% accuracy without ever misclassifying a live human, where Asterisk's AMD misclassifies 30 to 66% of them. For the AI callee, acoustic features do not transfer across recording conditions, but speech timing does, separating AI from human at 0.952 ROC-AUC, because synthesised speech leaves far shorter gaps between words. On production traffic, separating a live person from any automated far end reaches F1 0.979, and only 2.9% of live people are given an automated label, the error that matters most for an agent acting on the result.

papers.title: Extending indoor airborne infection risk modelling to 3D, with local surface deposition
papers.abstract: Mathematical models of indoor airborne disease transmission often rely on simplifying assumptions to reduce computational cost. In particular, aerosol concentrations may be assumed uniform across room height, allowing a two-dimensional (2D) formulation, while particle deposition on surfaces is represented by a first-order removal term acting throughout the computational domain. Here, we investigate how these assumptions affect predictions of airborne infection risk. We extend the Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS) [Xue et al. 2024] by developing a three-dimensional (3D) reaction-diffusion formulation in which aerosol deposition is represented by local removal at surfaces through a Robin boundary condition. We compare the original VIRIS framework with the extended model (VIRIS-3D-L) across three indoor spaces of increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home and a supermarket. Across all three settings, the original 2D formulation with global removal predicts lower infection risks than the 3D formulation with local deposition, with differences of up to 50%. The predictions of VIRIS-3D-L also show encouraging agreement with observations from a documented courtroom outbreak previously used to validate VIRIS. Although computation time increases by approximately a factor of four on average, simulations remain feasible on a standard laptop, taking between 7 minutes and just over two hours. These findings suggest that VIRIS-3D-L offers a more physically realistic framework for assessing indoor airborne infection risk without prohibitive computational costs, while the original VIRIS remains useful when rapid simulations are required.

papers.title: Coarse Embeddings Beyond Doubling: Persistence Diagrams and Multiparameter Modules
papers.abstract: We study coarse embeddings into Hilbert space and the asymptotic dimension of spaces of persistence diagrams and multiparameter persistence modules. We build coarse embeddings from admissible tent covers of bounded multiplicity at every scale, which doubling spaces carry but which do not require doubling: stacking them across dyadic scales gives an explicit $1$-Lipschitz coarse embedding, with lower gauge $c\sqrt{τt}$, or nearly linear for slowly decaying weights, and the same covers bound the asymptotic dimension by the multiplicity. The spaces of persistence diagrams are not doubling but carry such covers, and for diagrams with at most $n$ points our covers improve the constant of the known landmark embedding by a factor exponential in $n$. Slice by slice, the construction embeds multiparameter modules with boundedly many bars per slice under the matching distance on any finite net of slices, a class that contains the modules with at most $n$ generators. Under the continuous distances, bounding bars or persistent Betti numbers does not suffice: two-parameter modules with one bar on every slice have infinite asymptotic dimension, and neither they nor the modules of bounded support and bounded rank admit a coarse embedding into Hilbert space, under the matching or the interleaving distance.

papers.title: Samyama-SDG: A Declarative GraphQL @count and Regex/Ontology Synthetic Data Compiler with $O(1)$-Memory Referential Integrity and Causal Ground Truth
papers.abstract: Synthetic data generators face a divide between declarative relational mockets and domain causal simulators. Declarative generators specify entities, regexes, and foreign keys via schemas, but buffer parent primary-key pools in RAM ($O(N)$ memory) and lack ontology bindings or causal ground truth. Conversely, domain simulators emit realistic streams and ground-truth labels, but require thousands of lines of procedural code per domain. We present Samyama-SDG (sdg-rs), a Rust synthetic data compiler unifying declarative schema compilation with ontology-bound causal simulation. At Layer 1, Samyama-SDG compiles Cardinality-Extended GraphQL schemas (@count, @pk, @ontology, @regex, @dist, @fk, @after) and an Attribute Data Dictionary into a topologically sorted DAG. Combining stateless counter-based seekable PRNGs (SplitMix64 over $(\text{seed}, \text{entity}, \text{row}, \text{field})$) with index-bijective primary keys $f_{\text{PK}}(s, E, i)$ lets child tables resolve uniform or Zipfian foreign keys and multi-hop @after constraints in $O(1)$ memory without buffering parent tables. At Layer 2, causal processes layer fault propagation and machine-scorable ground truth (ground_truth.jsonl) over the same seekable PRNG and samyama-ontologies binder. Across three schemas, Samyama-SDG generates $1{,}000{,}000$ records in $128.79\text{ ms}$--$172.43\text{ ms}$ ($5.80\text{M}$--$7.76\text{M}$ rows/s) and $5{,}000{,}000$ records in $676.12\text{ ms}$--$808.56\text{ ms}$ at flat $31.4\text{ MiB}$--$35.1\text{ MiB}$ memory, with $0$ conformance errors across $1{,}150{,}000$ foreign keys and $900{,}000$ temporal constraints.

papers.title: Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope
papers.abstract: Artificial spin arrays assembled on surfaces enable atomic-scale studies of quantum correlations. Here we establish a hierarchy of connections between spin inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) and entanglement in spin-$1/2$ systems. We first show that the number of spectroscopically active transitions in a spin-$1/2$ dimer serves as an entanglement witness. Using the leading-order tunneling conductance for the tip placed on spin $i$, $dI(i)/dV$, we then relate spectral moments $\mathcal{M}^{(n)}(i)=\int V^n(d^2I(i)/dV^2)\,dV$ to quantum correlations. The zeroth moment probes the one-tangle in systems with a gapped, nondegenerate ground state. For rotationally invariant Heisenberg systems, the first moment yields thermal spin correlators $\langle\boldsymbol S(i)\cdot\boldsymbol S(j)\rangle$, enabling reconstruction of nearest-neighbor concurrence and spatial imaging of entanglement in spin chains. It also provides access to the internal energy and magnetic specific heat, both usable as entanglement witnesses. Applying this approach to experimental IETS data from nanographene spin chains, we find good agreement with theory. We further discuss how the second moment probes longer-range correlations and the inverse moment relates to local spin susceptibility. For spin-$1/2$ trimers, we connect inter-multiplet inelastic spectral weight to genuine tripartite entanglement quantified by the concurrence fill. Finally, we reconcile the local character of IETS with its sensitivity to nonlocal entanglement through an analogy with digital quantum circuits, where Hamiltonian evolution implements multiqubit operations. These results establish IETS as a tool for quantifying and imaging entanglement in engineered on-surface spin systems.

papers.title: Costate-Conditioned Dynamic Programming for Parallel-in-Time Solution of Equality-Constrained Optimal Control Problems
papers.abstract: Gradient based trajectory optimisation algorithms spend most of their per-iteration time on a structured Newton--KKT system. The system corresponds to an equality-constrained linear-quadratic optimal control problem and dedicated Riccati-type solvers exhibit linear complexity in the horizon length. Parallel-in-time algorithms exhibit the potential to reduce the complexity to logarithmic in the horizon by distributing several subtrajectories over multiple cores and then stitch together the results by means of an associative scan. Existing exact formulations condition each subtrajectory on its terminal state. Each subproblem then carries the reachability to that terminal state explicitly as constraint rows. The associated reachability decision however is ill-conditioned for weakly actuated systems. In this work we condition each subtrajectory on the terminal costate instead. The resulting subproblems can now be computed by a free-end Riccati recursion without reachability carrying rows. This approach effectively compensates for the ill-conditioning of weakly actuated systems but requires additional bookkeeping with Lagrangian multipliers when stitching together the various subproblems. Numerically the method reproduces a direct solution of the primal-dual Newton-KKT system to $10^{-12}$ in relative terms, on a weakly controllable chain of masses. The accurracy rivals that of a sequential recursion, whereas terminal-state conditioning loses up to six digits or fails. Operation counts on a problem with 64 subtrajectories and a horizon of 4096 stages gives a speed-up of 26 compared with a sequential solve.

papers.title: Evaluating Anterior Cruciate Ligament Risk of Injury Using a Graph Convolutional Autoencoder
papers.abstract: Current solutions for assessing the risk of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury typically rely on expensive motion-capture labs that require substantial resource investment or subjective evaluations of specific athletic stress tests by experts. The Drop Vertical Jump (DVJ) and the Single Leg Hop (SLH) are two examples of such tests typically used to track progress in ACL rehabilitation. In this paper, we develop an unsupervised learning model that runs entirely on a smartphone for two tasks, based on an autoencoder architecture with multiple layers of graph convolutional networks, which utilizes pose estimation data to determine a person's injury risk status. Our model accurately predicts athletes at high risk of injury for both athletic stress tests, with average sensitivities and specificities of 78% and 78% for the DVJ, and 75% and 74% for the SLH. Our findings support the development of a widely accessible smartphone solution for real-time screening of ACL injury risk.

papers.title: Fundamental Noise Processes in Pulsar Timing
papers.abstract: The stability of spin rates and emission regions of radio-emitting neutron stars (pulsars) has enabled remarkable advances, including the detection of exoplanets, testing theories of gravity, and stimulating the vigorous exploration of a new window in gravitational wave astronomy an nanohertz frequencies. An ideal astrophysical clock would emit identical pulses at a constant rate, propagating along single geodesics through a perfect vacuum. In reality, the timing precision achievable with pulsars is limited by spin noise, variability in the beam produced in a complex magnetosphere, and multipath propagation through a turbulent interstellar medium, with additional limitations from uncertainties in the changing pulsar -- observatory vector and instrumental effects. Here we present the fundamentals of pulsar timing, its current limitations, and prospects for improvements in timing precision. We develop metrics to assess the timing quality of a pulsar and use them to evaluate sources currently included in pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) as a means for characterizing the quality of future pulsar discoveries. With increases in telescope sensitivity, pulsar timing precision will increasingly be limited by propagation effects in the interstellar medium. We identify sources of non-Gaussianity in timing residuals and separate out effects that are chromatic or achromatic, as well as effects that vary on short (seconds to minutes) and longer (days to months) timescales. Modern wide-bandwidth receivers provide simultaneous arrival times across a range of frequencies, enabling the robust mitigation of chromatic interstellar effects and the identification of non-Gaussian events superimposed on random fluctuations. We recommend changes to timing procedures that leverage instrumentation advances to improve timing precision.

papers.title: Supercuspidal, discrete, and elliptic densities for reductive groups over non-archimedean local fields
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be the group of points of a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of arbitrary characteristic, with residue field of size $q$. For a principal congruence tower $K_n$ attached to a Lie algebra lattice $\mathcal{L}$, the supercuspidal and discrete series proportions of the Plancherel mass of the $K_n$-fixed vectors both converge, with error $O(q^{-n/4})$, to the probability that a Haar-random form in the dual lattice $Λ=\mathcal{L}^\vee$ is elliptic. For $\mathrm{GL}_d$, the supercuspidal limit confirms a prediction of Howe. This probability is positive, and we characterize when it is one. More generally, outside a union of congruence cells of total mass $O(q^{-n/4})$, each cell determines a common Levi class for the supercuspidal and discrete series supports of every tempered representation containing its character. The limiting mass of each class is the probability that a Haar-random form in $Λ$ lies in the corresponding stratum. The proof combines finite Fourier analysis, quantitative estimates for parabolic incidence maps, and a Jacquet-module argument that detects unitary exponents.

papers.title: Coherent radio emission at 45 MHz from the nearby planet-hosting star GJ 725A
papers.abstract: Ultra-low-frequency (<100 MHz) coherent radio emission from exoplanet-hosting stellar systems carries information about planetary and stellar magnetic fields, as well as the space weather environment - information that is difficult to obtain at other wavelengths. We carried out the circularly polarized LOFAR LBA Sky Survey, the most sensitive circularly polarized survey in this frequency range, using the LOFAR low-band antenna system. As part of this untargeted search, we detected a signal in a 1h observation that is coincident with the quiescent, planet-hosting, solar-neighborhood M dwarf GJ 725A at a distance of 3.5 pc. The signal has a high circular polarization fraction of $74\pm16$% and a peak brightness of $B=135\pm17$ mJy/beam between 42 MHz and 50 MHz. It was undetected in the 50-66 MHz range, with a 3$σ$ upper limit of $B<48$ mJy/beam, corresponding to a drop of at least a factor 3 across 12 MHz, and indicating a strong spectral feature or cutoff around 50 MHz. Our detection represents the lowest-frequency confirmed detection of a stellar system. Based on the high estimated brightness temperature ($\sim10^{14}$ K), transient character and polarization fraction, the emission is most plausibly attributed to the electron cyclotron maser instability. The available observations are not sufficient to identify the astrophysical origin of the emission. We consider three plausible scenarios: auroral emission of a yet undetected wide-orbit giant planet with a magnetic field $B\geq18$ G, star-planet interaction with the known 11 d orbit terrestrial planet GJ 725Ab, or an origin due to stellar magnetic activity. Ultra-low-frequency monitoring, combined with new, preferably simultaneous observations in the X-rays, UV, and H$α$, and a search for a wide-orbit (thousands of days) giant planet across the full allowed parameter space will allow us to distinguish between these scenarios.

papers.title: SoK: Assessing Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption in Software Development: Standards, Lifecycle Coverage, Deployment Maturity, and Evidence of Readiness
papers.abstract: Standardised post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is critical for protecting software systems against future quantum threats, but standardised algorithms alone do not provide a pathway for their secure integration into software. This paper presents a Systematisation of Knowledge (SoK) of PQC integration in software development, synthesising existing approaches across implementation, migration, and developer education. We analyse these approaches against NIST PQC standards and PQC migration guidance, software development lifecycle coverage, cybersecurity practices, deployment maturity, and testing and evaluation evidence. Our analysis shows that existing work establishes important technical and organisational foundations but provides disconnected support across the software development lifecycle, with limited coordination between preparation, implementation, migration, deployment, maintenance, and developer practices. Evaluation evidence also remains concentrated in controlled or early-stage settings, providing stronger evidence of technical feasibility than operational readiness. We identify cross-cutting gaps and research directions for developing lifecycle-oriented, empirically validated approaches that connect technical, developer, and organisational requirements for secure PQC integration.

papers.title: Efficiently Estimating Cycle Statistics on Graphs via Spanning Trees
papers.abstract: Simple cycles encode feedback and alternative routes in networks and are important for routing problems, the convergence of dynamical processes on networks, message passing and belief propagation, or even static network characterizations such as structural balance in signed networks. Being able to assess and sample from the cycle structure of a graph is thus of interest in many analysis contexts. However, due to the combinatorial growth of the cycle space with graph size, the computational cost for such sampling is high. Therefore, we here introduce a sampling framework that enables us to sample from the cycle structure without enumerating all cycles. Specifically, the method draws uniform spanning trees and collects the fundamental cycles created by their non-tree edges, such that each tree provides an informative subset of simple cycles. Because cycles are included with unequal probabilities and are dependent within each subset, we formulate an inclusion-probability-based Horvitz-Thompson estimator, which we average over random subsets, a procedure we call Monte Carlo Horvitz-Thompson. For this, we sample multiple Horvitz-Thompson estimators and introduce a method to further subsample the individual estimators for increased computational performance. For sampling cycles, the estimator is unbiased if exact cycle inclusion probabilities are known. To extend the method to larger networks, we derive an efficient mean-field approximation for the inclusion probabilities and characterize the graph regimes in which it remains accurate. Experiments on synthetic and real-world networks demonstrate the computational scaling and statistical performance of the framework. We then illustrate the utility of Monte Carlo Horvitz-Thompson estimation by estimating cycle counts and cycle-level frustration statistics in signed spin systems. An implementation is available in the py-raccoon package.

papers.title: Neyman Orthogonalized Specification Tests for Conditional Tail Index Models
papers.abstract: We develop specification tests for parametric conditional tail index models of heavy-tailed distributions. The tests are based on a projected empirical process that removes the first-order effect of estimating the null parameter. Within the conditional Hall class, we identify conditions under which projection also eliminates the leading Pareto approximation bias in the test process, permitting lower thresholds while preserving asymptotically correct size. We establish the validity of the tests via multiplier bootstrap and characterize power against fixed and local alternatives. For log-linear models, bootstrap validity extends to settings in which covariates of observations above a common threshold concentrate and the smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix tends to zero. We further propose a novel threshold selection rule based on an estimate of the Pareto approximation bias after projection. The rule uses the estimated bias to determine whether a reference threshold can be lowered to retain more observations, with potential gains in power. The finite sample performance of the tests is examined through simulations and a real data application.

papers.title: PINR-ESI: Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Implicit Neural Representation Framework for EEG Extended-Source Imaging
papers.abstract: EEG extended-source imaging aims to localize active cortical regions and characterize their extent, yet supervised inverse networks typically depend on synthetic EEG-source pairs and may be sensitive to synthetic-to-real mismatch. We propose a physics-informed self-supervised implicit neural representation (INR) framework for spatial source reconstruction without paired source labels or simulation-based supervised pretraining. The lead-field matrix encodes the source-to-sensor volume-conduction model and constrains the INR through agreement between predicted and measured EEG. Cortical current density is represented as a continuous coordinate-based neural field. Forward EEG prediction samples the field at cortical vertices and applies local smoothing before lead-field mapping. A classical inverse estimate provides warm initialization and observation-specific spatial guidance through prior-guided support regularization. Simulations across varying SNRs, source extents, and source counts showed low spatial dispersion and good localization performance. Quantitative evaluation on clinical EEG recordings from epilepsy patients and qualitative analysis of scalp EEG during intracranial stimulation supported feasibility for real-world source imaging. These findings suggest the potential of physics-informed self-supervised INR for extended-source imaging.

papers.title: Construction of entropies for cross-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: The analysis of cross-diffusion systems with nonsymmetric and indefinite diffusion matrices often relies on the existence of entropies, that is, Lyapunov functionals whose dissipation often yields gradient estimates. We propose a general strategy for constructing entropies for two-species cross-diffusion systems, based on the assumption that the mobility matrix is symmetric, in accordance with Onsager's reciprocal relations. The symmetry condition leads to a linear hyperbolic equation in two variables, which can be reformulated as a linear transport system along the eigendirections of the diffusion matrix, related to the approach of Jenssen and Kogan for hyperbolic conservation laws. Positive solutions to this system yield a family of entropies parametrized by two arbitrary functions of one variable. Sufficient conditions for their existence on (possibly unbounded) characteristic rectangles are given, the mechanisms that may prevent the existence of an entropy are identified, and systems without any entropy structure are presented. The general construction recovers known entropies for models arising in physics and biology and provides new ones. For systems with an arbitrary number of components, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of separable entropies and give a rank criterion for the uniqueness of entropies (up to affine functions). Cross-diffusion systems without symmetry of the mobility matrix are also discussed.

papers.title: NaijaFacts: A Framework for Disentangling Language from Knowledge in Facts about Nigeria
papers.abstract: Multilingual benchmarks for African languages mostly translate generic questions into local languages, measuring linguistic competence but not whether models know facts about Africa. We introduce NaijaFacts, a benchmark of factual and statistical questions about Nigeria, authored by native speakers and grounded in authoritative official statistics, with every question available in English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yorùbá, Igbo, and Hausa. Answering similar questions for the UK and US yields a country by language matrix that disentangles a language effect (the model knows the fact but degrades in a low-resource language) from a knowledge effect (the fact is absent in every language). Across eight frontier and Nigeria-adapted models, the knowledge effect dominates: English-query accuracy is 49-50% for the US/UK but 20% for Nigeria. The language effect is smaller and tracks web representation, degrading from English to Yorùbá (9 points on Nigeria, up to 24 on US/UK questions). We find scale does not help: the strongest models reach 66-79% on the UK and the US but none exceed 31% on Nigerian statistics. Extending to all 54 African countries with our best performing frontier model shows the same profile continent-wide, 96% on culture and 98% on politics against 26% on statistics, so the gap is not specific to Nigeria.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage needs Multiple Perspectives
papers.abstract: The origin of the quantum speedup is a topic of ongoing research. We propose a logical criterion for the possibility of a speedup within the continuous-variable and odd-prime qudit settings. There, Wigner function nonnegativity signals the possibility of efficient classical simulation in the state-injection scenario. We consider representations of quadrature/Weyl measurements in a single von Neumann algebra that reproduce the Born statistics in a particular state. If in that state, the set-theoretic universe of the algebra is ZFC-satisfiable, i.e. every ZFC-theorem holds with unit probability, all measurement contexts can be represented in a single commutative algebra of `beables'. Furthermore, the statistics admit a noncontextual hidden variable model, ensuring Wigner nonnegativity for two or more modes or qudits. For a single mode, a stronger notion of linear representation ensures commutativity, and with it, ZFC-satisfiability independently of the state, as well as Wigner nonnegativity. In consequence, in any setting that cannot be efficiently simulated, it must be impossible to merge the models associated with every context into a single ZFC-satisfiable one: quantum advantage needs multiple perspectives.

papers.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
papers.abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.

papers.title: Function-Preserving Audits of Visual Weight Readers
papers.abstract: A neural field can encode the same image with different weights. A reader that recognizes one such representation may therefore rely on parameter coordinates rather than the visual function. We study this distinction through function-preserving transformations, measuring recognition, prediction disagreement, and numerical fidelity together. Across shape, digit, and natural-image fields, high accuracy on the original weights coexists with substantial sensitivity to equivalent representations. On 10,000 official CIFAR10 test origins, one-period hidden-bias shifts change 7.3% of a released HiddenProbe configuration's predictions while barely changing accuracy; three-period shifts change 22.0% and reduce accuracy from 57.8% to 54.4%. Output-only ProbeGen remains unchanged. These effects are smaller than in a separate adapted-reader study, where matched phase and sign controls remove the corresponding sensitivities. Controlled readout studies show why invariance is insufficient: complete canonical hidden features reach 38.7% on MNIST, whereas explicitly composing those activations, outgoing weights, and output bias into field outputs reaches 81.5%. The information is present, but the learned readout does not recover it as effectively. A separate 720-response study of language models reading numerical weights shows why stochastic audits require repeats on both inputs: observed accuracy losses need not yield rejection of response-law equality. Together, these results distinguish invariance, useful visual information, and the evidence required to evaluate stochastic readers.

papers.title: TAQ-MOTR: Tracking-Aware Detection Query Formation for End-to-End Multiple Object Tracking
papers.abstract: Tracking-by-propagation (TBP) methods perform end-to-end multi-object tracking by propagating track queries across frames, jointly handling detection and identity association without heuristic post-processing while naturally modeling temporal information. However, as detection and association are tightly coupled, detection queries in TBP are expected to discover currently untracked objects and provide complementary current-frame evidence for challenging tracks whose queries and identities are retained. Existing methods largely inherit detection-query formation from single-frame detection and construct such queries before the decoder with little awareness of trajectory states. Consequently, currently untracked objects may be missed, while challenging tracked objects with reduced visibility under occlusion may lack complementary evidence, causing association failures or duplicate responses. To address these issues, we propose TAQ-MOTR, a tracking-aware detection query formation framework that employs a pre-decoder Hybrid Query Generator (HQG) to fuse current-frame image features, track memory, and learnable memory. By conditioning detection queries on trajectory states, TAQ-MOTR adapts them to \rev{the discovery of currently untracked objects and tracked-object complementation We further introduce a training-only auxiliary detection branch whose one-to-one label assignment is decoupled from that of the main tracking branch, providing additional detection supervision to strengthen the shared HQG and decoder for the discovery of currently untracked objects. TAQ-MOTR improves performance on DanceTrack, SportsMOT, and BFT, achieving 72.0 HOTA, 63.1 AssA, and 76.6 IDF1 on the DanceTrack test set. Code is available at https://github.com/Magicmiya/TAQ-MOTR

papers.title: Mamba3R: Fixed-Capacity Selective State Memory for Long-Sequence 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Streaming 3D reconstruction must maintain geometric quality over long inputs within a fixed GPU budget. A pretrained recurrent model provides bounded state, but freezing its backbone also fixes its learned state-observation interactions. We introduce Mamba3R, a jointly designed state-memory adapter that provides a trainable adaptation path without updating the backbone or task heads. A selective state-space mixer jointly transforms native state features and a fixed-capacity auxiliary memory, explicit read and write paths carry information across frames, and a decomposed feedback path regulates what the added memory feeds back. Only 1.28 million adapter parameters are trained. Under a shared periodic-reset protocol, it lowers trajectory error and improves accumulated surface and depth accuracy over recurrent baselines on public indoor and outdoor datasets and robot-recorded traversals, gaining up to 40 percent on one metric. Matched comparisons support both the choice of the mixing operator and the utility of carrying the auxiliary memory across frames. Allocated memory remains unchanged and throughput moves by at most 1.4 percent from one to two thousand frames. Replaying its recorded traversals offline, the platform's RTX 4060 averages 11.7 frames per second within 5.1 GiB with the same checkpoint, a mean throughput covering the 10 Hz sensor rate.
