The general validity of this relation is guaranteed by the natural contribution of a susceptibility term, which is experimentally accessible by tuning the system-reservoir coupling strength. We show how the partial dynamical activity encompasses previous definitions of activity in the weak-coupling Markovian limit and that it provides an information-geometric interpretation of correlator-based activities. We illustrate the tight constraint on precision that our bound provides with the example of the dynamics of a strongly interacting finite-size system and of steady-state coherent transport through a double quantum dot, where quantum effects invalidate previously developed kinetic uncertainty relations. We expect our bound to provide a powerful tool for optimizing precision in arbitrary quantum systems.

papers.title: QVal: Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly act over long horizons, where outcome-only rewards say little about which intermediate actions were good. Dense supervision methods address this by scoring intermediate steps, but they are usually evaluated through the downstream performance of a full training pipeline. This is expensive, confounds signal quality with other training choices, and means that methods are rarely compared on common ground. We introduce QVal, a training-free testbed that measures the $Q$-alignment of a dense signal: whether it orders the candidate actions in each state the same way as their returns under a reference policy do. We benchmark 21 methods from seven families with six open-weight backbones in four environments. Simple prompting baselines are the most $Q$-aligned on average, and performance clusters strongly by family. Code-generated signals do well only in small state and action spaces; embedding-based signals are weak; self-distillation signals are anti-aligned; and no method is $Q$-aligned in open-ended environments. When five of these signals guide an actor at test time by choosing among four proposed actions, $Q$-alignment strongly correlates with the gain in task success. QVal is designed to be easily extensible to new environments and methods, enabling researchers to compare new signals cheaply before committing to a training run.

papers.title: A Quantum-Classical Surrogate Model for the Collision Operator of the Lattice Boltzmann Method
papers.abstract: We introduce a hybrid approach utilising a quantum machine learning surrogate model to approximate the non-linear collision dynamics of the LBM. It offloads the non-unitary operations that challenge pure quantum solvers. The surrogate's expressivity relies on variational quantum circuits that implement partial Fourier series, while data re-uploading extends the representable frequency spectrum. Unlike previous approaches that use a fixed relaxation parameter, the relaxation step is embedded analytically in the circuit, allowing the learned equilibrium to be used for any relaxation parameter without retraining. We reassess standard VQC metrics, including expressibility, entanglement, and effective dimension, by relating them directly to task-specific surrogate performance and identifying the architectural parameters that determine approximation accuracy. The proposed surrogate is validated against the classical BGK collision operator using benchmark problems, including the Taylor-Green vortex for energy dissipation and the double shear layer for shear-driven instabilities and nonlinear flow evolution. Our results show that the surrogate closely reproduces the BGK reference on both benchmarks, using a single set of trained circuits across all relaxation parameters. These findings suggest that hybrid quantum-classical strategies offer a practical path toward realising the potential of quantum computing in fluid engineering.

papers.title: An annihilation-number Caro-Wei bound: a TxGraffiti conjecture and an independence-number bracket
papers.abstract: Computable independence bounds give intervals that can be compared by containment or by their worst-case endpoint ratios. For positive maximum degree $Δ$, the Caro-Wei sum $W$ bounds the independence number from below, while $(Δ+1)W/2$ bounds it from above. A second interval has the Havel-Hakimi residue as its lower endpoint and the annihilation number as its upper endpoint. This note proves that the annihilation number does not exceed the Caro-Wei upper endpoint. This upper bound is sharp, with equality for regular graphs of positive degree and even order. Since the residue is at least $W$, this upper bound places the residue-annihilation interval inside the Caro-Wei interval. Both endpoints can improve strictly on one graph, although the sharp worst-case endpoint ratio remains unchanged, even for connected graphs. The annihilation-number bound also proves a conjectured lower estimate based on the annihilation number and residue for every connected graph with at least three vertices. Equality in this estimate holds for exactly eight graph types, while the single edge violates it. For maximum degree at least three, however, the estimate never exceeds the residue, even without connectedness.

papers.title: The inclination cross-check: binary-pulsar timing and gravitational-wave polarimetry
papers.abstract: Radio timing and gravitational-wave (GW) polarimetry provide independent measurements of a binary's inclination. We study their consistency through $\eps=s_{\rm Shapiro}-s_{\rm GW}$, where $s_{\rm Shapiro}$ is the Shapiro-delay shape and $s_{\rm GW}$ is inferred from the tensor polarization amplitudes. We combine a time-dependent, finite-arm detector response with radio timing averaged over each integration, retaining the amplitude--inclination covariance and the nonlinear orientation posteriors. For hypothetical 15-minute binaries at 5 kpc and $65^\circ$ inclination, four years of GW data and a 125-h radio campaign give $σ_\eps=5.4\times10^{-3}$ for a double neutron star and $1.0\times10^{-3}$ for a pulsar--black-hole binary when two static timing harmonics are fitted. An apsidally evolving radio model with $e=0.01$ and a free apsidal rate gives $4.5\times10^{-3}$ and $0.94\times10^{-3}$, respectively, with the circular GW covariance held fixed. Changes in the relative tensor amplitudes can be absorbed by the GW fit as an apparent inclination shift and revealed by the radio measurement. An inaccurate detector response can produce a similar discrepancy even when its Fisher errors are nearly unchanged. These forecasts use the $n=2$ GW harmonic and assume a fixed orbital plane, sustained radio visibility, and the specified timing precision; additional harmonics can provide further orientation information.

papers.title: CoffeeBench: Benchmarking Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Economies
papers.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly capable of handling complex, long-horizon tasks and may eventually take on business management, a role traditionally performed by humans. Deploying them safely requires monitoring their capabilities and behavior in environments that reflect real economies. We introduce CoffeeBench, a benchmark built on a compact simulation of a coffee supply chain with realistic business mechanics. Six autonomous LLM coding agents run its farmers, roasters, and retailers, and negotiate and trade with one another to maximize their own net income over 90 simulated days. We evaluate eight recent proprietary and open-weight models by letting each run one roaster while a fixed background model runs the other five firms, and scoring that roaster's net income. Claude Sonnet 5.5 earns the highest net income, closely followed by GPT-6 Astra. The leaders sell at higher prices, and the best model also buys its inputs far more cheaply, whereas weaker models trade at thin margins. Since performance targets are a common cause of accounting fraud in human firms, we also test whether agents under KPI pressure inflate their numbers. Under a revenue target, circular trades occur for some pairs of models: one agent proposes that the two rival firms sell goods back and forth at inflated prices so that both book revenue, and the rival accepts. We hope CoffeeBench serves as an early step toward a future in which LLM agents manage firms without misconduct. We release our code and agent trajectories.

papers.title: Quantum optimal control of steady orbits
papers.abstract: Periodically driven dissipative systems can settle into steady orbits - fixed infinite loops on their dynamical manifolds. In quantum mechanics, steady orbits occur in cooling engines, lasers and masers, precision metrology devices, and magnetic resonance. Steady orbits and stroboscopic steady states are a promising target for quantum optimal control, but the numerical complexity is prohibitive: infinite loops defeat state-of-the-art algorithms that use explicit numerical propagation in the time domain. We report a solution to this problem and introduce a numerically efficient quantum optimal control algorithm for steady orbits. We use this algorithm to design microwave pulse sequences that dynamically polarise nuclear spins and enhance their magnetic resonance signals, while taking into account instrumental distortions. Improved performance relative to leading current methods is demonstrated experimentally.

papers.title: SmoQyElPhQMC.jl: An open-source Julia package for efficient and scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled models
papers.abstract: We introduce version 1.0 of the SmoQyElPhQMC.jl package, an open-source Julia code for performing scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled model Hamiltonians. SmoQyElPhQMC.jl is built upon the SmoQyDQMC.jl codebase and implements improved versions of the algorithms presented in [B. Cohen-Stead \textit{et al}., Phys. Rev. E 105, 065302 (2022)] to enable (near-linear) scalable simulations of a broad class of uncorrelated $e$-ph models both in system size and inverse temperature. By extending the functionality of the flexible scripting interface introduced in SmoQyDQMC.jl, the SmoQyElPhQMC.jl package continues to allow users to adapt it to different workflows and interface with other software packages in the Julia ecosystem. The code for this package can be downloaded from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/SmoQySuite/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl or installed using the Julia package manager. The online documentation, including examples, can be obtained from our documentation page at https://smoqysuite.github.io/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl/stable/.

papers.title: Express Language Modeling
papers.abstract: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.

papers.title: Generative Molecular Morphing for Flexible-Size Design via Unbalanced Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: The success of generative molecular design depends on a model's steerability toward high-reward samples. Because many molecular properties are intrinsically linked to molecular size, accurately capturing the joint distribution of properties and the number of atoms is essential. However, current diffusion and flow-based models fix the number of atoms, which ultimately limits their ability to navigate this complex relationship. To address this, we introduce Morph, a flexible-size generative model for conditional and unconditional 3D molecular design based on geometric graphs. By dynamically adapting size, Morph can seamlessly integrate existing structural priors, like scaffolds, and significantly enhances property steering. We show that Morph matches current fixed-size state-of-the-art models while significantly increasing sampling flexibility. We demonstrate out-of-distribution generation in regimes where previous models fail, paving the way for enhanced generative modeling for molecular design.

papers.title: Evidence-Guided Neural Architecture Selection under Uncertainty for Subject-Specific Blood Glucose Forecasting
papers.abstract: Reliable neural architecture selection is an open challenge in time-series forecasting under limited, noisy, and heterogeneous data, where standard heuristic architecture design and validation approaches fail to ensure accurate and reliable prediction and generalization. We propose EVIDENT (EVidence-based IDEntification of Neural archiTectures), a framework for architecture selection that integrates Bayesian training, evidence-based ranking, and task-specific validation under uncertainty. The framework explores the candidate architecture pool and identifies the lowest-capacity model that satisfies a prescribed validation criterion. We demonstrate this method using temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) for individualized blood glucose forecasting in type 1 diabetes patients. The results show that EVIDENT systematically rejects both under- and over-parameterized TCN architectures on population-level diabetes data, while identifying models that generalize reliably to unseen patients. When multiple architectures are competitive, the framework further supports plausibility-weighted ensemble predictions that enhance predictive performance. Compared with a random-search baseline, EVIDENT identified smaller architectures with more consistent forecasting performance on unseen patients. These findings establish EVIDENT as a strategy to neural architecture discovery, enabling reliable model selection for high-consequence forecasting in data-limited and heterogeneous settings.

papers.title: Underdetermination in the Quantum-Mechanical Bootstrap with Mixed Functional Operators
papers.abstract: The bootstrap method for quantum mechanics is a powerful tool for computing the energy eigenvalues of a Hamiltonian. However, we point out that a conventional implementation employing the standard bootstrap matrix may be insufficient when the potential contains different types of functions, such as polynomial and exponential terms. In such cases, the standard constraints may not fully capture the relations between the corresponding operator sectors, and the method may fail to reproduce the correct spectrum. A similar problem may arise when evaluating expectation values of operators of different types. This issue can occur in a wide range of systems, including statistical models and matrix models. We propose three possible resolutions to this problem.

papers.title: Non-monotone clustering and energetic regime switching in aggregation-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: We investigate transient clustering dynamics in nonlocal aggregation-diffusion systems from an energetic perspective. Starting from a stochastic interacting particle system, we study the associated macroscopic McKean-Vlasov equation on the torus and use its Wasserstein gradient-flow structure to analyse the competition between interaction-driven aggregation and entropy-driven diffusion. Through numerical experiments for locally attractive interaction kernels, we observe non-monotone clustering behaviour in intuitive geometric observables: in particular, the density peak height may first increase and subsequently decrease along trajectories converging to equilibrium. Using the decomposition of the free energy as a diagnostic, we identify alternating aggregation- and diffusion-dominated regimes underlying these transient dynamics. We investigate to what extent transitions between these regimes are related to the evolution of geometric observables, such as the peak height. Our results illustrate how non-monotone transient clustering can arise even in a dissipative gradient-flow system and highlight the complementary information provided by geometric clustering observables and the free-energy-based regime classification.

papers.title: Perturbative Nicolai-Map Diagrammatics: Application to Poincaré Supergravity
papers.abstract: We develop a perturbative, diagrammatic framework for constructing Nicolai maps and apply it to four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ Poincaré supergravity expanded around flat Minkowski space. It provides an alternative to the coupling-flow-operator construction, which faces several obstructions when extended to local supersymmetry. Expanding the bosonic effective action and the Nicolai map jointly in the gravitational coupling $κ$ and the loop-counting parameter $\hbar$, we derive the Nicolai-map defining conditions, i.e. the free-action and determinant-matching conditions, order by order. The diagrammatics enumerates all admissible local terms in the Nicolai-map ansatz from the effective-action diagrams and reduces the construction to a finite system of nonlinear polynomial equations. Carried through order $κ^{2}$, the resulting constraints are found to be independent of the detailed bosonic input and hierarchical, order-$κ^{2}$ consistency further restricting the order-$κ$ data. A consistent Nicolai-map construction for the Einstein--Hilbert graviton sector is found to require the Rarita--Schwinger gravitino already at this order: Einstein gravity admits a Nicolai map only through its $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric completion, Poincaré supergravity, supporting Nicolai's characterization of supersymmetry.

papers.title: Symmetry-breaking and hysteretic transitions in an actively coupled optical trimer
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear dynamics of a non-Hermitian optical trimer consisting of three lossy waveguides with complex-valued coupling. Building on our previous analysis of its global dynamics, we adopt a site-resolved approach to elucidate the bifurcation structure and the organization of oscillatory states across the individual waveguides. We identify a hysteretic transition from reflection-asymmetric periodic states to periodic states exhibiting a combined reflection-translation symmetry. This transition involves a double-loop hysteretic regime characterized by the coexistence of multiple attractors. Analysis of the spatial intensity profiles and their Fourier spectra reveals distinct oscillatory behavior among the waveguides. In particular, in the regime with combined reflection-translation symmetry, the central waveguide exhibits a dominant spatial wavenumber approximately twice that of the edge waveguides. We further identify a third dynamical regime emerging through a pitchfork bifurcation of limit cycles, which breaks the combined reflection--translation relation and gives rise to two reflection-related periodic solutions. Despite this transition, the 2:1 relation between the dominant spatial wavenumbers of the central and edge waveguides persists. These results demonstrate how nonlinear interactions, complex coupling, and dissipation shape multistability, chaotic dynamics, bifurcations, and site-dependent oscillations in a minimal non-Hermitian photonic system.

papers.title: Certified Policy Optimisation for Nested Causal Bandits via PAC-Bayes Risk
papers.abstract: Critical sequential decisions are rarely single-timescale: a strategic decision causally shapes the context in which every subsequent tactical choice is made; standard bandit and reinforcement-learning theory does not capture this causal coupling between timescales. We formalise the problem class as Nested Contextual Causal Bandits (NCCBs), a hierarchical SCM where each level's action sets the next level's context distribution, and propose Nested Causal Thompson Sampling (NCTS), which draws one mechanism-factorised belief per episode and acts recursively under it. Our main theoretical result is a causal PAC-Bayesian excess-risk bound that certifies any candidate deployment policy from historic data alone, off-policy and anytime, answering the deployment question: can we trust this agent here, and at what risk? Experiments on a hierarchical SCM show that, against a matched RFF-GP joint regression on the same function class, the factorised SCM-mechanism posterior transfers significantly better zero-shot under exogenous distribution shifts, the recursive meta-to-inner commit significantly dominates the joint-commit alternative in distribution, and the certificate significantly contracts as offline data accumulates. Combining these results, we establish progressive certified handover, a safe-deployment method: each timescale flips from a legacy controller to NCTS when gains can be certified, independently of the others.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for kinetic shock waves: simultaneous accuracy of lower- and higher-order moments, with and without moment supervision
papers.abstract: We investigate physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for one-dimensional kinetic shock waves governed by the Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) and Shakhov collision models, with and without moment supervision. The trace-free third-order and the fourth-order moments enter the fluxes of stress and heat flux through a shock; the aim, to our knowledge not previously examined for kinetic PINNs, is simultaneous accuracy of these and the lower-order moments of one predicted distribution. Data-assisted calculations, including anchor and closure studies, combine kinetic residuals with moment observations. For the BGK shock tube, a positive eight-moment representation whose spatial envelope follows the far-field decay of the initial condition gives heat-flux, stress and higher-moment discrepancies of $0.33\%$, $0.67\%$ and $1.8$--$2.0\%$ against the 6400-cell discrete-velocity method (DVM) reference supplying its observations; a five-field representation leaves the latter uncontrolled. Equation-trained characteristic-integral PINNs use analytic initial and incoming-boundary distributions and their own predicted moments. Their BGK and Shakhov shock-tube heat-flux and stress discrepancies are $0.41\%$ and $0.36\%$ against 3200-cell references; against the 6400-cell reference the BGK values are $0.21\%$ and $0.18\%$, and $0.4$--$0.9\%$ for the higher moments. Stationary neural continuation covers Shakhov Mach 2--5 and BGK Mach 6--7. Characteristic correction reduces the Mach-7 heat-flux and stress discrepancies from $3.37\%$ and $1.34\%$ to $0.42\%$ and $0.43\%$; at Mach~8 they are $0.62\%$ and $0.79\%$, and at Mach~12, across references, $0.40$--$1.03\%$ and $0.41$--$2.65\%$. Three independent Mach-2 initialisations assess repeatability. It is established that lower moments do not determine higher ones; the contribution is to quantify which moments each information regime recovers.

papers.title: Hybrid neural denoising for resource-efficient near- and sub-threshold radio triggering of extensive air showers
papers.abstract: Autonomous radio self-triggering for extensive air showers requires strong rejection of radio-frequency interference while preserving weak pulses within station-level hardware constraints. We present a hybrid neural trigger comprising a compact waveform denoiser followed by a classifier. The method is evaluated using experimentally measured high-interference background traces and detector-folded simulated air-shower pulses produced with the Pierre Auger Offline chain, with the benchmark concentrated in the near-threshold regime. Hardware constraints are incorporated through hyperparameter optimisation, quantisation-aware training, and high-granularity fixed-point quantisation. Applying the conventional peak-envelope trigger after denoising increases its area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve from 0.63 to 0.98. At a false-positive rate of 10^-4, the full denoiser-classifier chain retains about 41% of the held-out signal traces, compared with 27% for the classifier acting on the raw waveform and about 2% for the peak-envelope reference. The fixed-point firmware is synthesised, placed, and routed on representative field-programmable gate array targets, where it achieves timing closure with microsecond-scale latency and compact arithmetic-resource usage. These results establish hybrid neural denoising as a practical FPGA-compatible route toward radio-only triggering of weak and inclined air-shower signals in noisy environments.

papers.title: Match classification in the last round of four-team round-robin tournaments
papers.abstract: Classification of matches played in the last rounds of sports competitions is a well-established tool for evaluating tournament designs. Our paper offers the first comparison of deterministic and probabilistic match classification models by analysing the most prominent example of four-team round-robin competitions, the group stage of the FIFA World Cup. We show that both models are highly relevant in practice: all (four) deterministic and (six) probabilistic match types occurred in the 2014 and 2018 FIFA World Cups, respectively. The probabilistic model, which accounts for the relative benefits of attacking and defending, provides a deeper insight; for instance, the competitive matches from the deterministic approach can be of any of the six probabilistic types. Therefore, the probabilistic model is used to decompose the impact of three reforms introduced in the 2026 FIFA World Cup: the expansion to 48 teams, the modified qualification rules, and head-to-head tie-breakers.

papers.title: DeltaBox: Millisecond-Scale Sandbox Checkpoint and Rollback for Stateful AI Agents
papers.abstract: Emerging LLM-powered AI agent workloads, such as test-time tree search and reinforcement learning (RL), require high-frequency state exploration, relying on rapid checkpoint/restore (C/R) of the complete sandbox state, including files and process state. Existing mechanisms duplicate the entire state, causing hundreds of milliseconds to seconds of latency per C/R, which severely bottlenecks deep search and large-scale fan-outs. We observe that consecutive sandbox states between checkpoints differ only marginally. Therefore, instead of full duplication, a sandbox should only duplicate the changes between consecutive checkpoints (Key Insight), yet the lack of OS support makes this hard to realize. We propose a new OS-level abstraction, DeltaState, that delivers change-based C/R for agents through co-designed OS mechanisms. First, DeltaFS checkpoints file state by freezing the writable layer and inserting a new one, turning updates into copy-on-write and rollback into a layer switch. Second, DeltaCR quickly restores process state by forking from a frozen template process. A coordinator pairs the two so each checkpoint is one consistent (filesystem, memory) state. Building on these mechanisms, we present DeltaBox, an agent sandbox with millisecond-level C/R. On SWE-bench, DeltaBox hides its checkpoint work (10.83 ms) under inference and rolls back in a mean 1.86 ms, with the same warm-template fork driving low-cost RL rollout fan-out. DeltaBox is open-sourced at https://github.com/delta-box.

papers.title: SpecHop: Continuous Speculation for Accelerating Multi-Hop Retrieval Agents
papers.abstract: Large language models increasingly use external tools such as web search and document retrieval to solve information-intensive tasks. However, multi-hop tool use in complex tasks introduces substantial latency, since the model must repeatedly wait for tool observations before continuing. We study how to accelerate such trajectories without changing the final trajectory the model would have taken without acceleration, assuming access to faster but less reliable speculator tools. We develop a theoretical framework for lossless speculation in multi-hop tool-use settings, characterizing the optimal achievable latency gain. We propose SpecHop, a continuous speculation framework that maintains multiple speculative threads, verifies predicted observations asynchronously as target tool outputs arrive, commits correct branches, and rolls back incorrect ones. This preserves accuracy while reducing wall-clock latency. We show that SpecHop can approach oracle latency gains with enough active threads. Empirically, on retrieval-augmented multi-hop tasks, SpecHop closely matches theoretical predictions and reduces latency by up to 40\% in some settings. Code: https://github.com/mehrdadsaberi/spechop

papers.title: Affine ANEC selects the closed FRW branch for geodesically complete cosmology
papers.abstract: Using the affinely parameterized averaged null energy condition (ANEC) along radial null geodesics, we prove that, within the globally nondegenerate Friedmann--Robertson--Walker (FRW) class with $a(t)>0$ for all cosmic times, non-static flat models and all open models cannot be both null geodesically complete and ANEC-satisfying. Bounded oscillatory or cyclic flat/open models obey the same obstruction; in non-static periodic cases the negative affine-ANEC contribution accumulates over infinitely many cycles, giving $I_{\rm ANEC}=-\infty$. The sign obstruction is absent in closed $(k=+1)$ FRW geometry, where positive curvature can offset the negative expansion contribution to the affine ANEC, allowing nonsingular, geodesically complete cosmologies with ordinary NEC-respecting matter. We construct closed-FRW scalar-field models and contrast them with their flat realizations, which require NEC-violating support. We show that neglecting small positive curvature in a flat reconstruction of the expansion history can produce an apparent phantom equation of state, with a percent-level shift at $z=1$. Our main result is a curvature classification of ANEC-compatible eternal FRW cosmologies within this class: non-static flat and all open models are obstructed, while the closed branch admits explicit complete realizations, with global de Sitter as the vacuum representative.

papers.title: Probing (sub-)solar-mass black holes and superspinars with current and next-generation gravitational-wave observatories
papers.abstract: We investigate the detectability and parameter estimation prospects of (sub-)solar-mass collapsed binaries with current and next-generation gravitational wave detectors, allowing the dimensionless component spins to extend phenomenologically beyond the Kerr bound, $(|χ|>1$) (where $χ$ is the spin parameter). Using the inspiral-only TaylorF2 waveform and a Fisher-matrix analysis, we study binaries with component masses in the range $0.1\!-\!2\,M_\odot$ and compare the performance of Advanced LIGO with that of a third-generation network consisting of Cosmic Explorer and the Einstein Telescope. We find that third-generation detectors substantially improve the signal-to-noise ratio and the measurement of intrinsic binary parameters, particularly the component spins, while also providing significantly improved sky localization. For favorable configurations, the primary spin can be measured with precision $Δχ_{1z}\sim10^{-3}-10^{-2}$, demonstrating enhanced sensitivity to potential Kerr-bound violations. However, strong anti-correlations between the component spins limit the interpretation of small marginalized spin uncertainties as definitive evidence for superspinars. We also examine formation scenarios for (sub-)solar-mass collapsed binaries and show that dense dark-matter environments, particularly the Galactic Centre, can significantly enhance their formation and merger rates. Our results demonstrate the potential of future gravitational wave observations to probe low-mass collapsed objects and possible departures from the Kerr bound, while highlighting the need for physically consistent superspinar waveform models and Bayesian model comparison for a definitive interpretation.

papers.title: Boundary Behavior of Bisectional Curvatures for Weighted Bergman Metrics
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the asymptotic boundary behavior of the holomorphic bisectional curvature for weighted Bergman metrics. By characterizing extremal functions via $L^2$-orthogonal projections, we establish an explicit formula for the weighted bisectional curvature. Utilizing the squeezing function, we then obtain quantitative upper and lower bounds for the curvature on bounded pseudoconvex domains. Furthermore, we prove that at strongly pseudoconvex boundary points, the bisectional curvature asymptotically coincides with that of the unit ball. As an application, these results provide a streamlined and unified proof for the known asymptotic behavior of the bisectional curvature of the Kähler-Einstein metric.

papers.title: Set-indexed and multiple sums in high dimensions
papers.abstract: We consider multiple and set-indexed sums of random vectors taking values in Euclidean space of growing dimension. It is shown that, when viewed as finite metric spaces, the sets of values of such sums converge in probability. The limit is identified as a generalization of the Wiener spiral, which appears as the high-dimensional limit of single-index sums.

papers.title: Adequate Losses via Quantitative Linear Logic
papers.abstract: As neural components are increasingly embedded in existing symbolic software -- including safety-critical systems -- the question arises of how to specify and enforce the safety of the newly introduced neural parts. Unlike traditional logical specifications, these must be amenable not only to the standard Boolean interpretation, but also to training and optimisation. The latter calls for a quantitative interpretation of the logical syntax, subject to further requirements such as smoothness and differentiability. Moreover, the qualitative and quantitative sides of the logic must share a unifying proof-theoretic and categorical semantics. Finally, the new logic should link cleanly to the substructural and program logics that underpin the verification of existing symbolic programs. In this paper, we present a logic that ticks all of these boxes. We introduce a family of calculi, $p$QLL, indexed by a hardness degree $p$, prove a cut-elimination theorem for them, and establish completeness with respect to enriched residuated `soft' lattices. At $p = \infty$, $p$QLL reduces to multiplicative additive linear logic (MALL), and provability in $p$QLL converges to provability in MALL as $p \to \infty$. We express optimisation objectives in the syntax of this logic and prove the quantitative adequacy of neuro-symbolic loss functions -- a result that has eluded the neuro-symbolic machine learning community for nearly a decade.

papers.title: Shortcut Mitigation via Spurious-Positive Samples
papers.abstract: Shortcut mitigation strategies commonly rely on training data annotations, group-balanced held-out data or the presence of all groups, i.e., all combinations of (spurious) attributes and classes, in the training data. However, these requirements are rarely met in practice. We instead propose a method for targeted model analysis to identify a small set of instances in which the model relies on spurious attributes. Using that set and following ``this feature should not be used for prediction'' reasoning, we identify highly relevant neurons in an intermediate layer and regularize their impact. This ensures that models learn to depend on informative features rather than being right for the wrong reasons, thereby improving robustness without requiring additional balanced held-out data or annotations.

papers.title: Evaluating a Large Language Model for Radiotherapy Patient Scheduling under Realistic Clinical and Operational Constraints: a Feasibility Study
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy scheduling must balance clinical constraints and operational objectives. We evaluated the feasibility of using a large language model (LLM) to generate treatment schedules through simulation and retrospective clinical comparison. A one-year simulation modeled 1,400 new patients across 12 treatment categories and three linear accelerators (LINACs). Structured prompts provided ChatGPT with patient information, schedule status, clinical rules, and operational objectives. Scenarios assessed treatment-time consistency, LINAC continuity, gap reduction, and handling of infeasible requests. LLM schedules were compared with heuristic and constraint programming (CP-SAT) approaches under two objective settings. A six-week retrospective analysis included 2,043 clinical appointments. LLM-generated schedules met all predefined feasibility constraints in the evaluated scenarios, with 98.6-98.8% of fractions within preferred treatment-time windows. Prioritizing LINAC continuity reduced switching from 52.4 +/- 2.6% to 9.4 +/- 0.6%. Gap-constrained temporal relaxation reduced average daily gaps to 47.1 +/- 8.5 minutes and Friday gaps to 89.2 +/- 18.4 minutes while maintaining low overtime. The framework identified predefined violations in infeasible requests and suggested corrective actions. Heuristic and CP-SAT methods also generated feasible schedules, with performance dependent on objective weighting. In retrospective evaluation, all approaches scheduled appointments without overtime; LLM strategies reduced mean gaps by 50.8-77.1% and improved treatment-time consistency from 86.7% to 99.5-99.9%. These findings support further evaluation of structured LLM scheduling as a human-in-the-loop decision-support approach for radiotherapy.

papers.title: Bardeen spacetime as quantum corrected black hole: Grey-body factors and quasinormal modes of gravitational perturbations
papers.abstract: We study axial gravitational perturbations of the asymptotically flat Bardeen spacetime interpreted as a string-T-duality-inspired quantum-corrected Schwarzschild black hole. Starting from the anisotropic-fluid background, we derive the Regge--Wheeler-type master equation and the corresponding effective potential, and compute quasinormal modes with high-order WKB--Padé and time-domain methods. We show that increasing the quantum-correction scale $\ell_0$ raises and shifts the barrier inward, causing the black hole to ring at higher frequencies and decay more slowly. The same deformation suppresses low-frequency transmission, shifts the onset of grey-body factors to larger frequencies, and reorganizes the partial and total absorption cross-sections. Overall, the results identify a clear and consistent imprint of short-distance regularization on both ringdown and scattering observables.

papers.title: When Adaptation Fails: A Gradient-Based Diagnosis of Collapsed Gating in Vision-Language Prompt Learning
papers.abstract: Adaptive prompting mechanisms have been proposed to enhance vision-language models by dynamically tailoring prompts to inputs. However, in frozen few-shot prompt learning with CLIP-style backbones, we systematically observe that adaptive gates and prompt-selection modules often collapse: they produce nearly constant outputs, contribute negligible gradient signals, and frequently fail to outperform fixed prompts. To further explore this issue, we present a systematic diagnostic study to uncover the underlying causes and conditions of adaptation failure. Through controlled experiments across datasets and multiple prompt learning architectures, we identify two recurring failure modes: gradient magnitude imbalance and gate degradation. Our findings invite a re-examination of indiscriminately adding architectural complexity in parameter-efficient learning and clarify when prompt-level adaptive gating is, and is not, effective in this regime.

papers.title: Exposing and Mitigating Temporal Attack in Deepfake Video Detection
papers.abstract: While spatiotemporal deepfake detectors achieve high AUC, our experiments reveal their susceptibility to evasion attacks. These models tend to overfit on fragile temporal spectrum cues, rather than learning robust semantic causality. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose SpInShield, a temporal spectral-invariant defense framework explicitly designed to decouple semantic motion from manipulatable spectral artifacts. We propose a learnable spectral adversary that dynamically synthesizes severe spectral deformations, simulating extreme attack scenarios. By employing a shortcut suppression optimization strategy, SpInShield compels the encoder to extract reliable forensic cues while purging unstable spectral statistics from the latent space. Experiments show that SpInShield obtains competitive performance on widely used datasets and outperforms the strongest baseline by 21.30 percentage points in AUC under simulated amplitude spectral attacks.

papers.title: Finding accurate eigenvalues and eigenvectors of positive semi-definite matrices given a subspace
papers.abstract: We revisit a classical problem in numerical linear algebra: given a $k$-dimensional subspace $\mathcal{Q}$ with orthonormal basis $Q$ that approximates the leading eigenspace of an $n\times n$ positive semi-definite matrix $A$, the goal is to extract high-accuracy eigenvalues. The Rayleigh-Ritz (RR) method is the standard algorithm for the task, which has been shown to be optimal in several ways (when $A$ is symmetric, not necessarily positive semi-definite $A\succeq 0$). In this paper, we show that when $A\succeq 0$, alternative methods can outperform RR, including Nystr{ö}m and one-sided projected SVD, while having the same computational complexity; that is, the main cost is in computing $AQ$, plus an $O(nk^2)$ term. In particular, we advocate the use of Nystr{ö}m's method, quantitatively showing that the approximate leading eigenvalues have better accuracy than RR, and the improvement can be arbitrarily large. The significant accuracy improvement occurs for the first $i$ eigenvalues if $λ_i \gg λ_{k+1}$ and uniformly for all $k$ eigenvalues if $λ_k \gg λ_{k+1}$. This theoretical observation can be extended to the case where we extract $k$ leading eigenvalues from a larger-dimensional subspace. A similar improvement is numerically observed for the purpose of approximating the leading eigenvectors. In contrast, when the target eigenvalues are the trailing ones, the situation is reversed, and the Nystr{ö}m method performs poorly; we suggest a remedy based on a shift for this situation.

papers.title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on Cayley graphs over dihedral groups
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of Cayley graphs over dihedral groups that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. For $n\ge 3$, let $D_n:=\langle a,b : a^n=b^2=1,\ bab=a^{-1}\rangle$ be the dihedral group of order $2n$, and let $S\subseteq D_n\setminus\{1\}$ satisfying $S=S^{-1}$ and $\langle S\rangle =D_n$. We show that the Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(D_n,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $(D_n,S)$ is equivalent to one of the following pairs: $(D_n,\{b,ba\})$; $(D_n,\{a,a^{-1},ba,ba^{-1}\})$, where $4$ does not divide $n$; or $(D_{2m},\{b,ba^{m},ba,ba^{m+1}\})$, where $m$ is odd. Our proof combines the representation theory of $D_n$ with tools from algebraic number theory.

papers.title: SoCal: A Language for Memory-Layout Factorization of Recursive Datatypes
papers.abstract: Array-of-structures (AoS) to structure-of-arrays (SoA) is a classic compiler transformation that improves memory locality and enables data-parallel execution. Existing AoS-to-SoA transformations target regular, array-based programs in imperative languages, such as C. However, many applications traverse tree-shaped data such as ASTs in compilers, DOM trees in browsers, and k-d trees in scientific workloads. Prior work speeds up functional programs over trees by serializing algebraic datatypes (ADTs) into one contiguous buffer. Such a representation interleaves the fields of every node, similar to an AoS layout. We introduce a factored layout of ADTs, which stores its fields in separate buffers, producing a layout that resembles SoA. In a factored layout, a traversal can focus on relevant fields and ignore the rest, similar to extracting a column from a SoA representation; in this setting, traversals over scalar fields can be vectorized. Working with raw byte arrays is error-prone, though: wrong indexing can silently read bytes from a wrong field or write past the end of a value. We therefore introduce SoCal, a type-safe language for expressing traversals over factored ADTs. Our compiler, Colobus, transforms a simple functional language with ADTs reminiscent of Haskell to C, using SoCal as the intermediate representation. Colobus generates traversals over byte arrays in the factored representation and performs optimizations such as field skipping and vectorization. Across a suite of benchmarks, Colobus shows the average speedups of 3.8x and 5.2x over fold and map passes, respectively.

papers.title: Multi-Objective Adaptive Beamforming Using Partial Knowledge of Dynamic Dielectric Media for Non-Invasive Microwave Hyperthermia
papers.abstract: We investigate multi-objective adaptive beamformer design strategies for non-invasive microwave hyperthermia. Our focus is to address the challenges of maintaining focused power deposition in desired locations while reducing unwanted heating elsewhere under conditions of changing dielectric properties. The process of heating the media causes changes in the dielectric properties of the media, which can degrade the effectiveness beamformers with static weights. Typical hyperthermic beamformer designs calculate antenna beamforming weights using patient-specific high resolution dielectric maps obtained by MRI or microwave tomography, however this process is time consuming and difficult to perform in real-time. In this work, we explore the efficacy of microwave hyperthermia in various inhomogeneous media under changing dielectric conditions, with the goal of informing the design of future adaptive real-time microwave hyperthermia techniques. We aim to achieve cell apoptosis by obtaining temperatures of $\sim$ 45 $^\circ\text{C}$ through selective absorption of electromagnetic wave focusing at a 2.5 GHz carrier frequency with little to no knowledge of the changes in the dielectric media and simultaneously place nulls to avoid unwanted heating outside of the treatment zone. We investigate the effectiveness of the linear constrained minimum power (LCMP) algorithm for near-field multi-objective beamforming and examine the power density obtained from finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations on simple analytical models and anatomically realistic numerical breast phantoms. To gain a comprehensive knowledge of the efficacy of the beamformer we evaluate the resulting thermal maps of the models in simple homogeneous cases, heterogeneous cases and MRI-derived phantom breast models.

papers.title: Analytically Characterized Optimal Power Control for Signal-Level-Integrated Sensing, Computing and Communication in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: In next-generation wireless edge systems, efficient functionality integration is essential to address the growing demands of communication, computation, and sensing. Signal-level integrated sensing, computing, and communication (Sig-ISCC) is envisioned, where a single waveform simultaneously supports sensing, computing and communication via over-the-air computation (AirComp). Meanwhile, federated learning (FL) is widely regarded as a promising distributed machine learning framework that enables network intelligence in a privacy-preserving and secure manner, and exhibits strong synergy with AirComp, which alleviates the communication bottleneck of FL. In this paper, we study uplink Sig-ISCC design for AirComp-FL with joint target detection. We formulate the joint power and receive-scaling control problem, where edge devices' transmitted signals should serve both sensing and AirComp purposes. The goal is to minimize the AirComp aggregation distortion subject to a joint target-detection requirement. Although the resulting problem is non-convex in the original variables, we show that it admits an equivalent convex reformulation after a suitable variable transformation. By exploiting analytical optimality properties, we develop a robust, optimal, and polynomial-time-complexity algorithm that efficiently achieves the optimal transmit powers and receive scaling factor. Simulation results validate the optimality and numerical robustness of the proposed algorithm and show its superior FL performance compared to baseline methods.

papers.title: The SK model with a sparse variance profile: free energy and AMP-based magnetization estimation at high temperature
papers.abstract: A generalization of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model for spin glasses is considered, in which the interaction matrix is endowed with a variance profile that has no particular structure and may be sparse. In the first part of the paper, an asymptotic equivalent of the free energy is derived at sufficiently high temperatures, regardless of the signature of the variance profile matrix. In the second part, the mean of the spin vector under the Gibbs measure is estimated using an Approximate Message Passing algorithm that generalizes the one used for the SK case. The dynamical approach of Adhikari et al (J Stat Phys 2021), originally developed for the classical SK model, is adapted to the present setting to obtain these results.

papers.title: Quantum limits on squeezing
papers.abstract: In our work, we show how, for a network of bosonic modes, canonical commutation relations constrain the coefficients relating input and internal modes. Based on these constraints, we derive a lower bound on the total steady-state squeezing achievable in reservoir-engineered (dissipative) squeezing schemes, quantified by the sum of mode-optimal quadrature variances each normalized to its corresponding input variance. The bound on this normalized sum follows solely from canonical commutation relations and stability, and is saturated in the strong-coupling limit at unity. Furthermore, we show that adding independent parametric driving terms for each mode changes the quantum noise--gain balance and yields, for the same normalized mode-optimal sum, a distinct optimum bound, approaching 1/2. In addition, we show how these constraints allow us to reformulate the Duan inseparability criterion for a three-mode bosonic system in terms of a single parameter-dependent figure of merit. Our results apply directly to current electromechanical and nanomechanical experiments and indicate that the two-mode bounds can be experimentally approached even at room temperature.

papers.title: Lagrange: Operating Italy's First Publicly-Accessible Quantum Computer for Research and Education
papers.abstract: We describe the design, implementation, and nine-month operational experience of the software management stack for Lagrange, an IQM Spark five-qubit superconducting quantum computer jointly acquired by LINKS Foundation, Politecnico di Torino and the Italian National Institute of Metrological Research (INRiM), and managed by LINKS. Lagrange is, to our knowledge, the first quantum computer in Italy that is fully operational and accessible to students and researchers from multiple institutions under formal service agreements, and to the general public under commercial agreements. When installed in mid-2025, the IQM Spark hardware was delivered by the vendor with authentication only: no billing, project management or fair usage enforcement were provided. We developed a modular middleware layer that filled that gap without modifying any vendor client software, by intercepting API calls through a proxy that enforces project-based budgets, reservation-aware authorisation, and per-user fairness policies. The middleware adopts a plugin architecture that cleanly separates vendor-specific logic from site-specific policies, enabling reuse across different quantum hardware backends and deployment contexts. Since entering production in September 2025, the system has processed over 240,000 quantum jobs totalling more than 1 week of QPU execution time, with greater than 98% uptime. Notably, students at Politecnico di Torino regularly use the machine during both lectures and formal examinations -- a practice we believe to be unique in Europe. We report on the system architecture, the operational lessons learned, and the infrastructure choices that made this deployment possible.

papers.title: Composite quantum gates simultaneously compensated for multiple errors
papers.abstract: Systematic control errors remain a primary obstacle to realizing high-fidelity single-qubit gates. To suppress these errors, we construct phase-controlled and variable-area X and Hadamard composite gates that compensate for simultaneous quasistatic amplitude and detuning errors in a two-level rectangular-pulse model. Our construction uses two complementary strategies: (i) cancellation of error derivatives of the full unitary propagator in the Cayley-Klein parametrization, and (ii) direct minimization of the average gate infidelity over prescribed error ranges. For shorter sequences, our approach yields performance comparable to established analytical solutions. Selected longer sequences achieve substantially lower mean gate infidelities than established comparison pulses over the prescribed error domains, including reductions of several orders of magnitude. Across the derived composite-gate families, the central mean infidelity decreases approximately exponentially with sequence length. Selected controls retain high fidelity in simulations with finite pulse edges and time-dependent detuning, without a need for recalibration.

papers.title: Linear Response for Bernoulli Convolutions
papers.abstract: Let $μ_λ$ be the Bernoulli convolution measure with parameter $λ\in(0,1)$. We study the regularity of the function %We prove that $h=h_ϕ:λ\mapsto \int_{\mathbb{R}}ϕ(x)\,dμ_λ(x)$ for Hölder observables $ϕ$. We describe sufficient conditions for both smoothness and non smoothness of this function. In particular, we show that for almost every function with respect to certain Wiener like measures on $C[0,1]$, $h_ϕ$ exhibits a phase transition: it is almost nowhere differentiable for small $λ$ and it is almost everywhere differentiable for large $λ.$

papers.title: Extremely high-energy bremsstrahlung in matter
papers.abstract: The theory of bremsstrahlung $e \to eγ$ by extremely high energy electrons passing through ordinary matter has been qualitatively incomplete. We revisit the suppression of bremsstrahlung by the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) effect, here accounting for quantum disruption of that effect from pair production. Our analysis covers the full range of ultra-relativistic electron and photon energies (subject to a few simplifying approximations).

papers.title: CPGRec+: A Balance-oriented Framework for Personalized Video Game Recommendations
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of gaming industry requires advanced recommender systems tailored to its dynamic landscape. Existing Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based methods primarily prioritize accuracy over diversity, overlooking their inherent trade-off. To address this, we previously proposed CPGRec, a balance-oriented gaming recommender system. However, CPGRec fails to account for critical disparities in player-game interactions, which carry varying significance in reflecting players' personal preferences and may exacerbate over-smoothness issues inherent in GNN-based models. Moreover, existing approaches underutilize the reasoning capabilities and extensive knowledge of large language models (LLMs) in addressing these limitations. To bridge this gap, we propose two new modules. First, Preference-informed Edge Reweighting (PER) module assigns signed edge weights to qualitatively distinguish significant player interests and disinterests while then quantitatively measuring preference strength to mitigate over-smoothing in graph convolutions. Second, Preference-informed Representation Generation (PRG) module leverages LLMs to generate contextualized descriptions of games and players by reasoning personal preferences from comparing global and personal interests, thereby refining representations of players and games. Experiments on \textcolor{black}{two Steam datasets} demonstrate CPGRec+'s superior accuracy and diversity over state-of-the-art models. The code is accessible at https://github.com/HsipingLi/CPGRec-Plus.

papers.title: Generating Concept Lexicalizations via Dictionary-Based Cross-Lingual Sense Projection
papers.abstract: We study the task of automatically expanding WordNet-style lexical resources to new languages through sense generation. We generate senses by associating target-language lemmas with existing lexical concepts via semantic projection. Given a sense-tagged English corpus and its translation, our method projects the annotated synsets onto aligned target-language tokens and assigns the corresponding lemmas to those synsets. To generate alignments and ensure their quality, we augment a pretrained base aligner with a bilingual dictionary, which is also used to filter incorrect sense projections. We evaluate the method on multiple languages, comparing it to prior methods, as well as dictionary-based and large language model baselines. Results show that the proposed project-and-filter strategy improves precision while remaining interpretable and resource- efficient. We release our code, documentation, and generated sense inventories at https://github.com/UAlberta-NLP/ExpandNet.

papers.title: Distinguishability of locally diagonal orthogonally invariant quantum states
papers.abstract: We study the distinguishability of quantum states under local operations with classical communication (LOCC), separable, and positive-partial-transpose (PPT) measurements, focusing on locally diagonal orthogonally invariant (LDOI) states -- those invariant under local diagonal orthogonal twirling. This class includes many important families such as Werner states, isotropic states, X-states, and Dicke states. We show that optimal PPT and separable measurements for distinguishing LDOI states can always be taken to be LDOI, and the LOCC supremum can be approached by LDOI LOCC POVMs, enabling a dimensional reduction from $n^4$ to $O(n^2)$ in the associated optimization problems. We establish efficiently computable bounds on the distinguishability of orthonormal LDOI bases and prove that for a broad class of such bases -- including all two-qubit cases -- the LOCC supremum equals the PPT and separable optima. More generally, we show the gap between PPT and LOCC distinguishability is at most $(n-2)/(2n^2)$ for local dimension $n$.

papers.title: Minimizing classical resources in variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling
papers.abstract: Measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) is a framework for quantum information processing in which a computational task is carried out through one-qubit measurements on a highly entangled resource state. Due to the indeterminacy of the outcomes of a quantum measurement, the random outcomes of these operations, if not corrected, yield a variational quantum channel family. Traditionally, this randomness is corrected through classical processing in order to ensure deterministic unitary computations. Recently, variational measurement-based quantum computation (VMBQC) has been introduced to exploit this measurement-induced randomness to gain an advantage in generative modeling. A limitation of this approach is that the corresponding channel model has twice as many parameters compared to the unitary model, scaling as $N \times D$, where $N$ is the number of logical qubits (width) and $D$ is the depth of the VMBQC model. This can often make optimization more difficult and may lead to poorly trainable models. In this paper, we present a restricted VMBQC model that extends the unitary setting to a channel-based one using only a single additional trainable parameter. We show, both numerically and algebraically, that this minimal extension is sufficient to generate probability distributions that cannot be learned by the corresponding unitary model.

papers.title: DD-03B: Target-level analysis of ligand-protein dissociation pathways reveals ligand-specific exit pathways weakly coupled to binding affinity
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand interactions are conventionally described by a structure and a binding affinity (Kd). Kinetic simulation datasets have grown rapidly, but most analyses remain structure-centred and RMSD-based, and the kinetic information carried by the trajectories is rarely extracted. Here we analyse 766,550 complete dissociation trajectories for 15,540 protein-ligand complexes grouped into 3,687 UniProt accessions. Each trajectory is reduced to a uniform record of 119 descriptors-ligand and structure size, trajectory statistics, the pathway distribution of escape events, and pocket and escape-volume descriptors-so that records from different systems can be compared, joined and searched. This tokenisation shows that the pocket and the ligand act on the same quantity at different levels: the pocket defines the repertoire of exits, and the ligand sets the weights. In open sites the repertoire collapses to one broad mode and affinity tracks ligand size and contact; in confined pockets the exit ensemble splits into several channels whose weights follow ligand size rather than binding affinity. UniProt grouping is a convenient classification above the PDB entry but not the right final unit: two systems illustrate domain separation and degeneracy, and a structural classifier would be preferable. We present the framework as a general analysis paradigm for molecular dynamics trajectory libraries.

papers.title: A rational model for the fiberwise THH transfer I: Sullivan algebras
papers.abstract: Given a map $f$ of fibrations over a space $B$ such that the fiber of $f$ is simply connected and finitely dominated, we prove that its fiberwise THH transfer, considered as a map of parametrized spectra over $B$, is rationally modeled by the Hochschild homology transfer of a Sullivan model of $f$. The proof goes in two steps. Firstly, we use the machinery of higher categorical traces to show that the fiberwise THH transfer can be computed internally to parametrized spectra. Secondly, we model the resulting description rationally using work of Braunack-Mayer, who proved that parametrized spectra can be modeled by modules over Sullivan algebras. In Part II, we will use our result to obtain a rational model of the Becker-Gottlieb transfer, and for applications to manifold topology.

papers.title: Bridging Distant Ideas: the Impact of AI on R&D and Recombinant Innovation
papers.abstract: We study how artificial intelligence (AI) affects firms' incentives to pursue incremental versus radical knowledge recombinations. We develop a model of recombinant innovation embedded in a Schumpeterian quality-ladder framework, in which innovation arises from recombining ideas across varying distances in a knowledge space. R&D consists of multiple tasks, a fraction of which can be performed by AI. AI facilitates access to distant knowledge domains, but at the same time it also increases the aggregate rate of creative destruction, shortening the monopoly duration that rewards radical innovations. We obtain three main results. First, the effect of increasing the share of AI-automated R&D tasks is non-monotonic under specific conditions: firms initially target more radical innovations, but beyond a threshold they shift the focus toward incremental innovations. Second, with falling optimal distance, we may have increasing expected log-growth of knowledge due to higher innovation frequency or a hump-shaped growth. Finally, we identify a sufficient condition under which the target distance chosen in the decentralized equilibrium is sub-optimal from a social welfare point of view.

papers.title: On intersections of function fields
papers.abstract: Let $X:\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{R}$ and $Y:\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{T}$ be holomorphic maps between compact Riemann surfaces such that $X^*M(\mathcal{R})\cdot Y^*M(\mathcal{T})=M(\mathcal{E})$, where $M(\mathcal{S})$ denotes the field of meromorphic functions on a Riemann surface $\mathcal{S}$. We study the problem of determining when the degree $[M(\mathcal{E}):X^*M(\mathcal{R})\cap Y^*M(\mathcal{T})]$ is finite and attains the minimal possible value $\mathrm{deg}\,X\cdot\mathrm{deg}\,Y$. When $X$ is a Galois covering, we give a complete characterization in terms of factorizations of $Y$ into an equivariant map followed by a Galois covering. We also establish some results without the maximality condition, as well as general results on the functional equation $A\circ X=B\circ Y$ when one of the maps involved is a Galois covering.

papers.title: Quantum simulation of a nonuniform Dicke model in a two-dimensional trapped-ion crystal
papers.abstract: Existing experimental realizations of the Dicke model in atomic or ionic systems are based on global observables assuming uniform spin-boson coupling, while inevitable experimental nonuniformity on the one hand requires site-resolved measurement of spin states, and on the other hand provides potential quantum advantage in simulating multi-spin distributions. Here we report the quantum simulation of a nonuniform Dicke-like model, due to either the inevitable experimental imperfection or the engineered spin-phonon coupling pattern, in a two-dimensional (2D) crystal of up to 200 ions. We explicitly demonstrate the sensitivity of few-spin observables and multi-spin distributions to the spatial inhomogeneity of the model, and examine the relaxation dynamics of the nonuniform model by measuring the subsystem entropies of selected ion groups. Our work enables the study of Dicke-like models beyond the symmetric subspace, paving the way toward understanding the role of nonuniformity in its thermalization and quantum chaos behavior.

papers.title: Smooth plane curves with a unique outer Galois point and their automorphism groups
papers.abstract: We consider smooth plane curves $\mathcal{X}$ of degree $d\geq4$, defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, that possess a unique outer Galois point. This geometric condition forces the curve to be a cyclic covering of the projective line, and ensures that its automorphism group fits into a specific theoretical framework. For each possible non-cyclic reduced automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}_{\operatorname{red}}(\mathcal{X})$, we fully characterize the defining equation of $\mathcal{X}$ and the precise structure of its full automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{X})$. This comprehensive analysis not only identifies the exact form of the equation for each automorphism type but also establishes the detailed criteria under which these scenarios can occur, thereby offering a complete classification of defining equations for smooth plane curves with a unique outer Galois point and a non-cyclic reduced automorphism group.

papers.title: Scalable topological quantum computing based on Sine-Cosine chain models
papers.abstract: We propose a scalable framework for quantum information processing based on Matryoshka-type sine-cosine chains, a hierarchy of one-dimensional chiral-symmetric lattices obtained by repeated ($P$ times) square-root construction starting from the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain. A chain of order $P$ can host $2^{P+2}-2$ protected edge states, so a single physical device can encode a qudit of equivalent dimension (or, equivalently, several independent qubits) instead of one qubit per device. We show that (i) the adiabatic defect-transfer step underlying SSH-based topological gates carries over unchanged to the Matryoshka chain, transferring the full set of defect states simultaneously; (ii) a Y-junction braiding protocol then composes single-qudit gate operations in all energy sectors at once, increasing the operation density per physical device; and (iii) the same edge states provide a quantum memory whose capacity scales exponentially with the chain order at fixed physical length. Numerical fidelity analysis under on-site, hopping, and correlated angle disorder shows partial, chiral-symmetry-protected robustness.

papers.title: RECOVER: Robust Entity Correction via agentic Orchestration of hypothesis Variants for Evidence-based Recovery
papers.abstract: Entity recognition in Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) is challenging for rare and domain-specific terms. In domains such as finance, medicine, and air-traffic control, these errors are costly. If an entity is entirely absent from the ASR output, text-only post-correction has little signal to recover it. To address this, we introduce RECOVER, an agentic post-ASR entity-correction framework. It leverages multiple hypotheses as evidence from ASR, retrieves relevant entities, proposes Large Language Model (LLM) correction under constraints, filters them through deterministic guardrails and uses an LLM critic that judges each surviving edit and can trigger a targeted feedback round to recover an entity the first pass missed. The hypotheses are used by one of several strategies, namely 1-Best, Entity-Aware Select, Recognizer Output Voting Error Reduction (ROVER) Ensemble, LLM-Select and Adaptive Routing. Evaluated across five diverse datasets over a Whisper-large-v3 baseline, it achieves up to 49% relative reduction in entity-phrase word error rate (E-WER) and increases entity recall by up to 14 percentage points while preserving the overall word error rate (WER), with LLM-Select the strongest strategy.

papers.title: Thermalization Across Scales on a Digital Quantum Processor
papers.abstract: Thermalization of isolated quantum many-body systems normally unfolds via dynamical spreading of entanglement across progressively increasing spatial scales. The speed of this dynamical process, however, can be affected by the presence of local disorder. Here we study the crossover between slow and fast thermalization in a disordered two-dimensional Heisenberg Floquet model using digital quantum simulations with up to 100 superconducting qubits. Our experiment measures subsystem purities and $Z$-basis marginal collision entropies for patches of up to $3\times 3$ qubits. We resolve the onset of thermalization across scales by tracking each quantity's approach to its asymptotic value. In regimes where the system is moderately entangled, we validate our calibrated quantum simulations against state-of-the-art classical simulations. Near the crossover to fast thermalization, the classical methods no longer reliably converge due to volume-law growth of entanglement. By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.

papers.title: A Variational Latent Equilibrium for Learning in Neuronal Circuits
papers.abstract: Brains remain unrivaled in their ability to recognize and generate complex spatiotemporal patterns. While AI is able to reproduce some of these capabilities, deep learning algorithms remain largely at odds with our current understanding of brain circuitry and dynamics. This is prominently the case for backpropagation through time (BPTT), the go-to algorithm for learning complex temporal dependencies. In this work we propose a general formalism to approximate BPTT in a controlled, biologically plausible manner. Our approach builds on, unifies and extends several previous approaches to local, time-continuous, phase-free spatiotemporal credit assignment based on principles of energy conservation and extremal action. Our starting point is a prospective energy function of neuronal states, from which we calculate real-time error dynamics for time-continuous neuronal networks. With this, as a first contribution we provide a simple and straightforward derivation of the adjoint method dynamical equations, the time-continuous equivalent to BPTT. Importantly, additional approximations are necessary to avoid unphysical temporal non-localities. One such approximation was recently proposed in Generalized Latent Equilibrium (GLE), but enforcing temporal locality of the backpropagating dynamics induces an error in the gain that becomes problematic when processing complex signals. Thus, our second contribution is to design a learning rule for the backward weights to find a fully local (in space and time) set of equations for neuron and synapse dynamics that corrects for this gain difference. With this inclusion of backward weight learning, our theory provides a rigorous framework for spatiotemporal deep learning in the brain, while simultaneously advancing a blueprint for physical circuits capable of carrying out these computations.

papers.title: ViroGym: Realistic Large-Scale Benchmarks for Evaluating Viral Proteins
papers.abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) have shown strong potential for zero-shot prediction of missense variant effects, yet systematic benchmarking on viral proteins remains limited, a critical gap given the need for proactive tools that can anticipate emerging mutations ahead of experimental validation. Here we introduce ViroGym, a comprehensive benchmark evaluating pLMs across three tasks: 79 deep mutational scanning (DMS) assays covering eukaryotic viruses with 552,065 mutated sequences across 7 phenotypic readouts, 21 influenza neutralisation tasks, and a real-world pandemic prediction task for SARS-CoV-2. We benchmark well-established pLMs on fitness landscapes, antigenic diversity, and pandemic forecasting, and find that the ProGen2 family consistently achieves the strongest performance across all three tasks. Crucially, DMS and neutralisation performance reliably identifies models that generalise to real-world emergence, even though the mutation sets they surface barely overlap, revealing that complementary in vitro benchmarks capture the evolutionary constraints needed for real-world mutation forecasting. The data and code supporting this study are publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/GSK-AI/viroGym

papers.title: Timing-Aware Satellite Association for Multi-LEO Direct-to-Handset Communications
papers.abstract: The rapid deployment of large-scale low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations has positioned direct-to-handset (D2H) communications as a key enabler of future non-terrestrial networks. However, the limited link budget of handheld devices makes broadband service delivery challenging, and multi-satellite cooperative transmission is often required to provide sufficient power gain. In practice, such cooperation is severely hindered by asynchronous reception across satellites. This paper analyzes the received-signal model under the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) transmitter structure and shows that satellite-dependent propagation delays prevent simultaneous timing alignment for multiple user terminals (UTs). This timing mismatch induces severe inter-carrier interference (ICI) and inter-symbol interference (ISI), even from the intended signals, which fundamentally constrains the achievable cooperative gain. To address this issue, we propose a timing-aware satellite association strategy that enables cooperation only with satellites expected to satisfy a UT-side timing tolerance, thereby avoiding dominant asynchronous interference by design. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy improves throughput performance compared to single-satellite transmission and fully connected multi-satellite baselines.

papers.title: Multi-Band Sensing in FR3 with Background Dense Multipath Components
papers.abstract: Multi-band sensing has emerged as a key enabler of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), one of the six primary usage scenarios defined for IMT-2030 (6G). The introduction of frequency range 3 (FR3, 7-24 GHz), comprising non-contiguous sub-bands across a wide frequency span, further reinforces the importance of multi-band operation. In such scenarios, frequency-dependent propagation effects that are collectively referred to as dense multipath components (DMC), including clutter, diffraction, and diffuse scattering, must be carefully considered. Building on prior literature and our experimental observations, this paper proposes a novel ISAC channel analysis tailored to multi-band sensing, based on a channel model with background DMCs. It also assesses the sensing trade-offs among sub-bands by analyzing Cramér-Rao bound (CRB)-based fundamental limits. Furthermore, a scalable multi-band estimator is proposed that resolves angular ambiguities arising from the grating lobes effect. Simulation results of the multi-band estimator demonstrate substantial gains in estimation accuracy and reductions in false alarm rate over single-band estimators operating on each constituent sub-band within the CRB-achieving regime. In a representative test case, the proposed estimator achieves reductions of 37.41% and 17.04% in the root mean squared error of delay estimation compared to single-band estimators operating at 8.75 GHz and 21.7 GHz, respectively.

papers.title: Prodiabatic Elimination: Higher Order Elimination of Fast Variables with Quantum Noise
papers.abstract: Adiabatic elimination plays a central role in cavity quantum electrodynamics by removing fast cavity degrees of freedom, but at the cost of losing their finite-time response in multi-time correlations. We introduce prodiabatic elimination, a systematic expansion of the quantum Langevin equations that retains vacuum-noise contributions alongside higher-order corrections to the eliminated cavity field. This provides controlled access to arbitrary time- and normally ordered multi-time correlation functions, including photodetection observables, beyond what can be recovered from effective atomic dynamics alone. In the driven-dissipative Jaynes-Cummings model, we identify a vacuum-mediated effective repulsion between detected photons that suppresses short-delay bunching. For a single-photon switch, we analytically resolve a finite heralded response time arising from the cavity field's delayed adjustment to the atomic transfer.

papers.title: Finitary Cartesian closed varieties and semigroup actions
papers.abstract: We build on some ideas of Richard Garner. Let $M$ be a monoid and $B$ a Boolean algebra. A matched pair $[B|M]$ consists of $B$ and $M$ satisfying some axioms introduced by Garner. He then showed that every such matched pair determines a Boolean left restriction monoid $S = S[B|M]$. In this paper, we show that the data of a $[B|M]$-set, an action of a matched pair, may be encoded by means of what we call a factorizable Boolean supported action by $S$. This means that the category of $[B|M]$-sets is equivalent to the category of factorizable Boolean supported actions of $S$. We deduce, as a result of Garner's work, that every non-degenerate finitary Cartesian closed variety is equivalent to the category of factorizable Boolean supported actions of some Boolean left restriction monoid $S$.

papers.title: Evaluating Chain-of-Thought Reasoning through Reusability and Verifiability
papers.abstract: AI applications increasingly compose multiple models, where one model acts on the output produced by another model.
