Neither continuity of the functional nor commutativity of the algebra is assumed. We give a detailed account of three proofs: the original argument of Gleason and, independently, Kahane and Zelazko; the polynomial proof of Roitman and Sternfeld; and a proof by the author. We explain the complex analysis behind each: a special case of Hadamard's factorisation theorem, a polynomial argument using the fundamental theorem of algebra, and the Polya-Saxer theorem on zero-free entire functions and their derivatives. The elementary entire-function lemma needed for the first proof is proved in full; the Polya-Saxer theorem is used without proof. We give full details of the algebraic argument common to the three proofs, which deduces multiplicativity from the preservation of squares, including the non-commutative case. We then discuss applications and counterexamples, and present an extension to Ransford's generalised spectra using the Roitman--Sternfeld argument. We conclude with a brief guide to the more recent literature.

papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Adversarial Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses Across Seven Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) deployed in safety-critical settings must resist adversarial inputs designed to elicit harmful outputs. We present a systematic empirical evaluation of five adversarial jailbreaking attack families---direct requests, roleplay-based jailbreaking, hypothetical framing, instruction override, and obfuscation---across seven open-weight LLMs served locally: Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma2-9B, and Phi-4-14B. We further evaluate four defense mechanisms---keyword blacklisting, self-reminder prompting, paraphrase-based sanitization, and perplexity-based filtering---against two high-ASR models (Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B) on a 20-prompt subset. Across 250 prompts per model, a content judge counted obfuscation attacks as harmful (HARMFUL or PARTIAL responses) at a pooled rate of 62.3%, the highest of any family, although only 7.1% of responses were rated HARMFUL. Hypothetical framing was the highest family for three of seven models. Obfuscation succeeded at nonzero rates on all seven. The content judge has not yet been validated against human labels. We find that model size does not significantly predict adversarial robustness (Spearman Rho =-0.64, p=0.12, n=7). A rule-based judge suggested a large gap between the two Llama-3 generations (16.8% and 40.8%); the content judge does not (17.2% and 18.4%). Self-reminder prompting gave the largest reduction, cutting ASR from 50% to 10% on Mistral-7B and from 45% to 5% on Llama-3.1-8B (40 percentage points on each model, against matched no-defense runs, scored with the rule-based judge; these defense results are provisional because that judge has known defects). Our code and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/Mdniloykhan/jailbreak-eval-7llms.

papers.title: Nodal magnon spin current at an antiferromagnet/altermagnet junction
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermally driven magnon spin current across a junction between a $d$-wave altermagnet (AM) and a ferromagnet (FM) or an antiferromagnet (AFM). The current consists of a component independent of the interface angle and an angularly dependent component with the $d$-wave form. For a sublattice-symmetric interface, the two junctions behave oppositely under reversal of the altermagnetic domain: in the FM/AM junction the angularly dependent component is odd and cancels on averaging over the domains, whereas in the AFM/AM junction the angularly independent component vanishes by symmetry and the angularly dependent component survives the domain average at a fixed Néel vector of the AFM. Both follow from a selective tunneling: a pair of spins bonded across the interface transmits magnons when the spins are parallel and not when antiparallel, which makes the AFM/AM junction a magnon valve: the configuration in which the bonded spins are antiparallel blocks the current up to the sublattice admixture of the magnons. We reveal the uniqueness of the altermagnet by comparing with the anisotropic antiferromagnet. The anisotropic tunneling is detectable as the sign reversal of the current between the interfaces normal to $[310]$ and $[130]$, and the valve reads the Néel vector of the altermagnet relative to that of the antiferromagnet through the magnitude of the current at a fixed interface.

papers.title: A Spectral Boundary for Independence Learnability
papers.abstract: Learning independence is fundamental to statistical inference and machine learning, yet learning independence between entire time series by a test remains challenging when only a single observation record is available. Existing guarantees often rely on structural or mixing assumptions, while stationarity and ergodicity alone do not permit consistent testing. In this work, we identify a class-level boundary governed by shared nontrivial Koopman eigenvalues, which represent common persistent oscillatory frequencies of the two processes. When no such eigenvalues are shared, we extend shift-based rank calibration with finite-window dependence witnesses and a data-adaptive threshold to construct a deterministic, weakly consistent test with finite-sample false-positive control, without quantitative mixing assumptions. Conversely, we show that no possibly randomized test can achieve vanishing false-positive probabilities under every independent jointly totally ergodic law while consistently detecting every dependent jointly totally ergodic law with a shared nontrivial eigenvalue. This impossibility already holds when the shared point spectrum is exactly the cyclic group generated by any single prescribed irrational eigenfrequency, identifying a spectral obstruction to universal learning of full-process independence.

papers.title: Theoretical Study of Classical Dynamics of Electron in Two-Frequency Paul Trap
papers.abstract: We present a theoretical study of trapping an electron in a two-frequency Paul trap, motivated by future hybrid architecture consisting of a doubly charged calcium ion (Ca$^{2+}$) and an electron. By isolating the electron from ionic-electron interactions, we formulate the equations of motion for the electron in the time-dependent trap potentials and cast them in the Hill form. Stability and dynamics are then analysed in terms of the dimensionless q-parameters, which encode the applied voltages, drive frequencies, trap geometry, and the particle's charge-to-mass ratio. Under the combined action of the two radio-frequency fields, the trapped electron's classical motion is shown to be approximated well by a slow secular oscillation modulated by two distinct motion sidebands originating from the low- and high-frequency RF drives. The approximation method presented here enables a quick evaluation of the relation between the device-design q-parameters and the electron motion. It offers a crucial foundation for developing physical models of electron-ion interactions in electron-ion traps.

papers.title: Geometry Matters in Packed 3D Attention
papers.abstract: Packing a 3D field into a token sequence gives every token two indices: a coordinate in the sample and a position in memory. Raster, Morton, and block-contiguous layouts change the position and leave the coordinate alone. A positional mechanism indexed by sequence position can therefore learn the memory layout rather than the object, and accuracy on the training layout cannot reveal that it has. We introduce PACK3D, a local-global attention operator that separates memory layout from attention geometry. It attends exactly within a coordinate-defined neighborhood, sees the whole field through pooled summaries, and rotates queries and keys with axial RoPE at token-grid coordinates. Because keys are rotated before pooling, each query-to-summary logit is a weighted sum of query-key terms evaluated at the summarized tokens' displacements from the query. The operator is equivariant to any repacking that carries coordinates, neighborhoods, summary memberships, and within-block slots along with the tokens. When evaluated on Allen WTC-11 microscopy at 262k tokens, PACK3D and a matched packed-sequence RoPE control reach comparable Dice on the training layout. Repacking the same validation volumes then costs the packed control 0.048 macro Dice on average, with a loss in all six seeds, while PACK3D changes by 0.0001. On MSD Heart and Spleen, sequence indexing again changes more predictions under repacking, at little cost in Dice. PACK3D also exceeds a parameter-matched 3D U-Net by 0.009 Dice over six seeds, and a full PACK3D layer runs within 7-31% of window-attention latency while adding a global pathway. Geometry, not storage order, should index attention over packed 3D fields. Code is available at https://github.com/amilworks/Pack3D.

papers.title: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents
papers.abstract: When an LLM agent fails, repair methods choose which action to replace and what to put in its place. They often score candidate repairs with greedy replay, a stronger model, an environment oracle, or a judge that reads the failed log. We ask whether these evaluators pick repairs that help the agent that will actually execute them. Holding failed trajectories and candidate single-step repairs fixed, we label every candidate with independent rollouts of the deployed policy and measure how much deployment value each evaluator's choice loses. On failures not screened for repair value, pre-specified tests show that greedy replay loses 0.08-0.13 in expected net success gain in ALFWorld and 0.06-0.13 in net reward in WebShop, relative to selection with the deployed agent's own rollouts. At an equal rollout budget, selecting repairs for Qwen2.5-7B with Qwen2.5-14B rollouts loses 0.25 in ALFWorld and 0.07 in WebShop, twenty 14B rollouts per candidate are worth no more than two of the 7B agent's own, and fresh rollouts confirm that the two models prefer opposite repairs on selected disagreement cases. The agent's own fine-tuned successor is a worse evaluator still: after one round of training on verified repairs, its rollouts lose 0.55-0.60 when they select repairs for the agent it was trained from, as a pre-specified test confirms. Relative to what selection is worth, substitute models forgo 11-53%; on $τ^2$-bench, where selecting is worth only 0.10, they lose 0.03. Repairs should be verified with the executor that will run them, and repair labels should name their executor, including its training version.

papers.title: The 't Hooft model on (A)dS$_2$
papers.abstract: We solve large-$N$ two-dimensional QCD with fundamental quarks---the 't Hooft model---on rigid AdS$_2$ and dS$_2$. Their isometries preserve the null gauge $A_-=0$ and in affine coordinates the curvature enters the light-front Hamiltonian only through the special-conformal generator of the null line. The $SL(2,\mathbb{R)}$ Casimir then results in an exact meson equation: 't Hooft's equation plus a Legendre operator whose sign is determined by the curvature. On AdS$_2$ it is related to equations proposed in the context of folded/segmented strings and light-front holography. The pion is massless in the chiral limit and obeys a Gell-Mann--Oakes--Renner relation that fixes the chiral condensate, the dimensions cross over from Regge to logarithmic growth once the flux tube exceeds the curvature radius, and the flat-space integrable structure survives. We also solve the problem of a quark interacting with an antiquark placed at the boundary: beyond a critical coupling the string pulls it back to the boundary, resulting in a scattering phase. On dS$_2$ and due to the expansion of space, the mesons are unstable resonances even at $N=\infty$ and eventually dissociate. Their widths are given by Boltzmann factors at the de Sitter temperature.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for nef bundles
papers.abstract: We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact Kähler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.

papers.title: Doubly robust estimation of direct and spillover effects using multiple pre-treatment periods
papers.abstract: Under interference, the treatment of some units affects the outcomes of others, so that the effect on a treated unit consists of a direct and a spillover component. A non-treated comparison group then generally identifies neither component, but the difference between the total effect on the treated and the spillover effect on the comparison units. Under certain identifying assumptions, both components may be identified separately when multiple pre-treatment periods are available, even in the absence of an uncontaminated comparison group. Under a no-anticipation assumption, pre-treatment outcomes are free of both components for every unit. Extrapolating the pre-treatment trend within a group, as in interrupted time-series approaches, therefore identifies the counterfactual outcome in the absence of any treatment, provided that the model used for the extrapolation is correctly specified. Applied to the treated it gives the total effect on them, applied to the non-treated at a given level of exposure the spillover effect on them. Disentangling the two components in addition requires effect homogeneity across treated and non-treated units with the same exposure and covariates, as well as common support in exposure. We derive doubly robust and Neyman-orthogonal expressions for the effects of interest, which permits controlling for possibly high-dimensional covariates by machine learning. A simulation study confirms the root-$n$ consistent behaviour of the estimators and the reliability of the standard errors under specific regularity conditions. We apply the framework to the compulsory licensing of enemy-owned patents in the United States in 1919. Licensing raised patenting in the licensed subclasses and in technologically close ones alike, so that a comparison-group design understates the total effect.

papers.title: S3-S2ST: Semantically Supervised Streaming Speech-to-Speech Translation
papers.abstract: Streaming speech-to-speech translation requires timely decisions about when partial input is sufficient for accurate translation. We present S3-S2ST, a model that learns to translate and speak from semantically aligned streaming supervision. By converting utterance-level speech pairs into incremental training examples, we teach a learned policy when to commit translations. Its adjustable threshold controls the quality--latency tradeoff on a fixed 640\,ms input grid. S3-S2ST delivers competitive English--Chinese translation on FLEURS and leads the evaluated streaming systems in translation quality on the internal 9-pair test set. On RealSI, adapting the threshold to buffered speech further improves quality over a low fixed threshold with little change in first-audio latency. We have released the training and inference code and 4B model weights at https://github.com/QwenAudio/S3-S2ST

papers.title: Two-sample inference for sequence-derived feature distributions from deep sequencing data
papers.abstract: Many biological contexts involve heterogeneous populations of related molecular variants within a single individual. For example, some viral infections such as HIV-1 exhibit substantial diversity within a single host. Advances in sequencing technology now make it possible to characterize such populations by generating up to thousands of genetic sequences from a biological sample. In many settings, each sequence can be mapped to a numeric feature, such as Hamming distance to a reference sequence. This collection of feature values defines a one-dimensional distribution that characterizes individual-level viral diversity. When comparing these features across independent groups, past analyses have typically reduced each individual's data to a single summary value, such as the mean or mode. We propose a framework that retains the full individual-level distribution as the object of analysis. Drawing on existing tools from distributional data analysis, our framework uses Wasserstein barycenters to summarize the observed individual-level distributions within groups into a single representative distribution. These group barycenters are then compared using differences in quantiles and tested for equality. A practical challenge is that the number of sequences obtained, known as sequencing depth, can vary across biological samples. Through simulation studies, we examine when low sequencing depth can distort inference and present practical strategies for addressing these issues. We then illustrate the framework using data from the HIV-1 Antibody Mediated Prevention efficacy trials and a human B cell receptor sequencing study of vaccine-elicited immune responses. By using the entire collection of sequences for each individual, our approach can reveal group differences that may be obscured by single-number summary analyses.

papers.title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise in specialty medicine, yet existing evaluations largely focus on isolated clinical encounters rather than assessing the distinct clinical responsibilities along longitudinal care pathways. We introduce NPC-RubricBench, a phase-aware benchmark for evaluating multistage clinical reasoning across the cancer care continuum, using nasopharyngeal carcinoma as a defined disease context. Curated from real-world records of 405 patients at two cancer centers, it comprises 941 evaluation units across six sequential care stages, from work-up through follow-up, and 17,688 patient-specific criteria across five dimensions. Each assessment is restricted to clinical evidence available at the corresponding decision point. Across 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs, we find strong diagnostic scores did not ensure reliable downstream care. Decision Quality ranged from 56.8 to 94.7 in diagnosis on a 0-100 scale, but dropped to 8.9-56.0 in staging and spanned 32.4-94.2 in treatment. Crucially, failure modes differed across phases: explicit decision errors predominated in anatomical staging (48.2%), whereas decision omissions were more frequent during initial work-up (33.4%) and post-treatment follow-up (30.4%). Varying query granularity revealed a trade-off between decision quality and other clinical requirements. Broad open-ended requests reduced decision quality across all 30 models, whereas more detailed, checklist-like prompts improved decision quality but were accompanied by lower evidence faithfulness and safety adherence. These findings highlight the need to assess clinical reliability against the distinct clinical requirements of each phase along the longitudinal care pathway. Finally, NPC-RubricBench informs the design of stage-aware clinical guardrails and offers a reusable blueprint for evaluating LLMs across other cancers and chronic diseases.

papers.title: Model Selection for Off-Policy Evaluation via Bellman Tournaments
papers.abstract: Model selection and hyperparameter tuning pose a central challenge in off-policy evaluation (OPE) because estimation errors in fitted $Q$-functions and occupancy ratios cannot be directly evaluated using held-out transition data. Existing Bellman-residual-based validation methods often require auxiliary regressions, while many minimax-based methods require optimization over separate critic classes. We propose pairwise Bellman validation (PBV), a family of penalized Bellman tournament methods that reduces validation to computing held-out sample averages. PBV constructs critics from pairwise candidate differences, on the log scale for occupancy ratios, and selects the candidate with the smallest worst-case penalized score. This construction approximates oracle critics given by $Q$-function errors and log ratios of candidate to true occupancy ratios, whose Bellman and adjoint Bellman moments control estimation error. Critic penalties account for approximation error under candidate-class misspecification. We establish finite-sample oracle inequalities relative to the best available candidate, even under candidate-class misspecification. For $Q$-function selection, unweighted PBV avoids importance weighting but requires a coercivity condition on a quadratic form induced by the Bellman operator. Importance-weighted PBV (IW-PBV) uses marginalized importance weighting to exploit Bellman contraction under the target-policy occupancy measure, avoiding this condition. For occupancy-ratio selection, adjoint PBV (A-PBV) exploits KL contraction of the adjoint Bellman operator to obtain oracle guarantees under the offline data law. On Hopper and DeepOPE, unweighted PBV is competitive with LSTD-Tournament, often achieving higher accuracy on Hopper, while importance weighting can further improve performance under controlled overlap.

papers.title: Positivity of simplicial volume and uniqueness for the twelve-vertex flag three-spheres
papers.abstract: We study the twelve-vertex flag triangulation $T_{12}$ of $S^3$ and the Davis $4$-manifold $M(T_{12})$ associated with it. We prove that $T_{12}$ is, up to isomorphism, the unique flag triangulation of $S^3$ with twelve vertices in which every edge is contained in a square; this proves Milizia's Conjecture~6.31. We also prove a general criterion for the tangent Euler class of a Davis $4$-manifold to be bounded, and we verify it for $T_{12}$ by means of an explicit symmetric form. Since the Euler class takes the value $256$ on the fundamental class of $M(T_{12})$, the duality between bounded cohomology and simplicial volume gives $\|M(T_{12})\|>0$. This answers Milizia's Question~1.7.

papers.title: Long-time action stability for perturbed KdV near finite-gap tori
papers.abstract: We prove action and spectral stability near finite-gap tori of the periodic Korteweg--de Vries equation under autonomous analytic Hamiltonian perturbations of size $\varepsilon$. The estimates are uniform over prescribed compact families, without small-amplitude or nonresonance assumptions, and allow nearby initial data with infinitely many open gaps. Assuming a strong solution and a uniform higher Sobolev bound on $[0,T_0/\varepsilon]$, we permit one-derivative loss in the perturbing Hamiltonian's normal gradient. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and initial normal Birkhoff size $r_0$, the tangential action variations and weighted sum of normal actions are bounded by $C_δ(r_0^2+\varepsilon^{2δ})$, while the spectral-gap variation in $\ell^2$ is bounded by $C_δ(r_0+\varepsilon^δ)$, for every $0<δ<1/4$. A key ingredient is coercivity of the negative Hessian of the nonlinear KdV Hamiltonian on the full $\ell^2$ action space at every finite-gap action. We combine this with resonance analysis and corrected action observables evaluated along the solution. The hypotheses are verified for several local and nonlocal Hamiltonian perturbations.

papers.title: Controlled Block Proximal Linearized Method for Nonconvex and Nonsmooth Optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider multiblock nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization without assuming bounded iterates or coercivity of the original objective. We propose the Controlled Block Proximal Linearized (CBPL) method, whose control potentials establish boundedness while retaining the original objective, constraints and variables. We prove finite length and whole-sequence convergence to an effective critical point of the original objective, where one limiting subgradient annihilates all effective feasible directions. We establish finite total variation of the original objective and block functions, summable original effective residuals, and finite termination and linear or sublinear convergence rates for the original objective values. Scale orthogonality further gives full original criticality and, for homogeneous balancing controls, summable absolute objective errors with an $o(1/K)$ best-iterate bound. We establish a complete degeneracy theory for graph-regularized nonnegative factorizations: scale criticality is equivalent to graph collapse, and full criticality eliminates graph action; our controls prevent this collapse while retaining genuine reconstruction changes. Furthermore, our proposed method provides the practical, simple, and effective schemes for these applications, combining guaranteed convergence with explicit closed-form updates that can be applied directly to solve the original problems. We apply CBPL to graph-regularized sparse nonnegative matrix factorization with $\ell_0$-constraints ($\ell_0$-GSNMF), graph-regularized sparse nonnegative canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition with $\ell_0$-constraints ($\ell_0$-GSNCP), and graph-regularized sparse nonnegative independent-core matrix tri-factorization with $\ell_0$-constraints ($\ell_0$-GSNMTF). Numerical experiments demonstrate effectiveness, convergence and structural control.

papers.title: Semantic-Coupled Perception Framework for Autonomous Laparoscope Control
papers.abstract: In minimally invasive surgery (MIS), maintaining an appropriate field of view (FoV) is essential for surgical safety and efficiency. However, conventional autonomous laparoscope control methods often treat visual tracking and surgical phase recognition independently, limiting robustness under occlusion, entity overlap, and camera motion. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous laparoscope control framework that couples real-time surgical phase recognition with camera-motion-compensated visual perception. By exploiting phase-dependent relationships among surgical entities, the framework improves target state estimation under challenging visual conditions, supporting task-aware autonomous FoV control. Benchmark and phantom experiments evaluate the framework in surgical phase recognition, target tracking under occlusion and entity overlap, and autonomous FoV control, showing improved target visibility and task execution compared with fixed-FoV control. These results highlight the potential of incorporating task-level semantics into visual state estimation for autonomous laparoscope guidance.

papers.title: Detecting and Understanding Ambiguity in Visualizations with Role-Playing Vision Language Model Interpretations
papers.abstract: Communicative visualizations can support multiple chart-grounded takeaways, including divergent or conflicting ones; we refer to this variation as interpretive ambiguity. Such ambiguity can undermine a visualization's communicative goal when the supported takeaways diverge from its intended message. Evaluating visualizations with target audiences can surface this variation, but such evaluations can be costly and difficult to scale. In this work, we explore persona-conditioned Vision Language Models (VLMs) as a complementary evaluation tool for interpretive ambiguity. For a given visualization, our pipeline uses topic-relevant personas to elicit candidate contextual takeaways supported by interpretations of perceived visual patterns, such as trends and clusters. We derive a Target--Pattern--Scope framework for comparing these interpretations, use LLM judges to assign Compatible, Disjoint, or Opposing ambiguity labels to statement pairs, and summarize their distribution in an ambiguity profile. To improve chart grounding, we benchmark candidate VLMs on chart comprehension and select the highest-performing model for each chart type. We evaluate statement-pair labeling against human-authored annotations and apply the approach to real-world, public-facing visualizations curated from established datasets. Through case studies, we examine how perceived visual patterns relate to contextual takeaways and how a visualization redesign changes the sampled interpretations. Our findings show how persona-conditioned VLMs can complement human feedback by generating candidate contextual takeaways and surfacing potential ambiguity for further inspection.

papers.title: Observable Self-Restraint in Repeated Cheap Talk
papers.abstract: A long-lived sender seeks to persuade short-lived receivers to take his preferred action. Receivers observe his past advice but cannot verify its accuracy. Restrictions on recommendation histories alone can support a partially informative equilibrium. Under rolling quotas, which cap favorable recommendations within a fixed memory window, favorable advice is more costly when past favorable recommendations are more numerous or more recent. In an informative equilibrium, a violation can itself convey enough information about the current state for the receiver to follow the recommendation. After some sequences of states, the sender therefore breaks his own restriction, ending informative communication on the equilibrium path. As the sender becomes patient, suitable rolling quotas approach his normalized equilibrium payoff ceiling.

papers.title: Cutoff profile for the coupon collector with many collections
papers.abstract: We consider the problem posed by Erdős and Rényi in $1961$ about the limiting distribution of the number of draws $T_{n,m}$ that a coupon collector needs to complete $m$ collections of $n$ distinct types of coupons, when $m$ increases with $n$. Although the limiting distribution was studied in earlier works, we give a simple and self-contained proof that relates it to the cutoff phenomenon for an absorbing Markov chain. We also provide an alternative expression for the cutoff window in terms of the Lambert $W$ function.

papers.title: IRON-Meme: A Benchmark for Structured Understanding of Identities and Roles in Online Meme Narratives
papers.abstract: As polarization grows on social media, understanding how political memes shape online narratives has become increasingly important. Previous research has relied on either qualitative frameworks that are hard to scale or computational methods that lack theoretical grounding. Both approaches treat narrative categories in isolation and focus exclusively on moral portrayals of identity. To address these limitations, we introduce a framework grounded in social science theories, encompassing three categories: social identities (such as gender, politics, and ethnicity), viewpoints (ingroup and outgroup perspectives), and narrative roles (moral character, intelligence, appearance, and power). Building on this framework, we present IRON-Meme, a human-annotated benchmark comprising 1,110 political memes across substantially more templates than existing benchmarks. Our analysis of IRON-Meme shows that most memes assign derogatory roles and that identities, roles, and templates are systematically interconnected. Evaluation of nine vision-language models indicates that frontier-scale and reasoning models achieve the highest performance, while accuracy on social identities and narrative roles decreases for less frequent labels. Incorporating template background knowledge does not enhance narrative role classification, suggesting that meme interpretation relies on how memes are adapted for specific communicative purposes. We make IRON-Meme and our code publicly available.

papers.title: Measure Before You Train: Typed Decision Models vs. a Classical Baseline vs. a Generative LLM for Routing a Personal Multilingual Inbox
papers.abstract: Personal email agents decide, for every message, its type and urgency and whether to draft a reply, create a task or ignore it. In production these decisions are delegated to a generative LLM or to rules, and their error rate is rarely measured: the stored labels were written by the system itself. We describe Foyer, a self-hosted personal inbox agent, and a measurement protocol (stratified sampling, frozen snapshots, thread-grouped splits, secret redaction, human labels in the review loop) that produces ground truth before any training. On 231 emails in Italian and English we compare eleven systems: the stored production type, a TF-IDF + logistic-regression baseline, local and hosted typed decision models (Tev1, Nimble, Jeva, Jev) and generative LLMs. Four results. The stored production type scores 28% against a 57% majority class. With about two hundred labels a logistic regression has the highest point accuracy on every field (type 0.77 +/- 0.02 over five seeds) at a thousandth of the latency, but on every field at least one hosted model is statistically indistinguishable from it (exact McNemar, Holm-corrected). A generative model recovers part of the sender's relationship to the owner from the text (0.60); inheritance from the contact is right 98.6% of the time where the sender was seen before: it belongs in the contact graph, not in the prompt. Per-email accuracy is not the product metric: composed into actions, the classifier ignores 18% of the emails that needed action, against 4% for the best generative model; a cost-chosen threshold cuts that to 10%, indistinguishable from the hosted decision model's; on the adversarial corpus the thresholded classifier is the cheapest system above a missed-email price of 4. Two blind annotators agree with the reference at kappa 0.81 and 0.86 on type. v4 corrects threshold results computed on a truncated corpus in v1-v3.

papers.title: CauProphet: Teaching Agents to Develop Causal Cognition like Humans
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly support long-horizon tasks by leveraging external memory and past experience. However, existing agents mainly retrieve records or summaries, lacking the ability to form and refine causal understanding of the world. Inspired by human causal cognition, we introduce CauProphet, an agent that develops and updates causal knowledge within its Causal Cognition. For each task, CauProphet combines relevant knowledge in Causal Cognition with current evidence to construct a Causal Belief, a structured belief capturing causal factors and the effects of possible actions. It uses this belief for decision-making and continuously updates both the belief and Causal Cognition as new observations emerge, enabling causal knowledge that persists beyond individual experiences. Evaluations demonstrate that CauProphet progressively acquires causal knowledge and transfers it to future decision-making. In financial research, CauProphet leverages prior discoveries to improve downstream analyses and outperforms all baselines in mean rank correlation with next-day returns, achieving a 25.4% improvement over a baseline agent. It also improves prediction accuracy from 21.3% to 28.6% in dynamic real-world settings. Further experiments validate its ability to perform reliable causal analysis and action selection across scientific and everyday tasks, demonstrating the potential of causal experience learning for next-generation LLM agents. The project repository is available at https://github.com/OpenCausaLab/CauProphet.

papers.title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization for Targeted Structural Dynamic Vibration Attenuation
papers.abstract: Resonance-induced structural vibrations can compromise the performance, reliability, and service life of engineering structures. Multi-material topology optimization (MMTO) offers a promising approach to vibration attenuation by tailoring the spatial distributions of material constituents to optimize structural stiffness, mass, and natural frequencies. However, existing eigenfrequency-based MMTO methods face several challenges, including the need for flexible interpolation of multiple material properties, non-smooth optimization objectives associated with mode switching and repeated eigenvalues, and numerical difficulties in imposing differentiable constraints to exclude natural frequencies from prescribed operating frequency ranges. To address these challenges, we propose a novel MMTO framework for structural vibration attenuation based on several innovations: (1) a novel multivariate weight-based multi-material interpolation scheme to simultaneously represent material stiffness and mass density, (2) a bound-based optimization formulation to improve the smoothness and stability of gradient-based optimization by addressing mode switching, and (3) a smooth frequency-band formulation to smoothly approximate the discontinuous Heaviside function while enabling differentiable frequency-band constraints. Additionally, we systematically investigate and compare three different topology optimization formulations for dynamic vibration attenuation, including maximizing the fundamental eigenfrequency, maximizing the gap between adjacent eigenfrequencies, and excluding natural frequencies from prescribed frequency bands. Furthermore, we present the detailed derivation of analytical design sensitivities for the three formulations.

papers.title: Fermions Scattering Off Non-Abelian Rotors
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of $d=1+1$ chiral fermions interacting with a rotor impurity. The rotors are non-Abelian, taking values in either an $SU(N)$ group manifold, or an $SU(N)/SO(N)$ coset. At low energies, the fermions pass through the impurity, seemingly unimpeded, but trailing a topological line that is necessary for current conservation. In certain cases, these topological lines exhibit non-Abelian fusion and braiding. This can be viewed as a toy model that captures aspects of s-wave monopole-fermion scattering in $d=3+1$ dimensions.

papers.title: Onsager Algebras and Lattice Fermions
papers.abstract: We study the exact Onsager algebra of free lattice fermions in staggered, Wilson, and overlap incarnations, working in both Hamiltonian and Euclidean formulations in four spacetime dimensions. In each case, we show that the exact lattice algebra emanates the full chiral symmetry of the low-energy theory: if there are $N$ massless Dirac fermions in the continuum, the Onsager algebra reduces to a $U(2N)$ chiral symmetry. The details of which generators are quantised or ultra-local differ between formulations. There is also a trade-off between the locality of generators and the maximum compact subgroup of the Onsager algebra.

papers.title: Analytification and tropicalization via hyperfields and definable types
papers.abstract: We study the analytification and tropicalization of algebraic varieties over valued fields via Jun's spaces of hyperfield points. Our main new objects are a family of power-tropical hyperfields $H_n$ and their inverse limit $H$, recording at each level the class of a leading term modulo $n$-th powers of the residue field. They yield an enhanced tropicalization of the associated space $X(H)$, strictly finer than the Berkovich one exactly when the multiplicative group of the residue field is non-divisible: it specialises to the Berkovich analytification when the residue field is algebraically closed, to the real analytification of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu when it is real closed, and to a new $p$-adic analytification when it is $p$-adically closed. Over henselian valued fields of equicharacteristic $0$ we then construct a model-theoretic avatar of $X(H)$: the space $\widehat{X}_T$ of definable types orthogonal to the value group, which sharpens the geometry in the spirit of Hrushovski and Loeser and recovers their space over algebraically closed valued fields. We show that $\widehat{X}_T$ is strictly pro-definable, satisfies a model-theoretic Payne theorem, and definable compactness in such spaces satisfies a Heine-Borel type characterization. As an application, we analytify $p$-adic semi-algebraic sets and prove a strong density theorem for their tropicalizations, the exact $p$-adic counterpart of the real one of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu.

papers.title: Density Constraints Overcome the Energy-Density Trade-Off in Exchange-Correlation Functionals
papers.abstract: Exchange--correlation functionals are trained mainly on energies, and their densities often degrade as their energies improve. We present a supervised-learning algorithm that trains functionals on energies and accurate densities without self-consistent-field (SCF) solutions. From one Fock build at a fixed accurate density, it predicts the density that the functional would reach self-consistently and penalizes its deviation from the reference; for functionals linear in their parameters, training is convex. Refitting the MN15 form to 1,500 reaction energies under a constraint on 98 coupled-cluster densities gives the density-constrained hybrid DCH-D4. On 19 held-out energy sets its mean normalized error ratio is 0.96, against 1.76 for MN15, and on 145 densities outside the fit its mean density error is 22 times lower than that of MN15. Deep-learning neural GGA and meta-GGA functionals (NN-GGA and NN-mGGA) trained on only 6 energies and 11 densities lower the atomization-energy error on 103 molecules from 14.6 to 5.6~kcal/mol relative to PBE and from 3.7 to 3.3~kcal/mol relative to SCAN, while roughly halving the density error of each base functional. Accurate densities can thus enter functional training at the scale of modern energy databases.

papers.title: Unintended Side Effects of Value Training in LLMs
papers.abstract: As LLMs are increasingly deployed in value-sensitive contexts, aligning them with human values has emerged as a post-training objective in NLP, aimed at instilling additional values and guiding model behaviour. However, current evaluations remain narrow. Because values are interconnected, it is unclear how fine-tuning for specific values alters unrelated capabilities and behaviours. In this work, we adapt four instruction-tuned LLMs across individual Hofstede's value dimensions and evaluate them on both cross-value transfer and broader behaviours. We find that value-specific training produces unintended side effects on untrained values, risk preferences, social cognition, and safety traits. Consequently, we suggest that value alignment after post-training should incorporate broader behavioral evaluations, and we highlight the need to investigate where additional value training might best fit into the pipeline. We release all 48 value-tuned model checkpoints at https://huggingface.co/sidicity/cultural-value-models

papers.title: Improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri Inequalities under Constraints: Sharpness and Quantitative Remainders
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities on the sphere under moment constraints, with particular emphasis on sharp leading constants and quantitative remainder terms. For the Sobolev inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequality of Hang and Wang [30] (Int. Math. Res. Not., 2022) to a sharp one at $p=2$ under vanishing moment constraints of orders $m=1,2,3$. We also prove a general failure principle: if the unconstrained sharp Sobolev inequality fails, then the corresponding sharp improved inequality under moment constraints fails as well. For the Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequalities of Chang and Hang [10] and Hang [29] (Comm. Pure Appl. Math., 2022) to a sharp improved inequality at the critical order $s=\frac{n}{2}$ under arbitrary finite-order moment constraints. We further investigate the best remainder constant. In contrast with the two-dimensional first-moment case of Gui and Moradifam [28] (Invent. Math., 2018), where the best remainder vanishes, we show that it is positive in several higher-dimensional regimes. We also obtain quantitative remainder estimates for general almost sharp improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities, which in turn yield sharp inequalities at different scales. We further extend recent second-moment refinements to higher dimensions and higher orders. Finally, we obtain analogous results on sharpness, non-sharpness, and quantitative remainder estimates for improved Sobolev-type inequalities under symmetry constraints on general smooth closed manifolds.

papers.title: Flux-Based Time Bounds for Harmonically Degenerate Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: We study transfer-time estimates for finite-dimensional bilinear quantum control systems driven by an unbounded scalar control, in both the state-to-state setting (complex projective space) and the unitary synthesis setting (special unitary group). Lower bounds are recalled and refined via spectral and chordal methods. The main contribution is constructive upper bounds: we associate with the system a coupling graph whose edges correspond to non-resonant drift couplings, and construct transfer protocols along spanning trees. In contrast with earlier results requiring full rational independence of the spectrum of the control operator, our estimates allow rational resonances; they incorporate, via explicit correction factors derived from the arithmetic of the spectral gaps, the efficiency of the averaging procedure and of the phase adjustments. As an application, we consider finite-dimensional truncations of the planar quantum rotator under a dipolar electric field, and show that the transfer time between any two modes tends to zero as the truncation dimension grows.

papers.title: Global regularity and sharp decay rates for the one-dimensional hypo-viscous compressible Navier-Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the global regularity for the one-dimensional hypo-viscous compressible Navier-Stokes equations in the critical Besov spaces, where the initial data are close to the constant equilibrium state. We introduce an effective velocity, constructed as a combination of the density and the velocity, which is used to capture the high-frequency behavior of $a$. By performing elaborate high-frequency and low-frequency estimates together with a bootstrap argument, we obtain global existence for $\frac{1}{2}\leβ<1$. In particular, when $β=\frac{1}{2}$, we also prove the system is well-posed in critical space. Furthermore, under an additional low-frequency assumption, we establish the optimal time decay rates.

papers.title: Scalar fields in the background of a linear Vaidya spacetime
papers.abstract: We study, in a semiclassical, quasi-stationary approximation, the entanglement properties of massless scalar fields near the event horizon of a dynamical black hole modeled by an ingoing Vaidya metric with a linearly decaying mass. In the near-horizon limit, the geometry becomes conformally equivalent to an eternal black hole, allowing the use of modular theory to analyze vacuum entanglement. We first study the modifications to the entanglement across the bifurcation surface of such a black hole from that of an eternal one. The conformal factor accounting for the evaporation modifies the Bogoliubov transformation between global modes and modes across the bifurcate Killing horizon of the black hole, inducing a phase in the thermofield-double-like structure of the global vacuum. This phase change of the vacuum state is a consequence of the adiabatic shift of the horizon. A quantitative measure of the entanglement change due to the phase is obtained through the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. We compare the CHSH inequalities in the vacuum states for the static and the linear Vaidya black holes and find that the CHSH correlation quantity for the latter is decreased by a factor dependent on the evaporation rate. Next, we discuss the analysis of the linear Vaidya black hole formed from gravitational collapse. For this purpose we adapt an analysis by Wald for the case of the Schwarzschild black hole. The entangled global vacuum again has a thermofield double structure. However, we find, as expected, the near-horizon structure and state do not approach that of the eternal black hole. Rather, the thermal factor is modified by a factor incorporating the change in the black hole mass due to evaporation.

papers.title: HAVANA: A Hierarchical Video-Action Model for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires long-horizon instruction-consistent planning and short-horizon path planning grounded in the currently observed geometry. Anticipating how future observations evolve along the instructed route provides predictive guidance beyond the current field of view, motivating video-action models (VAMs) that learn representations of future visual states. However, many existing VAMs couple future visual prediction with action generation during inference, despite their distinct temporal requirements: instruction-conditioned route guidance can be reused across multiple control steps, whereas local trajectories must continuously adapt to fresh observations. To bridge this gap, we introduce HAVANA, a dual-system VAM that decouples predictive reasoning from reactive local planning. A slow system produces a compact language-conditioned latent plan from observation history, while a fast system combines the latest plan with the current observation to generate local trajectories. Their asynchronous execution enables rapid adaptation without repeated future prediction, and no future video is generated during inference. Experiments on OmniNavBench demonstrate state-of-the-art navigation performance over prior baselines, while zero-shot real-world deployments further show robust generalization to unseen environments.

papers.title: AVC-Reward: Event-Centric Audio-Video Consistency Evaluation
papers.abstract: As joint audio-video generation models become more capable, they can generate audio-visual scenes exhibiting three forms of complexity: multi-event composition, multi-layer audio mixture, and asymmetric cross-modal relations. However, current evaluations largely reuse metrics from earlier simple and unidirectional tasks. They typically evaluate an audio-video clip as a whole and rely on simple predefined relations, making them unsuitable for these increasingly complex scenes. We propose an event-centric evaluation framework that disentangles audio and visual events at the event level, analyzes each event independently, cross-validates relations across modalities, and aggregates the judgments into a coarse-to-fine, three-level consistency metric. The metric assesses global narrative harmony, event-level temporal synchronization, and fine-grained attribute alignment, providing a general formulation for audio-video consistency evaluation across diverse generation settings and cross-modal relations. We instantiate the metric as AVC-Reward, a trainable audio-video reward model. To evaluate the agreement between automatic judgments and human perception across generation paradigms and relation complexities, we construct AVC-Benchmark, which is primarily built from diverse positive and negative samples generated by various types of audio-video generation models. AVC-Reward achieves state-of-the-art alignment with human judgment among automatic methods, provides interpretable rationales that localize failures, and improves the audio-video consistency of a joint generation model when used as an online reinforcement-learning signal. Project page: https://tsuki0512.github.io/AVC-Reward.github.io/

papers.title: Variation of Shafarevich-Tate groups in Hida families
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{f}$ be a Hida family of cusp forms over a standard (power series) Iwasawa algebra. We determine the pseudo-isomorphism class of the big Shafarevich-Tate group attached to $\mathbf{f}$ over a suitable imaginary quadratic field by describing all its higher Fitting ideals; this description is given in terms of the universal Kolyvagin system of Howard's big Heegner points. As a second contribution, we study the variation of the structure of the Shafarevich-Tate groups of the classical specializations of $\mathbf{f}$.

papers.title: The role of distributed friction dynamics on heave-induced motion of offshore drilling systems: modelling, analysis, and simulations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the influence of friction dynamics on heave-induced disturbance propagation using a coupled hydraulic-structural drilling model formulated as a semilinear interconnection of ordinary and hyperbolic partial differential equations (ODE-PDEs), and capturing spatially distributed memory effects in the drillstring-wellbore interaction. First, local and global existence and uniqueness results are established, and sufficient conditions for boundedness and input-to-state stability are deduced via a small-gain analysis. Subsequently, extensive numerical investigations are carried out, including harmonic excitation studies, nonlinear distortion analysis, spatial amplification investigations, mechanism-isolation experiments, parameter sensitivity analysis, and broadband simulations under realistic offshore sea-state excitation. The simulation results indicate that, whilst the hydraulic response is governed primarily by wave propagation phenomena, compressibility, and boundary reflections, the structural dynamics display substantially greater sensitivity to distributed friction effects. Furthermore, drillstring-wellbore friction is shown to have a relatively limited influence on well-posedness but a potentially significant impact on stability margins. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for coupled hydraulic-structural dynamics and distributed friction mechanisms when analysing, monitoring, and controlling offshore drilling systems.

papers.title: SurgStreamer: proactive, request-driven monitoring of surgical video streams with structured state and a reusable reasoning layer
papers.abstract: Surgical teams could benefit from assistants that watch the video for requested events, such as "tell me when the clip applier appears during Calot triangle dissection", and answer questions about what has already happened. We formalise this task as request-driven event detection with exact semantics and causal alert decisions, and present SurgStreamer. It separates procedure-specific perception, which maps the 1-FPS stream to a structured state over tools, actions and phases, from procedure-agnostic reasoning, which evaluates a formal monitoring condition over this state and an event memory, either with exact rules or with a small controller that addresses entities through pointers rather than names. We evaluate this monitoring core with gold conditions. On a pre-registered, sealed test set of 12 laparoscopic cholecystectomies, SurgStreamer reached a macro event-F1 of 0.598 over full procedures. On identical 75-s windows with only the window available to every method, it scored 0.677. The tested configurations of the streaming vision-language model OneStreamer-4B, including ones fine-tuned on SurgStreamer's state or on video with an adapted vision encoder, scored at most 0.540 (Holm-adjusted p <= 0.012). At three external centres, re-training only perception raised performance on held-out procedures from 0.239 to 0.470. On a new procedure, pituitary surgery, controller weights trained on cholecystectomy matched an in-domain controller on oracle state (0.947 vs 0.938). On predicted state they missed the pre-registered non-inferiority margin (-0.024 [-0.040, -0.008]) unless the alert thresholds were re-calibrated. The results support separating perception from reasoning and point to perception under distribution shift as the main limitation.

papers.title: A perturbation theory for Feynman-Kac models and their particle interpretations
papers.abstract: We develop a perturbation analysis of Feynman--Kac models, describing how local errors introduced at each step of the Feynman--Kac recursion propagate over time. Under general conditions on the potential functions and the Markov transitions, which are shown to hold for a large class of state-space models, we prove that the global error for any time horizon $T\geq 1$ is bounded by $C\,Δ_T\log(1+Δ_T^{-1})$, where $Δ_T$ is the largest local error; this bound holds both for the prediction and the updated models. These conditions require no Lyapunov function and no stability of the Markov transitions, and allow for non-compact state spaces: confinement is provided by the potential functions. Our perturbation bounds hold in total variation and in the Kolmogorov norm; for the latter, we extend the Hardy--Krause variation and the Koksma--Hlawka inequality to unbounded domains. Our perturbation theory is applied to derive time-uniform bounds for linearized Kalman filters, Euler schemes for partially observed diffusions and nudged state-space models, as well as high-probability error bounds, uniform over whole trajectories, for particle filters and, more generally, for mean field particle methods such as sequential Monte Carlo and diffusion Monte Carlo algorithms.

papers.title: Infinite-variation Lévy processes are either strongly eroded or abrupt
papers.abstract: We prove that every real Lévy process of infinite variation is either abrupt or strongly eroded, resolving the conjectured geometric dichotomy on the smoothness of the convex hull of the graph of a Lévy path [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Probab. Stat. 60(4) (2024), 2352-2381]. We give counterexamples to the stronger point-hitting conjecture of Vigon. As applications, we classify convex-hull smoothness, Lipschitz-minorant contact sets and Burgers shock geometry.

papers.title: Read, Parse, Describe: Unified Document Parsing with Visual Element Description Generation
papers.abstract: Document understanding systems are typically evaluated as separate components via layout analysis, optical text recognition, reading-order prediction, and image captioning. This separation leaves scientific figures, captions, and visual semantics weakly connected, and fails to measure whether a model can produce a single page-level parse that is both structurally faithful and semantically accessible. We introduce Read-Parse-Describe, a unified dataset for document parsing with visual element description generation. Given a page image, models are required to output an ordered list of layout elements containing bounding boxes, semantic labels, reading-order indices, recognized textual content, and alternative text descriptions for visual elements. The benchmark is built from 2,402 documents, comprising 18,163 continuous pages, 125,218 layout elements, and 11,338 visual instances. Besides, we further propose a plug-and-play space-awareness enhancer that reuses multi-layer visual features and injects grid-aware spatial guidance into vision-language tokens for layout-aware generation. Experiments across end-to-end VLMs and pipeline parsers show that existing systems still struggle to jointly recover reading order and visual semantics, while our enhanced model achieves strong joint performance. These results highlight the need to move beyond isolated document parsing modules toward unified models that jointly read, parse, and describe complex documents. The new dataset and code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yuheng98chen/RPD-Unidoc

papers.title: The minimal width of neural networks and immersions of real projective space
papers.abstract: We investigate the minimal width of deep neural networks that can approximate all continuous functions from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^m$ in the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets. We show that whenever the real projective space $\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$ admits a smooth immersion into $\mathbb{R}^n$, the minimal width is at least $n+\min\{n,m\}$, assuming that the activation function is continuous and monotone. As a consequence, the minimal width of ReLU networks is $n+m$ whenever $n$ is equal to 2, 3, 4, 7 or 8 and $1\le m \le n$, extending results of Hanin-Sellke and Hwang.

papers.title: Probing Coherent Noise with Stabilizer Codes: Identifiability, Ambiguity, and Decoder Priors
papers.abstract: Coherent noise calls for a reusable physical model, but Pauli twirling erases it and full process tomography scales exponentially. We turn measurement-free quantum error correction into a probe: bit-flip and phase-flip codes polarize few-qubit coherent noise into single-logical-qubit channels, and the resulting fingerprint identifies an 11-parameter three-qubit family. An exact rational-arithmetic rank certificate, evaluated at a rational point in the interior of the parameter domain, proves local injectivity on a dense open subset of that domain. The map is nevertheless not globally injective: a compensating rotation combined with a site exchange yields exact collisions, which we classify and then remove by adding one two-qubit marginal channel. The site exchange is the only nontrivial permutation symmetry of the $n$-qubit chain generator at any $n$, so the classification is structural rather than a three-qubit accident. A Cramér--Rao analysis, checked at the level of individual measurement settings, reaches $0.01$~rad per parameter at a representative point for shot noise alone, and fixes the condition under which that number survives a non-unitary component: a stochastic part of total probability $p$ contributes a model error $8.4p$ in fingerprint norm that no number of shots removes, so the quoted precision presupposes $p\lesssim10^{-3}$; decoder priors rebuilt from such an estimate retain most of their correlation gain. Propagating the generator into a distance-three surface code gives a $14.8$-fold encoding gain when the generator is known exactly, and $1.21$-fold of the correlation gain survives when the prior is rebuilt from an estimate at the stated precision, closing the loop from characterization to decoding.

papers.title: Beyond the Trial-and-Error Loop: Hybrid Projection and Automated Tuning for Distributed Training
papers.abstract: Configuring distributed LLM training across hundreds of GPUs requires jointly optimizing tensor, pipeline, expert, context, and data parallelism alongside micro-batch size, recomputation, sharding, and overlap, a combinatorial space where memory legality can hinge on a single byte of activation accounting. Today, teams navigate it through expensive multi-node trial and error, burning GPU-hours on crashes and suboptimal recipes. We present Primus Projection, which closes this loop with two coupled components. First, a hybrid projection engine that measures what it can and simulates what it cannot: GPU microbenchmarks on as few as a single device capture compute kernels and any in-scope communication; a sub-node downscale-measure-upscale workflow analytically restores out-of-scope collectives, FSDP overlap, and the full pipeline schedule at the multi-node target. A pure simulation mode runs entirely on CPU, enabling pre-silicon planning without any GPU. Second, the Primus Tuning Agent treats the projection engine as a fast scoring oracle (seconds per candidate instead of tens of minutes) and uses it to drive an intelligent search over the configuration space. A deterministic seed planner sweeps single axes; an LLM investigation loop proposes cross-axis combinations the planner cannot reach, with an analytic memory pre-filter that rejects infeasible candidates before any GPU time is spent. Validated on Llama 3.1 (dense) and Mixtral 8x22B (MoE) across two GPU generations, all projections stay within ~10% of measured multi-node throughput, and fidelity holds at production scale: 4.7% error on DeepSeek V3 671B at 1,024 GPUs and 1.9% on Qwen3-235B-A22B at 256 GPUs. In a Mixtral 8x22B case study, the Primus Tuning Agent discovers a configuration delivering +27% throughput over the published 4-node BF16 reference at the same scale, in under 30 minutes of single-node exploration.

papers.title: Program Learning with Verifiable Rewards: Distilling Expert Traces into Programs
papers.abstract: Small language models struggle with tool-use tasks that require following multi-step procedures. Whether these failures reflect limited capability or missing procedural knowledge remains unclear. We introduce Program Learning with Verifiable Rewards (PLVR), which distils expert traces into reusable programs without updating model weights. Frontier models turn recurring operations in the traces into typed primitives and rules, and search assembles them using reference actions and training-task checks. A small frozen model executes the primitives, with deterministic verifiers checking their outputs. The resulting program guides a student's reasoning or checks its proposed actions. We evaluate the same program across students on $τ^2$-Bench Retail and Telecom and LiveMCPBench, using synthetic training tasks and unseen benchmark test tasks. On Telecom, PLVR raises an 8B model's success rate from 43.0% to 91.2%, while larger students reach up to 94.4%, compared with 57.9% for the best baseline. On Retail and LiveMCPBench, PLVR is competitive with the best baselines, although tool search remains more dependent on the student model. These results support program learning as a way to transfer expert procedures across frozen models, trading additional inference computation for more reliable tool use.

papers.title: Structured coordinate systems in $L^p(\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: We construct Schauder bases of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ with significant structural constraints on their elements. For every $1 \leq p< \infty$, we obtain bases of non-negative functions with basis constants arbitrarily close to one, as well as bases with positive biorthogonal functionals. For every $2 \leq p < \infty$, we construct Schauder bases consisting of translates of a single function, which can be chosen to extend to an entire function. When $p>2$, the translation parameters can be chosen from any prescribed unbounded subset of $\mathbb{R}$, a conclusion that fails for $p=2$. Finally, for $p>2$, the entire function generating the basis of translates can also be chosen non-negative.

papers.title: Existence and Uniqueness Proof for the Transport Equation and the Orthogonal Dynamics Equation for Zwanzig's Projection on Gaussian Spaces: A Vanishing Viscosity Method
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of unique solutions ${u\in H^1(0,T;L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))}$ of the transport equation $u_t=F\cdot\nabla u+f$ and the orthogonal dynamics equation ${u_t= Q_\text{Z} (F\cdot\nabla) Q_\text{Z} u+f}$, where $F$ is a time-independent vector field, $f$ is a forcing term, $P_\text{Z}=1-Q_\text{Z}$ is a Zwanzig projection (conditional expectation) on $L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n)$ defined by $P_\text{Z}h \propto \int h(\cdot ,y) ρ(\cdot,y)\rm{d}y$, and $γ$ is the standard Gaussian measure with density $ρ$. To this end, we develop a vanishing viscosity method based on the maximal regularity theory for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator on $L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The following assumptions guarantee the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions: ${f\in H^1(0,T;L^2_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_γ(\mathbb{R}^n))}$, ${g\in H^1_γ(\mathbb{R}^n)}$, $F\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $\rm{ess\,sup}_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left(x\cdot F-\rm{div}F\right) < \infty$, where $g$ denotes the initial value function.

papers.title: Under what conditions can coupling disorder render qubit dynamics CP-divisible in a finite spin bath?
papers.abstract: We investigate whether unresolved quasi-static Gaussian disorder in system--bath coupling can make finite spin-bath dynamics CP-divisible. The coupling varies between shots but is fixed within each, yielding a disorder-averaged tomographic map. For a single-spin Ising $ZZ$ bath with a fixed initial state, disorder can induce a polarization-dependent transition to CP-divisibility. A bath fully polarized along the longitudinal direction ($|m_z|=1$) yields CP-divisible dynamics irrespective of disorder, whereas zero longitudinal polarization or Haar-sampled bath states fluctuating independently of the coupling between shots preserve CP-indivisibility at any finite disorder strength for nonzero mean coupling. We extend this analytically to inhomogeneous Ising baths of any finite size $N$. For factorized bath preparations, one spin with zero longitudinal polarization and nonzero mean coupling suffices to retain CP-indivisibility at finite disorder. Strong disorder can render partially polarized baths CP-divisible. For homogeneous baths, the critical disorder ratio is independent of $N$. When bath states fluctuate physically between shots, independent Haar sampling preserves CP-indivisibility for finite $N$ if any mean coupling is nonzero. For a single-spin anisotropic Heisenberg bath, any nonzero transverse exchange preserves trace-distance backflow at finite disorder for every fixed preparation, provided the mean coupling is nonzero. Exact diagonalization up to $N=12$ shows trace-distance revivals for a fully polarized bath, in Haar averages over fixed product bath states, and for fluctuating bath states. Transverse exchange and physical bath-state fluctuations with zero average longitudinal polarization preserve CP-indivisibility at finite disorder. Yet increasing disorder can make trace-distance revivals experimentally unresolvable, making the dynamics appear Markovian.

papers.title: Mergers may not be the main channel for galaxy stellar mass growth at redshift $z\gtrsim5$: Predictions from cosmological hierarchical models and simulations
papers.abstract: Mergers are a crucial channel of galaxy growth, but their role relative to star formation remains uncertain at high redshift. Here we investigate merger rates and merger-driven stellar mass assembly for galaxies with stellar mass $M_\star \gtrsim 10^8 \, {\rm M_{\odot}}$ at $z\simeq 5-11$, by combining complementary theoretical approaches within $Λ$CDM. These include the DECODE semi-empirical model, the TNG100 and EAGLE hydrodynamical simulations, and the \textsc{L-Galaxies} semi-analytical model, together with the Millennium and TNG100-Dark simulations used to examine dark matter subhalo statistics and merger timescales. This compares models with different treatments of baryonic physics and galaxy-halo connections. We find that dark matter-only simulations predict merger timescales $\sim 30\%$ longer than those inferred from cosmological simulations including baryons. Galaxy major merger ($M_{\rm \star,sat} / M_{\rm \star,cen} > 0.25$) rates show a substantial model- and mass-dependent redshift evolution. Despite high rates, mergers contribute only $\lesssim 10\%$ to the total cosmic stellar mass density evolution. The average ex-situ stellar mass fraction ranges from a few percent to $\sim 25\%$ for all stellar mass bins at $z\gtrsim 5$, across different models and simulations. Their broad agreement implies that stellar mass assembly at cosmic dawn is dominated by in-situ star formation rather than mergers. These findings suggest that the high pair fractions identified by JWST may not directly trace efficient ex-situ stellar mass growth, highlighting the need for physically motivated merger timescales to interpret galaxy assembly in the early Universe.

papers.title: A Scaled-Up Empirical Study of Syntactic Language Models
papers.abstract: Syntactic language models (SLMs) that generate sentences along with their syntactic tree structures have shown promise in both syntactic generalization and downstream tasks. Prior studies, however, have mostly evaluated smaller models trained on less pretraining data and tested on narrower task suites. In addition, the design space of tree linearization and attention masks remains underexplored. We conduct a large-scale empirical study of 12 controlled configurations---one terminal baseline and 11 SLM variants spanning different linearizations and masks---at scales up to 1B parameters and 100B training tokens, evaluated across 11 downstream tasks and two syntactic benchmarks. The experimental results show that SLMs with standard causal attention match or exceed structural-mask variants across downstream and syntactic benchmarks. They require no architectural modifications and remain compatible with FlashAttention. We also observe that when scaling up to the 1B-parameter scale, the top-performing SLM variant no longer shows a clear advantage over a compute-matched non-structural baseline, suggesting that SLMs may become less competitive with scale. Our code is available at https://github.com/qlwpc/TG-Interpolation.

papers.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
papers.abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.

papers.title: Time-Frequency Continuous-Variable Quantum Teleportation with Single Photons
papers.abstract: Quantum teleportation, a key building block for quantum technologies, enables distant parties, Alice and Bob, to transfer an unknown quantum state using entanglement, local operations, and classical communication. In this work, we propose a quantum teleportation protocol for single-photon time-frequency continuous variables, where time is the time of arrival at a detector. We detail the operational requirements of the protocol, notably the nonlinear interactions needed for the photon-photon time-frequency entangling gate. By explicitly treating the detector position as the reference frame for time of arrival, we show that, even with ideal classical and quantum channels, the input-output fidelity is not unity unless the receiving party can correct the detector-position mismatch. This results in a trade-off between teleportation fidelity and the temporal bandwidth of the input photon wavepacket. The protocol itself can be used for remote detector synchronization. In particular, we show that time-frequency cat and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states provide an internal temporal ruler through fidelity revivals. We further derive the classical and best-copy fidelity thresholds for single-photon Gaussian wavepackets, finding that the relevant vacuum-equivalent shot noise is input-dependent, in contrast with quadrature-based continuous-variable quantum teleportation. Our proposal derives from a quantum theory of space-time events, whereafter we establish space as a reference for the time degree of freedom, thereby grounding our work in ongoing research on reference frames and superselection rules in quantum optics and quantum information. Beyond protocols harnessing time-frequency continuous variables of single photons, this work points toward remote synchronization in quantum communication architectures.

papers.title: Where Polanyi Meets Galois: Tacit Knowing as an Algebro-Deterministic Operation, Toward Re-rooting AI-Generated Science
papers.abstract: Tacit knowing is an operating regime of one memory substrate, not a separate kind of content. In VaCoAl (CASRAM, PyVaCoAl), an algebro-deterministic hyperdimensional memory over GF(2), one DAG of bound records is read in two ways. With every collision repaired (Rescue), the trace is exactly auditable but no path outranks another; with collisions tolerated (Don't Care), a path-integrated confidence $CR_2$ ranks direct over circuitous routes without being stated. This audit-valuation complementarity formalizes Polanyi's claim that tacit and explicit knowledge are not sharply divided. (1) Polanyi's from-to structure reads as non-commutative binding. (2) Full explication destroys the valuation (Lemma 1), as with Polanyi's pianist; tacitness is contingent or regime-bound, placing Polanyi, Nonaka, Tsoukas and Collins on one substrate. (3) The same lemma answers the popular dual-process moral ("train slow System 2 to tame fast System 1"), which mirrors the two-store reading of knowledge Polanyi rejected; Mercier and Sperber's reply, that reasoning is intuitive inference about reasons, matches his. (4) To know a large DAG is to cull it. Simon answered Polanyi's Meno argument: a test and a generator suffice. The AlphaGo-to-AlphaProof lineage builds that answer, yet a checker audits an endpoint and values no path: the tacit is relocated, not removed, and results are verified yet rootless. (5) Collins's three tacit knowledges map to bound structure, substrate valuation and value binding. (6) Our mentor-student DAG charts tacit transmission. (7) AI-solved problems with few follow-ups (Tao) are rootless explicit knowledge, re-rooted when LLMs generate, VaCoAl keeps the trace and the community values. (8) On Mercier and Sperber's theory an LLM is a sophist; truth-seeking lies in collective tacit knowing, Polanyi's conviviality, which we conjecture extends beyond humans. Testable predictions follow.

papers.title: Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Galerkin Solvers for Elliptic Partial Differential Equations on Curved Geometries with Hardware Validation
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum solvers measure time-evolved Krylov states and solve the problem classically on the observed basis states. We develop this approach for the positive-definite linear systems of elliptic partial differential equations. A Galerkin solve on the sampled Fourier modes gives the solution. We derive energy-norm error bounds that connect the measured outcome law to the solution error, a sample complexity, and a support-completeness theorem. The theorem shows that time averaging recovers solution modes that are hidden from every selection based on the source. For curved cross sections we give a constructive procedure: conformal coordinates fix the matrix class, isometries of the cross section give postselection rules that keep every solution mode, and the Lie derivative of the metric bounds the error from geometric uncertainty. We apply the method to pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts and to non-separable problems with up to 16 qubits. On 16 qubits the sampler reaches 0.2% error with 3% of the Fourier modes, while a selection from the source stalls at 13% error.
