Deposited and transferred particle fluences were calculated for this coating and all particle species, and the total ionizing dose (TID) in each layer was derived with GRAS. The selected coating will not be affected by corpuscular radiation for years in the ISS LEO environment, and the TID expected at the ISS Bartolomeo platform will not affect its optical properties.

papers.title: Nagata dimension, separation modulus and stochastic embeddings into trees
papers.abstract: The separation modulus of a metric space, introduced by Bartal in 1996, is related to different notions of dimensionality. Most generally, Naor and Silberman gave in 2011 an upper bound on the separation modulus in terms of Nagata dimension. We prove that this bound cannot be reversed; that is, there are metric spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension and stochastically embeddable into trees with uniform distortion, which therefore have uniformly bounded separation modulus. Similarly, we construct spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension whose spaces of probability measures endowed with the Earth Mover's Distance (equivalently, their Lipschitz-free spaces) are embeddable into $L_1$ with uniformly bounded distortion. By gluing these spaces together, we obtain infinite Nagata dimensional metric spaces whose separation modulus is finite and whose Lipschitz-free space is isomorphic to $\ell_1$, respectively. Finally, we provide relations between separation modulus and stochastic embeddability into trees, also known as random approximability by tree metrics, in particular for the case of snowflake metrics.

papers.title: Splitting Number at Singular Cardinals
papers.abstract: We study the splitting number at singular cardinals with emphasis on what we call the reduction to the cofinality problem: whether $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}$ holds for a singular cardinal $κ$. Our main tool is the transfinite logarithm function $\mathrm{log}_{2}(μ) := \min \{ λ\in \mathrm{card} \colon μ\leq 2^λ \}$ defined for every infinite cardinal $μ$. We prove that the reduction holds, and in fact $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathrm{log}_{2}(\mathrm{cf}(κ))$, whenever $\mathrm{cf}(κ)$ is uncountable and not weakly compact. When $\mathrm{cf}(κ) = \aleph_{0}$, we show that $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathfrak{s}$ provided that $\mathfrak{s} \leq \log_{2}(κ)$, while the failure of the reduction is consistent with $\mathrm{ZFC}$. When $\mathrm{cf}(κ)$ is weakly compact, we use a model constructed by Ben-Neria and Gitik to prove that, under suitable large cardinals hypothesis, $\mathfrak{s}_κ < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}$ is consistent. Furthermore, we show that the consistency strength of $\mathrm{ZFC} \, +$"$\exists κ\in \mathrm{card} [\mathrm{cf}(κ) > \aleph_{0} \wedge \mathfrak{s}_κ < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}]$'' is at least that of the negation of the singular cardinal hypothesis. Finally, we study the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}_κ$, extending several results about the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}$ to the uncountable setting. In particular, we show in $\mathrm{ZFC}$ that there are regular cardinals $κ$ such that $\mathfrak{s}_κ$ is singular, partially answering an open question posed by Fischer and Soukup.

papers.title: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models
papers.abstract: In September 2026, TypeSafe announced Jev as the first model in its System One category: unstructured state goes in, and typed, calibrated decisions that software can use directly come out. Jev's architecture and training data are unpublished, but many open typed-decision models have followed, including Nimble, the Decision 1.0-3.0 family and Clef. They answer structured questions about a piece of text, such as a yes/no check, a choice among labelled options or a graded score, by reading the text with a language model and scoring the options with a small readout. Each pairs a different readout with a different backbone, training mix and recipe, so it is unclear which design choices matter. We re-implement five readouts and train all of them under one protocol: the same backbone, the same 15 public English training sources, the same recipe with a per-head learning-rate sweep, and the same seed. Our experiments demonstrate that: The complexity of the head does not affect accuracy: on Qwen3-0.6B every readout reaches 81.3-82.0% in-domain accuracy, and a 0.5M-parameter cosine head, which scores each option by its cosine similarity to the question, matches the 27M-parameter joint schema head adapted from Clef in-domain at half its inference time. Reading all of a text's questions from one prompt also matches one prompt per question in accuracy, with 1.6 times faster inference and 2.1-2.5 times faster training on one H100. The backbone's size matters more than either choice: moving from Qwen3-0.6B to Qwen3-4B adds 4 points in-domain and 11 points on held-out sources, while the base, instruct and thinking checkpoints of the same model tie. We recommend spending effort on the backbone and keeping the head minimal.

papers.title: Loyalty Capture: Reporting Relationships and Structural Sycophancy in Frontier AI Models
papers.abstract: We show that AI models exhibit loyalty capture, a form of structural sycophancy in which reporting relationships influence models' recommendations to serve the personal interests of their supervisors, without any explicit instruction, user feedback, or adversarial prompting. Specifically, models reporting to a CEO are significantly more likely to recommend cutting investment spending when the CEO's bonus depends on raising current period earnings. This effect is predictably absent from a metric-irrelevant placebo. The behavior appears consistent with loyalty-based motivated reasoning: models identify the bonus target, calculate how their recommendation helps achieve the target, and dismiss considerations of long-term value, often presenting their recommendations without treating the incentive as a conflict of interest. Prompt-based interventions help whereas generic conflict disclosures or stakeholder bargaining fail to eliminate it. Taken together, our findings indicate that AI models deployed within reporting relationships can act in favor of their supervisor's incentives at the expense of the organizations they are meant to serve.

papers.title: Finite Element Approximation of Three-Dimensional Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Curve-Supported Controls
papers.abstract: We consider a linear-quadratic elliptic optimal control problem in three dimensions with a box-constrained control supported on a compact embedded $C^{1,1}$ curve strictly contained in a bounded convex polyhedral domain. The right-hand side of the state equation is a measure supported on the curve, and the state is singular along it. We establish well-posedness and first-order optimality conditions and derive curve-adapted weighted inequalities and finite element error estimates for the singular state. For continuous piecewise linear finite elements on quasi-uniform tetrahedral meshes and variational discretization of the control, assuming exact integration over the curve, we prove the almost quadratic estimate $\|\bar q-\bar q_h\|_{L^2(γ)}\le Ch^2(1+\abs{\ln h})^3$. The proof of this estimate requires new results, which are of independent interest. The convergence rate observed in a numerical experiment is consistent with the predicted algebraic order.

papers.title: LHAASO's Peanut source is a laboratory for studying magnetic fields in the Milky Way
papers.abstract: Recently, the LHAASO Collaboration reported gamma-ray emission from the Peanut-shaped source (Peanut), which extends over $4.5^\circ$ parallel to the Galactic plane at $b=-17.5^\circ$. The source is associated with the millisecond pulsar PSR J0218+4232, located at the eastern edge of the Peanut, at a distance of 3 kpc from the Earth and 0.9 kpc from the Galactic plane. Its location and bright gamma-ray emission above 25 TeV make it a natural laboratory for studying the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) in the transition region between the Galactic plane and halo. We interpret the observed emission as inverse-Compton scattering of CMB photons by electrons propagating along the large-scale GMF, accounting for turbulence through two models: Kolmogorov and Goldreich-Sridhar (GS). These models correspond to diffusive and ballistic particle propagation, respectively. While the GS case naturally provides conditions for one-sided gamma-ray emission, in the Kolmogorov case assumptions of one-sided particle injection and magnetic mirror at the source are necessary. We find that, in the Kolmogorov scenario, the Peanut's hotspots are likely associated with magnetic bottling, whereas in the GS scenario, they are related to magnetic field line geometry. Both models yield constraints on the GMF at the location of the Peanut.

papers.title: What You See Is (Not) What You Got: The Human Factor in PDF Signature Verification
papers.abstract: Signed PDF documents have legally binding value under frameworks such as the EU's eIDAS regulation. In this work, we present Genuine PDF Forgeries, a novel attack class that focuses on human factors in signature validation. Our attacks target the disconnect between cryptographically verifiable signer certificates and human-visible signature blocks embedded in documents. We analyze our attacks against 23 PDF viewers and validation tools across desktop platforms and the web. We find that nine of the 13 viewers that automatically report signature validity hide authenticated signer information behind additional user interaction. We then evaluate the attack in twin deception-based online studies with 584 EU-based participants. To further validate the impact, we perform a highly tailored real-world attack study with six trials within two privacy-sensitive organizations. Five of six organizational trials accepted requests authenticated using the forged visual identity. In the online studies (total n=584), the most effective attack variant deceives 71.9% of eligible participants on first impression, and 57.3% continue to be deceived even after we prompt for additional introspection. We derive viewer-side countermeasures and prototype a safeguard that overlays the untrusted signature block with signer information obtained from the validated certificate. Our results show that boolean validity indicators, not associated with the authenticated signer identity, are insufficient in practice.

papers.title: From $3\times2$pt to $4\times3$pt: calibrating galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments with galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra
papers.abstract: Combining galaxy clustering and weak gravitational lensing beyond two-point statistics offers a way to extract additional cosmological information while calibrating astrophysical nuisance parameters. We investigate this approach by combining 1-loop power spectra with tree-level bispectra, including all auto- and cross-bispectra of galaxy clustering and weak lensing, a combination that we refer to as $4\times3$pt by analogy with the well-known $3\times2$pt analysis. Modelling two- and three-point statistics consistently, with galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments described by the TATT model, we perform Fisher forecasts of dark energy constraints for a Euclid-like survey, with conservative scale cuts. When combined with CMB data, adding $4\times3$pt bispectra to the $3\times2$pt improves the dark energy figure of merit by about $30\%$, a gain that remains stable when using the three, four or five lowest redshift bins of our ten. To extend the analysis to ten tomographic bins, we compress the bispectra into skew-spectra, which improve the figure of merit by $20\%$ with the CMB and by $37\%$ without. We show that most of this improvement comes from the calibration of second-order galaxy bias parameters by three-point statistics, mainly by the galaxy-auto and the GGL bispectra. We also find that baryonic feedback is correlated with second-order intrinsic alignment parameters once the amplitude of the matter power spectrum is constrained by the CMB, and that bispectra reduce this correlation by calibrating intrinsic alignments, almost entirely through the GGL bispectra, a mechanism that could become more valuable with more flexible baryonic feedback models. These results demonstrate the potential of combined galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra to improve cosmological constraints from stage-IV galaxy surveys through the calibration of galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments.

papers.title: Numerical Thermodynamics of AdS Black Holes with Higher-Order Mass Corrections
papers.abstract: Inspired by noncommutative geometry and quintessence, we construct a new class of asymptotically anti-de Sitter black hole solutions characterized by a higher-order mass deformation term $\frac{aM^{n-1}}{r^n}$ involving two parameters, $a$ and $n$. Due to analytical difficulties, we approach the underlying thermodynamics through parallel programming simulations using CUDA codes. By considering models with $n=3$, $n=4$, and $n=5$, we numerically study certain thermodynamic properties, including the stability, the $P$-$v$ criticality, and the phase transitions.

papers.title: HARE: Fast Read Disturbance Threshold Profiling in Modern DRAM Chips via Reduced Timing Constraints
papers.abstract: Modern DRAM chips are vulnerable to read disturbance, which manifests as bitflips in a victim row physically near an aggressor row that is repeatedly activated. State-of-the-art mitigations rely on accurate and exhaustive profiling of the read disturbance threshold (RDT), i.e., the minimum number of aggressor row activations needed to induce the first bitflip. However, RDT changes significantly and unpredictably over time, motivating online profilers that dynamically adjust a mitigation's RDT configuration. RDT profiling is costly for online profilers (e.g., hundreds of seconds for a 16-bank DDR4 module) because 1) measuring a single DRAM row's RDT requires many activations and 2) each DRAM row can have a different RDT, requiring many rows to be profiled. We introduce HARE, an online RDT profiling technique that intentionally exacerbates read disturbance to quickly profile a DRAM module. HARE's key idea is to reduce the timing constraints between consecutive DRAM commands during profiling. Doing so significantly reduces profiling time by 1) directly reducing the execution time of the profiling command sequence and 2) exacerbating read disturbance such that the first bitflip occurs at a smaller activation count than with the conventional RowHammer sequence. From our characterization of 180 real DDR4 DRAM chips from four major DRAM manufacturers, we make three observations. First, HARE measures a DRAM row's RDT 31.2% faster than the RowHammer profiler and a DRAM module's minimum RDT with an average reduction of 21.7%. Second, HARE flips more than 95% of the cells that the RowHammer pattern flips. Third, HARE preserves the RDT ranking of rows well enough such that it can exhaustively reprofile a small set of rows to improve its minimum RDT estimation. Our end-to-end evaluations show that HARE enables significant system performance improvements and outperforms the RowHammer profiler.

papers.title: Radiation from scattering on multiple shockwaves
papers.abstract: It is well known that radiation produced by scattering an electron off multiple sources depends on the length of the mean free path between these scatterings. When this is sufficiently small, the spectrum is suppressed due to destructive interference, a famous result known as the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) effect. This is usually modelled approximately, with scattering centres treated linearly (e.g., as screened Coulomb potentials), high-energy probes and soft emitted photons. In this paper, we consider a scenario where multiple scatterings can be computed exactly: charged probe scattering on multiple null electromagnetic shockwaves. Here, the amplitudes for elastic scattering and single photon emission can be determined exactly, for arbitrary kinematics, in terms of the shock profiles in the transverse plane. We use these amplitudes to compute the radiation density (doubly-averaged over shock locations in the transverse plane and lightfront time) in the regimes of independent and interfering scatterings. For shock profiles which are radially symmetric in the transverse plane (including the ultraboosted Coulomb field), we recover the known LPM suppression, albeit with more general kinematics. In addition, our setup allows us to consider the source-free case of multiple scattering on impulsive/ultra-short plane waves, where we find much stronger suppression of the spectrum in the LPM regime.

papers.title: AutoOntic: Automatic Ontology Induction from Text for Knowledge Graph Construction
papers.abstract: Graph-based retrieval-augmented generation depends on the quality of the knowledge graph (KG) it retrieves over, yet schema-free LLM-based extraction pipelines typically produce flat graphs: deduplicated entities and relations with no type hierarchy and no domain/range constraints. We present AutoOntic, a pipeline that automatically constructs an ontology from text by canonicalizing open-vocabulary entity types and relations, inducing a hierarchy over the canonicalized types, and mining relation-level domain and range constraints. Its hierarchy induction procedure prioritizes types using corpus-derived relation-argument profiles and places them through local, LLM-adjudicated parent/child checks, allowing newly inserted types to trigger reassignment of existing parent-child links. The resulting hierarchy constrains entity deduplication and supports the induction of relation-level domain/range constraints. For intrinsic evaluation, we introduce a reference-based protocol that classifies induced ontology types as exact, broader, narrower, or unrelated to reference domain and range classes. On the Wikidata-TekGen and DBpedia-WebNLG subsets of Text2KGBench, over 90% of AutoOntic's induced endpoint types are semantically aligned with the reference classes across two LLM backbones: about half match exactly, while most remaining differences concern granularity. On MINE, knowledge graphs organized using an ontology built by AutoOntic achieve 88% retrieval accuracy. AutoOntic is available at https://github.com/screemix/AutoOntic.

papers.title: Quantitative Stability Region Estimation of Grid-Forming Inverters with Current Limiting via a State-Dependent Switched Energy Function
papers.abstract: With increasing renewable energy integration, grid-forming (GFM) inverters are becoming key components of future power systems. Compared with synchronous generators (SGs), GFM inverters have limited overcurrent capability and require current limiting. This can lead to switching between normal and current-limited operating modes under large disturbances, complicating synchronization dynamics and posing a longstanding challenge to existing transient-stability analysis methods. In this paper, a state-dependent switched (SdS) energy function theory is proposed for transient-stability analysis of GFM inverters with current limiting, whose dynamics can be abstracted as SdS nonlinear systems. Regional energy functions are constructed for individual operating modes and continuously matched at switching interfaces, yielding a continuous piecewise energy function. Hence, the derived conservative estimate of the stability region (region of attraction, ROA) spans different operating regions without prescribing subsequent current limiting activations and releases, a fundamental distinction from conventional methods using signal-mode energy functions. Techniques for incorporating damping energy are extended to the proposed framework to capture damping effects and further reduce the conservatism of the ROA estimates. The methodology applies to GFM inverters with different synchronization control loops and current-limiting strategies. Experiments on a physical GFM inverter under various grid contingencies validate the proposed quantitative transient stability assessment.

papers.title: On-Edge Acoustic Continual Anomaly Detection: A Cross-Platform Comparative Study
papers.abstract: Acoustic Anomaly Detection (AAD) serves as a non-contact approach for machine condition monitoring, yet much of the existing research is evaluated offline and rarely addresses embedded hardware constraints or microphone variations under operational drift. This paper presents a comparative evaluation of on-edge continual AAD across two embedded platforms the ESP32-S3 (with an external I2S digital microphone) and the Arduino Nicla Vision (with an onboard Pulse Density Modulation (PDM) microphone) using a shared detection model. The model utilizes a lightweight ShallowNet encoder and contrastive prototype learning to map spectrograms into a 32-dimensional embedding space. Both boards run an identical TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers (TFLM) encoder, performing on-device prototype learning updated via an exponential moving average. A cloud pipeline orchestrated through Firebase and MQTT enables remote data collection and retraining. Evaluated via a controlled speaker-replay protocol using standardized Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) Challenge Task 2 machine sounds, the ESP32-S3 achieved 82.35% to 95.00% accuracy across five machine types, while the Nicla Vision achieved 79.41% to 95.00%. The two platforms demonstrated comparable performance, confirming that the lightweight prototypical architecture transfers reliably across distinct hardware and sensor tiers.
